2611.05129.abstract: Web services provide walking directions for nearly every city, but following them reliably over long routes remains challenging for autonomous robots. Point-goal navigation policies rely heavily on accurate GNSS, while most vision-language navigation models struggle to execute even short instructions outdoors. We present WayTrace, a hierarchical system that connects web-map directions to robot motion through language. An off-the-shelf orchestrator vision-language model reads the turn-by-turn directions, a satellite map and recent camera images, and issues one atomic language command at a time, such as "cross the road to the left". An onboard trace predictor, trained on over one million automatically labelled samples from street-level images, draws the path for this command in the image, and a reinforcement learning policy tracks it. In long-range simulated missions, WayTrace remains robust to GNSS noise and rarely leaves crosswalks or sidewalks, while point-goal baselines degrade sharply with about ten times more violations. Deployed on a wheeled-legged robot, WayTrace completes real-world missions of up to 1.37 km at about 1.1 m/s through a busy city centre, rural trails and a university campus, handling crosswalks, staircases and construction sites. Project page: https://way-trace.github.io

llm.title_ja: WayTrace：具現化都市ナビゲーションのためのマップ・言語・トレース階層システム
llm.tldr_ja: ウェブマップの案内を言語を介してロボットの軌跡に変換する階層型システムにより、GNSSノイズに強く長距離の屋外都市ナビゲーションを実現する。
llm.problem: ポイントゴールナビゲーションは正確なGNSSに依存し、既存の多くの一言言語ナビゲーションモデルは屋外での短い指示の実行にも苦戦している。
llm.method: VLMオーケストレータが地図や画像からアトミックな言語命令を発行し、車載トレース予測器が画像上にパスを描画、強化学習方策がそれを追従する階層システムを構築する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機の車輪・脚ロボットによる1.37kmに及ぶ都市中心部でのミッションにおいて、交差点や階段などを頑健にナビゲートした。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語ナビゲーション

2611.05129.tldr_en: WayTrace is a hierarchical system that connects web-map directions to robot motion through language, and remains robust to GNSS noise and rarely leaves crosswalks or sidewalks, while point-goal baselines degrade sharply with about ten times more violations.

2611.05119.title: DexHOT: Learning Hand-Object Configuration Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
2611.05119.abstract: Dexterous manipulation involves not only moving objects, but also arranging the hand around them to maintain useful contacts and enable subsequent actions. Yet many learning-based systems specify goals primarily through object poses or trajectories, leaving hand-object configurations to emerge implicitly. We introduce DexHOT, which formulates dexterous manipulation as hand-object configuration transfer: moving between feasible configurations that jointly specify hand articulation and object pose relative to the wrist. DexHOT learns a reusable relation-conditioned transfer primitive from synthetic feasible configuration pairs, without human reference motions, and composes long-horizon behaviors through closed-loop tracking of configuration subgoals. On DexHOTBench with 120 objects, a single policy achieves 80.5% transfer success on seen objects and 69.4% on unseen objects; on a real dexterous hand, it achieves 61.5% success over 200 real-robot transfers and 90% task success across six demonstration-guided tasks. These results show that explicit hand-object goals provide an expressive and composable interface for dexterous manipulation. More details and videos are available at https://dex-hot.github.io/.

llm.title_ja: DexHOT：器用な操作のためのハンド・オブジェクト構成転移の学習
llm.tldr_ja: ハンド関節と手首に対するオブジェクト姿勢を共同で指定する構成転移として器用な操作を定式化し、多様なオブジェクトに対して高い転移成功率を実現する。
llm.problem: 多くの学習ベースシステムはオブジェクトのポーズや軌跡のみを指定し、ハンドとオブジェクトの構成を暗黙的に任せているため器用な把持が難しい。
llm.method: 人間参照モーションなしで合成された実行可能な構成ペアから、再利用可能な関係条件付き転移プリミティブを学習し、閉ループトラッキングで構成サブゴールを構成する。
llm.result: 120のオブジェクトを使ったDexHOTBenchおよび実機の器用なハンドによる実験において、高い転移成功率とタスク成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ハンドオブジェクト構成

2611.05119.tldr_en: DexHOT is introduced, which formulates dexterous manipulation as hand-object configuration transfer: moving between feasible configurations that jointly specify hand articulation and object pose relative to the wrist.

2611.05113.title: HLO-AMP: Hierarchical Loco-Manipulation from Object-Aware Motion Priors
2611.05113.abstract: Hierarchical pipelines for humanoid loco-manipulation typically pair a task-agnostic whole-body controller (WBC) with a downstream task policy. Such WBCs are often trained through manual reward shaping, which yields visibly machine-like motions; more consequentially, they are trained without the manipulated object in the scene. Object dynamics are instead approximated through randomized end-effector force disturbances, a proxy that fails to reproduce the distributed multi-contact wrench a real payload applies across the arms and torso, with the gap becoming critical near the platform's payload limit. In this work, we train the low-level (LL) controller itself as an object-aware motion prior: a single policy trained via motion imitation on retargeted motion-capture (MoCap) references that span the core motion primitives of the downstream task, with the manipulated object physically present in the scene. This single stage inherits natural human-like coordination from the references and absorbs the realistic contact wrench at its source, while exposing the same compact task-space command interface used by command-tracking WBCs. A reference-free high-level (HL) policy is then trained on top, with its action channel anchored to the empirical envelope of the low-level training data so that it generalizes the priors to a long-horizon multi-stage task while structurally preventing queries that would push the low level off-distribution. We instantiate the framework on a Unitree G1 for bimanual box pick-and-place: the same deployed policy generalizes across object masses and dimensions, initial and goal poses, and reactively recovers from intentional drops mid-carry. Video: https://youtu.be/viR_ULnRDQQ.
2611.05113.comment: Accepted at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026). Video: https://youtu.be/viR_ULnRDQQ

llm.title_ja: HLO-AMP：オブジェクト認識型モーション事前学習に基づく階層型ロコ・マニュピレーション
llm.tldr_ja: オブジェクトをシーンに配置した状態で低レベルコントローラをモーション事前学習させ、その上にリファレンスフリーの高レベル方策を構築することで、ヒューマノイドの器用な箱の運搬や動的なリカバリを実現する。
llm.problem: 従来のヒューマノイドの階層型ロコ・マニュピレーションは、オブジェクトを考慮しないタスク非依存の全身コントローラに依存しており、実際の把持力やペイロードの限界に対応できない。
llm.method: 操作対象オブジェクトをシーンに含めた状態で、モーションキャプチャの参照を用いて低レベルコントローラをオブジェクト認識型モーション事前学習として訓練する。
llm.result: Unitree G1を用いた二足歩行箱のピック＆プレース実験において、オブジェクトの質量や寸法の変化への汎化や、意図的な落下からの復帰を実現した。
keywords_ja: ロコ・マニュピレーション

2611.05113.tldr_en: This work trains the low-level (LL) controller itself as an object-aware motion prior, a single policy trained via motion imitation on retargeted motion-capture (MoCap) references that span the core motion primitives of the downstream task, with the manipulated object physically present in the scene.

2611.05093.title: LoopQ: Fair, Closed-Loop Evaluation of Quantized Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.05093.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) for vision-language-action (VLA) models promises smaller and faster VLA deployments. However, when analyzing existing VLA quantization works, we realised that it is hard to reason about the performance of the suggested quantization method compared to existing, similar, or in many cases, simpler PTQ methods. We present LoopQ, a closed-loop benchmark that compares multiple quantization policies on the same checkpoint, layers and engine, varying only the method and the kernels. We evaluate RTN, AWQ, GPTQ, ActQuant and QuantVLA on four VLAs with more than 180,000 episodes of LIBERO and LIBERO-plus, compare against QVLA's reported results on the same layers, and benchmark whether the four public VLA-quantization releases can be reproduced. We benchmark the methods on an NVIDIA H100, an L4, and a Jetson AGX Thor. Our results show that while quantization reliably saves memory, 2-3x for real low-bit models, VLA-specific PTQ methods underperform compared to simpler generic baselines. At 4 bits, RTN, AWQ and GPTQ match or exceed ActQuant and QuantVLA, plain RTN matches the calibrated methods, and plain AWQ matches the success QVLA reports for itself. Standard LIBERO hides the losses that do exist: configurations with no significant LIBERO loss lose 1.5-4.3 points under paired LIBERO-plus perturbations. Speed is a weaker story. At batch 1 on the H100, no quantized pi0.5 or OpenVLA-OFT configuration is faster than its 16-bit model (1.06-1.58x slower on library kernels); only the L4 with int8 kernels gains (4-14%), the Thor is slower on every 4-bit configuration, and the engine alone changes latency by 2.1x. Profiling explains why: pi0.5's quantized backbone is compute-bound, while its memory-bound action expert, 63% of GPU time and 13% of the parameters, stays in 16 bits.

llm.title_ja: LoopQ：量子化されたビジョン・言語・アクションモデルの公平な閉ループ評価
llm.tldr_ja: 同一のチェックポイントやエンジンを用いて複数の量子化ポリシーを公平に比較する閉ループベンチマーク「LoopQ」を提案し、汎用的な単純ベースラインがVLA特化手法と同等以上の性能を持つことを明らかにする。
llm.problem: VLAモデルのポストトレーニング量子化（PTQ）手法において、提案された手法の性能を既存の単純な手法と比較して評価することが困難である。
llm.method: 同一条件でRTN、AWQ、GPTQ、ActQuant、QuantVLAなどの複数の量子化手法をLIBERO等のタスクで評価する閉ループベンチマーク「LoopQ」を構築する。
llm.result: 4ビット量子化において、単純なRTNやAWQがキャリブレーション手法やVLA特化手法と同等以上の性能を達成する一方、速度面ではモデルのボトルネックにより必ずしも高速化しないことを示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2611.05093.tldr_en: LoopQ, a closed-loop benchmark that compares multiple quantization policies on the same checkpoint, layers and engine, varying only the method and the kernels, shows that while quantization reliably saves memory, 2-3x for real low-bit models, VLA-specific PTQ methods underperform compared to simpler generic baselines.

2611.05084.title: Sparse Anchors for Visual Multi-Session Registration in Changing Environments
2611.05084.abstract: Repeated robotic monitoring requires localization across visits to the same environment, even if the environment changes. Such changes can substantially reduce persistent visual content, and repetitive structures can lead to incorrect cross-session correspondences. In this paper, we address visual multi-session registration of a new data recording (the query session) to a previously reconstructed reference map. Under substantial visual and structural changes, cross-session localization may be possible only for parts of the trajectory. In our approach, we therefore rely on a sparse set of reliable absolute pose constraints and combine them with within-session relative-pose information to register the complete trajectory to the reference map. We first estimate absolute alignment hypotheses through visual place recognition, local feature matching, and geometric verification. We then use sequence consensus to reject hypotheses that are inconsistent with a common query-to-reference alignment and retain the remaining poses as absolute anchors. These anchors are refined through featuremetric alignment against a Gaussian feature field and combined with within-session relative-pose constraints in a robust pose-graph optimization. We evaluate our approach on 15 cross-session experiments from the challenging HILTI26 construction-site dataset, covering substantial scene changes and difficult-to-match environments. Our method achieves 94.4% recall within 1m and 100.0% within 5m, outperforming independent image localization, which peaks at 65.3% and 70.7%, respectively, as well as direct registration of independently reconstructed Structure-from-Motion geometry. Our results show that sparse, reliable absolute anchors can provide accurate and complete trajectory registration even when reliable cross-session correspondences are available only for part of the query session.

llm.title_ja: 変化する環境におけるビジュアルマルチセッション登録のためのスパースアンカー
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的プレース認識とシーケンスコンセンサスから得られるスパースな絶対ポーズ制約と相対ポーズを頑健なポーズグラフ最適化で結合し、激しい環境変化の中でも正確な軌跡登録を実現する。
llm.problem: 繰り返しロボット監視を行う際、環境の変化や繰り返し構造によって視覚的内容が減少し、クロスセッションでの正しい対応付けが困難になる。
llm.method: ビジュアルプレース認識等から絶対アライメント仮説を推定し、シーケンスコンセンサスによってスパースな絶対アンカーを抽出・精製してポーズグラフ最適化に組み込む。
llm.result: HILTI26建設現場データセットの15のクロスセッション実験において、1m以内94.4%のリコールを達成し、従来の手法を大きく上回った。
keywords_ja: マルチセッション登録
ビジュアルプレース認識

2611.05084.tldr_en: This paper addresses visual multi-session registration of a new data recording to a previously reconstructed reference map and shows that sparse, reliable absolute anchors can provide accurate and complete trajectory registration even when reliable cross-session correspondences are available only for part of the query session.

2611.05080.title: CRONOS: Benchmarking Non-Episodic Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation
2611.05080.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is promising for adapting robot policies to unstructured real-world environments. However, standard RL pipelines rely on episodic training with frequent scene resets, which is impractical for real-world deployment due to the need for substantial human intervention. While prior work has studied non-episodic RL in relatively small policies trained from scratch, its behavior when fine-tuning modern large-scale pre-trained vision-language-action (VLA) models remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce CRONOS, a simulation benchmark for RL fine-tuning of VLAs under non-episodic scene resets. CRONOS leverages high-fidelity physics simulators and adopts shared-scene multi-task settings. Using CRONOS, we show that naively fine-tuning pre-trained policies fails in non-episodic settings due to shifts in object configurations and end-effector poses; however, these challenges can be mitigated through targeted reset allocation and by addressing biases in pre-trained models. Moreover, we find that non-episodic training enhances long-horizon manipulation and improves generalization to previously unseen object configurations and task sequences. Project page: https://embodiedai-ntu.github.io/cronos/

llm.title_ja: CRONOS: ロボットマニピュレーションのための非エピソード型強化学習ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 非エピソード型シーンリセットの下でのVLAモデルのRLファインチューニング用に、高忠実度シミュレータと共有シーンマルチタスク設定を活用するシミュレーションベンチマークCRONOSを提案する。
llm.problem: 標準的な強化学習は頻繁なシーンリセットを伴うエピソード型訓練に依存しており、実世界への展開において実用的ではない。
llm.method: 高忠実度シミュレータと共有シーンマルチタスク設定を活用するシミュレーションベンチマークCRONOSを構築した。
llm.result: ナイーブなファインチューニングは失敗するが、対象を絞ったリセット割り当てや事前学習済みモデルのバイアス対処により改善可能であり、長期的マニピュレーションが向上することを示した。
keywords_ja: ファインチューニング
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.05080.tldr_en: It is shown that naively fine-tuning pre-trained policies fails in non-episodic settings due to shifts in object configurations and end-effector poses; however, these challenges can be mitigated through targeted reset allocation and by addressing biases in pre-trained models.

2611.05074.title: Nested Field-of-View Barriers for Teleoperated Multi-Robot Relay Chains
2611.05074.abstract: Teleoperation of mobile robots in communication-denied environments requires maintaining a communication link while allowing the operator to maneuver freely. We propose a shared-autonomy framework in which a teleoperated leader is followed by a chain of autonomous robots that relays a line of sight to a fixed base station, a geometric proxy for the link. Connectivity is enforced geometrically through visibility-based Control Barrier Functions (CBFs), with each agent computing its control input locally through a quadratic program. A strict visibility constraint guarantees connectivity, but a follower with no independent motion objective remains stationary, stalling the leader at the boundary of the safe set. Relaxing it preserves mobility at the cost of the guarantee. Our framework resolves this conflict through nested hard-soft visibility constraints: a full field-of-view (FoV) constraint enforced strictly to guarantee connectivity and a contracted FoV constraint imposed on each follower as a relaxed behavioral objective that drives it inward before the connectivity boundary is reached. We prove feasibility of the local quadratic programs and forward invariance of the connected, collision-free set under the resulting distributed controller. The contraction parameter shapes follower behavior without affecting the guarantee, which follows from the strict constraint alone. The framework is evaluated in confined and cluttered environments on two simulated systems: a kinematic integrator and software-in-the-loop Crazyflie quadrotors. Compared with a baseline tuned to reach the goal in comparable time, the framework keeps the links far closer to the connected set and moves the followers less.
2611.05074.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Submitted to the American Control Conference (ACC)

llm.title_ja: 遠隔操作されるマルチロボットリレーチェーンのためのネスト型視野バリア
llm.tldr_ja: 遠隔操作されるリーダーに追従して視線を中継するマルチロボットシステムにおいて、接続性と機動性のトレードオフをネスト型ハード・ソフト視野制約により解決する共有自律フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 通信が制限された環境での移動ロボットの遠隔操作では、オペレータの自由な操縦を許可しつつ通信リンクを維持することが求められる。
llm.method: 視界ベースの制御バリア関数（CBF）を用いたネスト型ハード・ソフト可視性制約を導入し、分散型コントローラを構築した。
llm.result: 局所的QPの実行可能性と結合・無衝突集合の不変性を証明し、シミュレーションによりリンク維持と移動性能の向上を確認した。

2611.05074.tldr_en: A shared-autonomy framework in which a teleoperated leader is followed by a chain of autonomous robots that relays a line of sight to a fixed base station, a geometric proxy for the link.

2611.05072.title: Trajectory Evaluation via Rollout-Free World Model for End-to-end Autonomous Driving
2611.05072.abstract: Although existing candidate trajectory evaluators have substantially improved end-to-end planning accuracy, their underlying mechanism remains suboptimal. Model-based evaluators typically make scoring future-aware by explicitly predicting candidate-conditioned future states over the planning horizon, which we term rollout. However, rollout incurs high inference cost and accumulates prediction errors. We argue that planning does not require reconstructing a full future scene for each candidate, but only future-relevant information for reliable comparison. We therefore propose RFWorld, a Rollout-Free World model for end-to-end trajectory evaluation. RFWorld constructs a shared scene memory and shapes it into a future-readable representation via lightweight training-time temporal readout with semantic supervision, keeping training overhead low. At inference time, candidate trajectories directly query the shared memory via sparse spatial readout for scoring, reducing computation by roughly the planning horizon times the number of candidate trajectories, while avoiding recursive rollout errors. Experiments on NAVSIM and Bench2Drive show that RFWorld learns a more planning-aligned world representation and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

llm.title_ja: ロールアウトフリーな世界モデルを用いたエンドツーエンド自動運転のための軌道評価
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の状態を明示的に予測する従来のロールアウトの代わりに、共有シーンメモリから直接情報を取得することで計算コストと誤差の蓄積を削減するロールアウトフリー世界モデルRFWorldを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のモデルベース評価器は将来の状態を明示的に予測するロールアウトを行うため、高い推論コストと予測誤差の蓄積を伴う。
llm.method: 軽量な時間的リードアウトで共有シーンメモリを構築し、候補軌道がスパースな空間リードアウトでクエリを行うRFWorldを提案する。
llm.result: NAVSIMとBench2Driveにおいて、計算量を大幅に削減しつつ、より計画に整合した世界表現と最先端の性能を達成した。

2611.05072.tldr_en: This work proposes RFWorld, a Rollout-Free World model for end-to-end trajectory evaluation, which constructs a shared scene memory and shapes it into a future-readable representation via lightweight training-time temporal readout with semantic supervision, keeping training overhead low.

2611.05062.title: FloMo: 3D Scene Flow as a World Action Model Intermediate for Learning from Human Video
2611.05062.abstract: Pretrained video generation models distill internet-scale motion priors into robot policies, but full video is a redundant signal for action prediction. We argue that dense 3D motion is the medium through which video pretraining best transfers to robot actions, and that predicting motion rather than video affords better sample-efficiency for action prediction. FloMo is a 5B video-generation model fine-tuned to predict 3D scene-flow and action tokens. Rendering scene flow as RGB and encoding it into the same latent space as video enables a pretrained video generation backbone to efficiently adapt to predict 3D scene flow. Co-trained on action-free human video and action-labeled robot teleoperation data, our model benefits from human-video pretraining and generalizes to unseen objects, motion primitives, and tasks. Replacing motion prediction with a video prediction objective degrades out-of-distribution generalization, while adding a video prediction target alongside motion lowers policy success rather than improving it. When motion, video, and action are predicted jointly, action tokens attend far more to motion than to video, suggesting that predicting video wastes model capacity. Together, these results indicate that motion effectively mediates the transfer from video pretraining to action. More information can be found at flomo-wam.github.io.

llm.title_ja: FloMo: 人間映像からの学習における世界行動モデル中間表現としての3Dシーンフロー
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みビデオ生成モデルを3Dシーンフローと行動トークンの予測に適応させ、人間の映像から効率的にロボットの行動学習へ転移させるFloMoを提案する。
llm.problem: フルビデオは行動予測にとって冗長な信号であり、ビデオ事前学習をロボット行動に効率よく転移させる必要がある。
llm.method: 5Bのビデオ生成モデルをファインチューニングし、3Dシーンフローと行動トークンを共同で予測するFloMoを開発した。
llm.result: 人間の映像事前学習の恩恵を受け、未知のオブジェクトやタスクに対して優れた汎化性能を発揮することを示した。

2611.05058.title: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action
2611.05058.abstract: Recent multimodal language models can reason directly about robot scenes, but it is unclear whether they need to repeatedly reinterpret raw visual observations at every step of an interaction. We propose shifting routine spatial reasoning from images to text and symbols through a 3D geometric abstraction that is refreshed locally from observations and read directly by the language models. Specifically, our interface represents scene geometry via typed, evidence-aware symbolic references to object parts, grounds them from calibrated RGB-D, and returns compact textual checkpoints with metric residuals after each action. Symbolic task structure can thus be reused across decisions while metric values are rebound to the current scene, with direct visual reasoning invoked only on demand. Across offline policy synthesis and continuous online execution, reasoning over grounded text and symbols improves multi-step manipulation completion while substantially reducing repeated multimodal queries, positioning explicit geometric state as an effective substrate for agentic robot policies.
2611.05058.comment: Accepted to the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Agentic Robotics. 13 pages, 8 figures. Project page: https://geometric-abstraction.github.io

llm.title_ja: エージェントポリシーは毎ステップ画像を見る必要があるか？推論と行動のための幾何学的抽象化
llm.tldr_ja: 毎ステップの生画像の解釈の代わりに、3D幾何学的抽象化に基づく型付きシンボル表現を用いてテキストとシンボルによる空間推論を行い、マルチステップマニピュレーションを改善する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル言語モデルがロボットシーンを直接推論できる一方で、インタラクションの毎ステップで視覚観測を繰り返し再解釈する必要性については不明確である。
llm.method: オブジェクトパーツへのシンボル参照を通じてシーン幾何学を表現し、較正されたRGB-Dからグラウンドしてテキストのチェックポイントを返すインターフェースを提案する。
llm.result: グラウンドされたテキストとシンボルに基づいて推論を行うことで、マルチステップマニピュレーションの完了率が向上し、重複するマルチモーダルクエリが大幅に削減された。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル言語モデル

2611.05058.tldr_en: This work proposes shifting routine spatial reasoning from images to text and symbols through a 3D geometric abstraction that is refreshed locally from observations and read directly by the language models, positioning explicit geometric state as an effective substrate for agentic robot policies.

2611.05029.title: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI
2611.05029.abstract: Continual learning in physical AI differs from conventional continual learning because small per-step policy errors can accumulate over a trajectory. Each deviation may move the agent outside the training distribution, increase subsequent prediction errors, and ultimately cause closed-loop task failure. This work introduces Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity (DRAP), a replay-free method that estimates the historical importance of adaptable model tensors from sample-level action gradients weighted by local trajectory-amplification risk. A ridge-regularized local linear model is fitted to expert state-action transitions, and the largest singular value of its state-transition matrix provides a policy-independent, Lyapunov-inspired estimate of one-step perturbation amplification. After each task, risk-weighted squared gradients are accumulated in a tensor-level importance memory. During subsequent tasks, DRAP uses normalized cumulative importance to scale the effective AdamW learning rate of each tensor, immediately reducing the plasticity of components that supported previous behavior at dynamically sensitive trajectory points. We instantiate DRAP on a fixed KappaTune-selected subnetwork of OpenVLA and evaluate replay-free sequential adaptation across the LIBERO Spatial, Object, and Goal suites. Compared with standard AdamW fine-tuning and EWC, the results show substantially improved retention of previously learned behaviors while preserving strong new-suite acquisition.

llm.title_ja: DRAP: 物理AIにおける継続学習のための動的リスク適応型可塑性
llm.tldr_ja: 軌道増幅リスクによって重み付けされた行動勾配からモデルの履歴的重要性を推定し、リプレイなしで継続的な適応を行う手法DRAPを提案する。
llm.problem: 物理AIの継続学習では、小さなポリシー誤差が軌道に沿って蓄積され、閉ループでのタスク失敗を引き起こす。
llm.method: 局所的な軌道増幅リスクで重み付けされた行動勾配を用いてモデルテンソルの履歴的重要性を推定し、AdamWの学習率をスケーリングするリプレイフリーな手法DRAPを導入した。
llm.result: LIBEROスイートを用いた評価において、従来手法と比較して新しいスイートの獲得を維持しながら、過去に学習した行動の保持能力が大幅に向上した。

2611.05029.tldr_en: DRAP is introduced, a replay-free method that estimates the historical importance of adaptable model tensors from sample-level action gradients weighted by local trajectory-amplification risk, and shows substantially improved retention of previously learned behaviors while preserving strong new-suite acquisition.

2611.05027.title: Haptic Shared Control for Multi-Robot Systems
2611.05027.abstract: Multi-agent systems offer significant advantages in terms of flexibility and redundancy, enabling the efficient distribution of complex tasks among multiple robots. However, their deployment requires advanced control strategies to ensure optimal cooperation between autonomous agents and human operators. We propose a modification of the global connectivity maintenance algorithm to incorporate measurements taken in agent's local frame, using sensors with limited fields of view. This algorithm, responsible for the autonomous behavior of the multi-robot system, is combined with different adaptive supervision strategies, allowing the user to exert control at varying scales over the entire group. (i) Single Agent Control (S): The operator directly controls a single robot, (ii) Pinning Control (P): The operator imposes constraints on multiple robots to influence the group, (iii) Centroid Control (C): The operator acts on the system's center of mass to steer the entire fleet. In conjunction with the connectivity maintenance algorithm, these methods ensure compliance with inter-agent constraints while providing haptic feedback to the user regarding the system's connectivity state. The effectiveness of these approaches was evaluated through a user study, comparing performance with and without haptic feedback across multiple scenarios tailored to the different control modes.
2611.05027.comment: PhD thesis, Université de Rennes (IRISA UMR 6074 / Inria Rennes), defended 30 April 2025. 134 pages, 38 figures

llm.title_ja: マルチロボットシステムのためのハプティック共有制御
llm.tldr_ja: 視野が制限されたセンサーを持つ自律エージェントの局所的測定を取り入れたグローバル接続維持アルゴリズムと、多様な適応的監督戦略を組み合わせたハプティック共有制御手法を提案する。
llm.problem: マルチエージェントシステムの展開には、自律エージェントと人間のオペレータ間の最適な協調を確保する高度な制御戦略が必要である。
llm.method: 局所フレームでの測定を組み込んだ接続維持アルゴリズムを、単一エージェント制御、ピニング制御、重心制御などの適応的監督戦略と統合した。
llm.result: ハプティックフィードバックの有無による性能を比較するユーザースタディを実施し、提案アプローチの有効性を評価した。
keywords_ja: ハプティック共有制御
ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.05023.title: HiLo-WAM: Decoupling Long-Horizon Task Evolution and Local Dynamics in World Action Models
2611.05023.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) improve robotic manipulation by jointly modeling visual dynamics and robot actions. However, most existing WAMs model dense short-horizon visual dynamics, capturing local interactions but providing limited long-range task context. Extending prediction horizons increases uncertainty and computation while entangling task-level evolution with fine-grained local dynamics, obscuring their dependencies and distinct roles in action generation. We propose HiLo-WAM, which decouples long-horizon task evolution from local visual dynamics while jointly modeling their interaction with robot actions. A sparse long-horizon visual stream captures historical task context and future evolution, while a dense local dynamics visual stream models short-horizon robot-object interactions. The two streams operate at different temporal scales within a unified dual-DiT architecture and guide actions through structured cross-stream attention. Progressive inference further reduces unnecessary computation through stream-wise partial denoising, joint denoising, and dynamic skipping. Experiments demonstrate strong long-horizon manipulation performance: HiLo-WAM achieves a 93.70% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 and a 17.43 progress score on RoboDojo long-horizon tasks, with robust in-domain and OOD performance on the Fourier GR-3 robot. Ablations confirm the complementary contributions of long-horizon task evolution and local interaction dynamics, while temporal-scale analyses highlight the importance of balancing temporal coverage and resolution. Progressive inference further achieves a 2.93x speedup while improving performance.

llm.title_ja: HiLo-WAM: 世界行動モデルにおける長期タスク発展と局所ダイナミクスの分離
llm.tldr_ja: 長期的なタスクのコンテキストと短期間の局所的相互作用を異なる時間スケールで分離してモデル化し、構造化されたクロスストリームアテンションで行動を導くHiLo-WAMを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のワールドアクションモデル（WAM）は短期間の視覚ダイナミクスをモデル化するため局所的な相互作用は捉えられるが、長期的なタスクコンテキストが制限され、計算量が増大する。
llm.method: 履歴と将来の進化を捉えるスパースな長期視覚ストリームと、ロボットとオブジェクトの相互作用をモデル化する密集した局所視覚ストリームを統合したデュアルDiTアーキテクチャを提案する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0やRoboDojoなどの長期タスクにおいて優れた成功率を達成し、プログレッシブ推論により高速化と性能向上を両立させた。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.05023.tldr_en: HiLo-WAM is proposed, which decouples long-horizon task evolution from local visual dynamics while jointly modeling their interaction with robot actions, and achieves a 2.93x speedup while improving performance.

2611.05003.title: Unifying and Beyond the Theory of Pervasive Capability Degradation in LLM Post-training SFT from Feature Interference
2611.05003.abstract: Pervasive Capability Degradation (PCD) refers to the phenomenon in which supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while adapting a large language model (LLM) to a target task, often erodes the general capabilities acquired during pre-training. Prevailing explanations attribute PCD to macroscopic distribution shift and therefore lack microscopic manipulability, leaving existing mitigation methods without a complete theoretical foundation. In this paper, we first develop a bottom-up geometric theory of PCD grounded in feature interference under superposition: narrow-domain SFT data disrupt the almost-orthogonal feature structure formed during pre-training, and the resulting interference drives activations across decision hyperplanes in the output Laguerre-Voronoi geometry, flipping predictions on general tasks. This theory unifies existing methods into six paradigms and reveals both the source of their efficacy and their theoretical limits. We then prove that cross-entropy under one-hot supervision cannot resolve PCD on its own, and accordingly propose the AEGIS loss, which directly constrains the drift of activation margins along all competing token directions, thereby decoupling interference suppression from task adaptation. Across 3 model families and 14 SFT tasks, AEGIS outperforms representative methods of every paradigm on target tasks and pervasive capabilities simultaneously, at only about 1.3 times the computational cost of standard SFT. Its generality, scalability, and mechanistic interpretability offer a new perspective on fully resolving PCD.

llm.title_ja: 特徴干渉によるLLM事後訓練SFTの普遍的能力劣化の理論の統合と拡張
llm.tldr_ja: スーパーポジション下での特徴干渉に基づいた普遍的能力劣化（PCD）の幾何学的理論を開発し、競合するトークン方向沿いの活性化マージンのドリフトを直接制約するAEGIS損失を提案する。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の教師ありファインチューニング（SFT）はターゲットタスクに適応する一方で、事前学習で獲得した一般的能力を損なう現象（PCD）を引き起こす。
llm.method: 干渉抑制とタスク適応を分離するため、すべての競合トークン方向に対する活性化マージンのドリフトを直接制約するAEGIS損失を提案した。
llm.result: 3つのモデルファミリーと14のSFTタスクにおいて、計算コストを抑えつつ、ターゲットタスクと普遍的能力の両方で従来手法を上回る性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: 教師ありファインチューニング

2611.05003.tldr_en: It is proved that cross-entropy under one-hot supervision cannot resolve PCD on its own, and accordingly the AEGIS loss is proposed, which directly constrains the drift of activation margins along all competing token directions, thereby decoupling interference suppression from task adaptation.

2611.05001.title: For You, Not for Everyone: Bystander-Aware Delivery of Critical Feedback in Robot Tutoring
2611.05001.abstract: Robots in shared settings may expose information intended for an individual user to nearby bystanders. Robot tutoring makes this concern particularly salient: critical feedback is directed at an individual learner, yet bystanders may overhear or see it. To address this, we compared context-invariant and context-adaptive robot behaviors in a between-subjects study with 40 participants. Following an initial phase without a bystander, a bystander entered the setting. Participants then received two scripted critical feedback messages concerning their pronunciation and handwriting, independent of their actual performance. With the context-invariant behavior, the robot tutor delivered both messages aloud. With the context-adaptive behavior, the robot tutor scanned for the bystander, turned its body and display away after detecting them, gave a spoken attention cue, and presented the same feedback messages silently on its display. Participants rated the robot tutor higher in perceived privacy awareness and perceived social competence in the context-adaptive condition than in the context-invariant condition, while evidence for reduced experienced embarrassment was inconclusive. These findings inform the design and evaluation of robots that respond to bystander presence by adapting how they communicate potentially sensitive information.

llm.title_ja: あなたのために、皆のために非ず：ロボット家庭教師における傍観者を意識した批判的フィードバックの提供
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット家庭教師が周囲の傍観者の存在を検知した際に、身体とディスプレイを背け、視覚的注意の手がかりを与えた上で、批判的フィードバックを静かに提示する文脈適応型行動の評価を行った。
llm.problem: 共有環境におけるロボットは個人向けの情報を近くにいる傍観者に漏洩する懸念があり、特にロボット家庭教師の批判的フィードバックにおいて問題となる。
llm.method: 文脈不変型と文脈適応型のロボット行動を比較する40名の参加者による被験者間実験を実施した。
llm.result: 文脈適応型条件のほうが、プライバシー意識と社会的コンピテンシーの知覚においてロボットがより高く評価されることが示された。
llm.limitation: 恥ずかしさの軽減に関する証拠は決定的ではなかった。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.05001.tldr_en: Compared context-invariant and context-adaptive robot behaviors in a between-subjects study, which inform the design and evaluation of robots that respond to bystander presence by adapting how they communicate potentially sensitive information.

2611.04974.title: LLMs as MDP Designers: A Dependency-Aware Agentic Framework for Automated Robot Policy Generation
2611.04974.abstract: We investigate the automated generation of executable robot reinforcement learning (RL) policies from natural-language task descriptions. Rather than using large language models (LLMs) as execution-time decision makers, we use them as designers that construct RL pipelines before deployment, including Markov decision process (MDP) formulation and simulator implementation. We identify a phase-wise structure in this problem: MDP formulation is dependency-structured and sequential, whereas simulator implementation becomes modular once the formulation is fixed. Based on this structure, we propose ARPG, a dependency-aware agentic framework that performs sequential MDP modeling, localized verification and correction, and simulator-structured implementation while externalizing intermediate artifacts. ARPG targets a key failure mode of automated policy generation: executable code may still yield non-learnable policies when state, action, reward, and termination artifacts are not semantically aligned. Experiments in Isaac Sim show that ARPG improves modeling correctness, environment executability, and policy-generation success compared with monolithic LLM baselines and off-the-shelf agentic systems. Additional demonstrations on custom robotics, standard RL, and engineering-domain MDPs further suggest that the same modeling pipeline can be reused beyond the main benchmark suite.
2611.04974.comment: Accepted to the 40th Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
2611.04974.tldr_en: ARPG is proposed, a dependency-aware agentic framework that performs sequential MDP modeling, localized verification and correction, and simulator-structured implementation while externalizing intermediate artifacts and improves modeling correctness, environment executability, and policy-generation success compared with monolithic LLM baselines and off-the-shelf agentic systems.

2611.04972.title: Caging Vision-Language Navigation for Legged Robots via Barrier-Certified Safety Architecture
2611.04972.abstract: By harnessing the inherent commonsense capabilities of pretrained Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs), current Vision-Language Action(VLA) models for legged robots excel at interpreting language-based navigation commands but lack the physical grounding and explicit safety assurance required for real-world operation. Therefore, this paper aims to cage Legged-Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) through a safety architecture that provides physical grounding and ensures navigation safety. The key idea is not to abandon the powerful capabilities of end-to-end VLA planning, but rather to augment and cage them. In particular, we integrate a high-level VLA planner with a low-level physical-grounding layer that leverages efficient state estimation, in-situ 3D spatial perception, and an Signed Distance Field (SDF) representation to generate executable trajectories. We provide a navigation planner with provable collision-avoidance guarantees under the stated assumptions by combining a low-dimensional Bezier-parameterized MPPI planner with Discrete Exponential Barrier Function (dEBF) constraints. The proposed Legged-VLN system is modular, making it compatible with various VLM/VLA models and agnostic to the robot platform. The proposed system is validated with extensive real-world experiments on humanoid and quadrupedal robots, demonstrating versatile, efficient, and safe vision-language driven navigation capabilities.

llm.title_ja: バリア認証型安全アーキテクチャによる脚式ロボットのための視覚言語ナビゲーションの囲い込み
llm.tldr_ja: VLAモデルの強力なエンドツーエンド計画能力を維持しつつ、物理的接地と証明可能な衝突回避保証を与える低レベルの安全レイヤーを統合したLegged-VLNシステムを提案する。
llm.problem: 脚式ロボット向けの既存の視覚言語行動（VLA）モデルは言語コマンドの解釈に優れるが、実世界運用に必要な物理的接地と明示的な安全性が欠けている。
llm.method: 高レベルVLAプランナーと、効率的な状態推定、3D空間知覚、符号付き距離場（SDF）表現、および離散指数バリア関数（dEBF）制約を組み合わせた低レベル物理接地レイヤーを統合した。
llm.result: 人型および四足歩行ロボットを用いた広範な実世界実験により、多用途かつ効率的で安全な視覚言語駆動ナビゲーション実証された。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション

2611.04972.tldr_en: This paper integrates a high-level VLA planner with a low-level physical-grounding layer that leverages efficient state estimation, in-situ 3D spatial perception, and an Signed Distance Field (SDF) representation to generate executable trajectories, and provides a navigation planner with provable collision-avoidance guarantees under the stated assumptions.

2611.04957.title: Safeguarding Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Connected and Automated Vehicles with Recursively Feasible Control Barrier Functions
2611.04957.abstract: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) shows promise in coordinating connected and automated vehicles but offers no safety guarantee. Although Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) can add this guarantee, their optimization problem can become infeasible in practice due to control bounds. Moreover, they often overapproximate vehicle and road geometry, which makes them conservative. This paper proposes the Backup-Horizon CBF (BH-CBF), which evaluates safety along a horizon until all vehicles stop. BH-CBF is recursively feasible under control bounds, and it considers the exact vehicle and road geometry. Based on BH-CBF, we derive a fully decentralized safety filter that only needs a single broadcast of vehicle states and routes per step and stays real-time in dense traffic. We use BH-CBF to safeguard a MARL policy over its life cycle: as a reward during pre-training, as a run-time filter at deployment, and as a filter in the training loop that keeps fine-tuning on unseen maps collision-free. In simulations on real-world maps of a roundabout and an intersection, BH-CBF avoids all collisions of unsafe MARL policies and keeps its safety guarantee at every step. Existing filters either collide, lose the guarantee, or fall back to full braking far more often. In recorded roundabout traffic with 1264 human-driven vehicles over 115 km, our safeguarded policies shorten the median travel time by 14% compared with the human drivers, without any collision.

llm.title_ja: 再帰的実行可能制御バリア関数を用いたコネクテッド自動運転車のためのマルチエージェント強化学習の保護
llm.tldr_ja: 車両が停止するまでのホライゾンに沿って安全性を評価し、制御境界の下で再帰的に実行可能なBackup-Horizon CBF（BH-CBF）を提案し、MARLポリシーの安全性を全ライフサイクルにわたり保証する。
llm.problem: マルチエージェント強化学習（MARL）は車両協調に有望だが安全性の保証がなく、従来のCBFは最適化問題が実行不可能になったり保守的になったりする。
llm.method: 停止までのホライゾンで安全性を評価し正確な形状を考慮するBackup-Horizon CBF（BH-CBF）を基にした、完全に分散型の安全フィルターを導出した。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実際の交通データを用いた検証において、未学習のマップでも衝突を完全に回避し、中央値の旅行時間を14%短縮した。
keywords_ja: マルチエージェント強化学習

2611.04957.tldr_en: The Backup-Horizon CBF (BH-CBF), which evaluates safety along a horizon until all vehicles stop, is proposed, which is recursively feasible under control bounds, and it considers the exact vehicle and road geometry.

2611.04873.title: Trusting Imagined Futures: Auditing Imagined Rewards for VLA Post-Training
2611.04873.abstract: Video world models enable candidate actions to be evaluated through imagined outcomes, but high predicted rewards can favor trajectories with poor execution quality. We introduce Trusting Imagined Futures (TIF), an offline supervision selection method for vision-language-action (VLA) post-training that audits predicted rewards using execution feedback. A multidimensional reward model predicts a utility score for candidate ranking and five dimensions of execution quality. An auditor uses reward predictions and uncertainty to identify overestimation patterns learned from paired imagined videos and real executions. TIF accepts the candidate with the highest predicted utility when its advantage over the existing trajectory exceeds a margin and its audit risk passes a threshold; otherwise, it retains the existing supervision. The retained real trajectories then supervise behavior cloning. Across four LIBERO suites and three training seeds, TIF achieves a mean success rate of 76.25%, improving over training on the existing trajectories by 3.00 percentage points with the same trajectory count and training budget. Adding audit gating yields 1.47 percentage points with the reward model and advantage margin held fixed. The gains persist against advantage ranking and logistic regression risk selection at matched replacement counts. On recorded videos from three real robot tasks, TIF increases clean completion among selected trajectories from 58.33% to 70.00% across 60 candidate pools.

llm.title_ja: 想像された未来の信頼：VLA事後訓練のための想像された報酬の監査
llm.tldr_ja: ビデオ世界モデルによって予測された報酬の過大評価パターンを、実行フィードバックと不確実性を用いて監査し、行動クローン作成の教師データを選択するTIF手法を提案する。
llm.problem: ビデオ世界モデルは想像された結果を通じて候補行動を評価できるが、予測された報酬の高さが実行品質の低い軌道を優先させてしまうことがある。
llm.method: 報酬の予測値と不確実性を用いてペアとなった想像ビデオと実実行から学習された過大評価パターンを識別する監査器を備えたオフライン教師データ選択手法TIFを導入した。
llm.result: LIBEROスイートでの実験において、同一の軌道数と訓練予算でベースラインを上回る平均成功率を達成し、実ロボットタスクでもクリーンな完了率を向上させた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.04873.tldr_en: Trusting Imagined Futures is introduced, an offline supervision selection method for vision-language-action (VLA) post-training that audits predicted rewards using execution feedback to identify overestimation patterns learned from paired imagined videos and real executions.

2611.04871.title: Physics-Based Plausibility Assessment of AI-Predicted Vehicle Parameters for Automotive Radar in Pre-Crash Scenarios
2611.04871.abstract: Automotive radar is a key sensing modality for safety-critical vehicle functions due to its robustness under adverse weather and lighting conditions. Recent advances in AI-based radar perception enable the direct estimation of object parameters from a single radar measurement cycle. However, the internal decision process of data-driven models is typically not explicitly linked to the underlying radar sensing physics. Consequently, object estimates may achieve high statistical accuracy while remaining physically inconsistent with the measured radar signature, particularly in previously unseen scenarios. Such inconsistencies are especially critical for heading estimation, as they directly affect trajectory prediction and collision assessment in pre-crash scenarios. This paper presents a physics-based consistency assessment framework for validating AI-derived vehicle hypotheses in automotive radar perception. The proposed approach generates an expected radar signature from AI-estimated object parameters using a physics-based reference model that incorporates occlusion-dependent edge visibility, aspect- and angle-dependent RCS modeling, and characteristic wheel-induced MD signatures. The expected signature is compared with the observed radar point cloud using a Wasserstein-distance-based consistency metric computed from three complementary features: the spatial distribution of detections along object edges, the local detection count, and the radar reflection intensity. In this way, physically implausible object hypotheses can be identified and corrected independently of the underlying neural network architecture and without model retraining or architectural modifications. The proposed consistency module is integrated as a cascaded post-processing stage for vehicle heading estimation.

llm.title_ja: プレクラッシュシナリオにおける車載レーダー向けAI予測車両パラメータの物理ベース妥当性評価
llm.tldr_ja: AIベースのレーダー知覚から得られたオブジェクトパラメータから物理ベースの参照モデルを用いて期待されるレーダーシグネチャを生成し、観測されたポイントクラウドと比較することで物理的に不自然な仮説を検証・修正するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: AIベースのレーダー知覚は単一測定サイクルからオブジェクトパラメータを推定できるが、データ駆動型モデルの内部決定プロセスがレーダーの物理センシングと結びついておらず、物理的に矛盾した推定が生じうる。
llm.method: 隠蔽依存のエッジ可視性やRCSモデルなどを組み込んだ物理ベース参照モデルにより期待されるレーダーシグネチャを生成し、ワッサースタイン距離に基づく一貫性メトリックで観測値と比較する。
llm.result: ニューラルネットワークのアーキテクチャや再学習を変更することなく、物理的に不自然なオブジェクト仮説を独立して特定・修正できることをカスケード型後処理ステージとして統合した。
keywords_ja: プレクラッシュシナリオ

2611.04870.title: PrimeSim: A Generalist World Model Simulator from Large-Scale Cross-Embodiment Demonstrations
2611.04870.abstract: A robot world model that serves as a simulator must do more than generate plausible videos: it must faithfully follow commanded actions, maintain consistency across camera views, and sustain coherent long-horizon rollouts. We present PrimeSim, an action-conditioned, multiview world model simulator that addresses these challenges through progressive midtraining and posttraining. Starting from a pretrained video generator, we midtrain on 30,110 hours of robot demonstrations spanning 22 platforms. To improve action following, we introduce a unified cross-embodiment action representation and frame-aligned dual-path conditioning to strengthen action-frame correspondence. To maintain multiview consistency, we develop view-aware interleaved attention with explicit camera identities, enabling cross-view information exchange while preserving view-specific representations. We further introduce a fast-video, slow-memory posttraining framework that transforms the bidirectional video generator into an efficient autoregressive simulator. By combining fast causal generation, self-rollout training, and hierarchical temporal memory, PrimeSim mitigates error accumulation from self-generated histories and supports coherent long-horizon simulation. PrimeSim runs at 10.1 FPS, remains stable over long-horizon rollouts on rigid and deformable manipulation tasks, and transfers to held-out platforms within 100 to 200 gradient steps where the pretrained backbone does not. Against five open-source action-conditioned world models it leads four of the five WorldSimProbe suites and posts the best overall EWMBench score, while fine-grained local calibration still trails the field; its rollouts are faithful enough to support GRPO-based policy optimization. We release the model weights, inference code, and training code.
2611.04870.hf_summary_en: PrimeSim is an action-conditioned multiview world model that uses progressive training, unified action representations, view-aware attention, and hierarchical memory to enable consistent, long-horizon robot simulation and policy optimization.

llm.title_ja: PrimeSim: 大規模クロスエンボディメントデモンストレーションからの汎用世界モデルシミュレータ
llm.tldr_ja: 統一された行動表現、視点認識アテンション、階層的時間メモリを活用し、一貫した長期的なロボットシミュレーションとポリシー最適化を可能にする行動条件付きマルチビュー世界モデルPrimeSimを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットの世界モデルシミュレータは、単なる妥当なビデオ生成だけでなく、命令された行動への忠実な追従、カメラビュー間の整合性維持、一貫した長期ロールアウトの維持が求められる。
llm.method: 事前学習済みビデオ生成器をベースに、30,110時間のロボット実演データを用いたプログレッシブミッドトレーニングと、高速因果生成・自己ロールアウト訓練・階層的メモリによるポストトレーニングを実施した。
llm.result: 10.1 FPSで動作し、長期ロールアウトにおいて安定性を保ち、未学習のプラットフォームへ数100勾配ステップで転移可能であり、WorldSimProbeスイート等で優れた成績を収めた。
llm.limitation: きめ細やかな局所的較正ではまだ他手法に劣る場合がある。
keywords_ja: クロスエンボディメント

2611.04870.tldr_en: This work introduces a fast-video, slow-memory posttraining framework that transforms the bidirectional video generator into an efficient autoregressive simulator that mitigates error accumulation from self-generated histories and supports coherent long-horizon simulation.

2611.04839.title: Coordinating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Action-Conditioned Latent Foresight
2611.04839.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated body motion and hand interaction over time, and a plausible-looking command sequence can still drop a held object or leave an interaction incomplete. We present action-conditioned latent foresight, a latent world-action model (WAM) that evaluates proposed command sequences before execution. An action generator proposes joint motion-hand command sequences from vision, language, and the robot state. An action-conditioned endpoint predictor estimates the visual features each sequence prefix reaches and measures progress toward a demonstration-derived subgoal, while a joint temporal prior scores temporal consistency given the robot state and preceding commands. The robot executes the first commands of the best-scoring sequence and replans from the next observation. During training, action consistency regularization reconstructs the first demonstrated command from observed and predicted feature changes, encouraging the predictor to retain action-relevant information. On ten tasks in the humanoid loco-manipulation simulation benchmark SIMPLE, our method achieves 89.7% average success, compared with 73.7% for Psi-Zero and 82.0% for DiT4DiT. On seven real-robot tasks, it achieves 85.7% under standard conditions and 65.7% under unseen object configurations, while GR00T N1.7 achieves 70.0% and 48.6%, respectively. Project page: https://ju6276.github.io/Action-Grounded-Foresight/

llm.title_ja: 行動条件付き潜在的先読みによるヒューノロイド移動マニピュレーションの協調
llm.tldr_ja: ビジョン、言語、ロボット状態から提案された関節・手のコマンドシーケンスを、実行前に視覚的特徴の到達予測や部分目標への進捗度測定によって評価・選択する潜在的世界行動モデルを提案する。
llm.problem: 人型ロボットの移動マニピュレーションでは身体動作と手のインタラクションの協調が必要だが、一見もっともらしいコマンドでも把持物を落としたりタスクを未完了にしたりする。
llm.method: 提案されたコマンドシーケンスの視覚的特徴の変化や進捗度を予測・評価し、最良のシーケンスの初期コマンドを実行して再計画を行う行動条件付き潜在的先読み手法を提案した。
llm.result: シミュレーションベンチマークSIMPLEおよび7つの実ロボットタスクにおいて、従来手法を大きく上回る平均成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーション

2611.04839.tldr_en: Action-conditioned latent foresight, a latent world-action model that evaluates proposed command sequences before execution, and an action generator that proposes joint motion-hand command sequences from vision, language, and the robot state are presented.

2611.04836.title: HTCE: Homeomorphism-inspired Topological Cross-Scene Experience Canonicalization and Reuse for Object Navigation
2611.04836.abstract: As embodied agents perform object-goal navigation across residential environments, they accumulate successful experiences whose semantic structure recurs across scenes even when geometric trajectories do not. Reusing such experience is challenging because differences in region naming and observation granularity produce distinct graph representations of similar approaches, while meaningful differences in anchors, branches, and endpoints must stay distinguishable. We introduce HTCE, a homeomorphism-inspired topological framework that canonicalizes and reuses navigation experience. Feature and topology subdivisions characterize representational variations, and their semantically constrained reductions produce comparable semantic sequences and structural signatures while preserving semantic anchors, branching relations, and navigation endpoints. HTCE then retrieves historical successful approaches through subdivision-aware matching as guidance for a frozen vision-language policy. Canonicalization compresses the experience index losslessly, merging 17.7--23.6\% of distinct stored route descriptions while retaining full task performance. Under a single frozen vision-language backbone shared by all compared systems, HTCE attains the best SR and SPL in every setting---59.9\%/31.8\% on HM3D v0.1, 71.0\%/31.5\% on HM3D v0.2, and 46.6\%/16.6\% on MP3D---with SR gains of up to 4.9 points and structured retrieval contributing up to 2.8 SPL points. The code is available in https://github.com/startracker0/htce.git

llm.title_ja: HTCE: オブジェクトナビゲーションのための同相写像にインスパイアされた位相的クロスシーン経験の正準化と再利用
llm.tldr_ja: 特徴と位相の細分化によりナビゲーション経験を表現の変動に依存しない構造的シグネチャへと正準化し、凍結された視覚言語ポリシーへガイドとして提供する位相的フレームワークHTCEを提案する。
llm.problem: 環境間でオブジェクトナビゲーションを行う際、領域名の違いや観察粒度の差により異なるグラフ表現が生成されるため、過去の成功経験の再利用が困難である。
llm.method: 同相写像にインスパイアされた位相的フレームワークにより、意味的アンカーや分岐関係を保持しつつ、ルート記述を正準化して検索・再利用するHTCEを開発した。
llm.result: HM3DやMP3Dなどのベンチマークにおいて、視覚言語バックボーンを共有するすべての比較手法の中で最高の成功率（SR）とSPLを達成した。
keywords_ja: オブジェクトナビゲーション
位相的フレームワーク

2611.04817.title: The Pen is Mightier than the Pixel: Natural Textual Unlearnable Example for Large Vision Language Models
2611.04817.abstract: The proliferation of Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs), trained on vast and often sensitive datasets, raised concerns regarding data privacy and unauthorized usage. Unlearnable Examples (UEs), which subtly perturb training data to mislead the models, have emerged as a promising defense method. This paper presents the first exploration of UEs specifically on LVLMs, which poses unique challenges due to their inherent multimodal nature. We propose a novel text-based perturbation method, Natural Textual Unlearnable Examples (NTUE), which can effectively mislead LVLMs by subtly manipulating the image label, establishing a shortcut between an identity of interest and a separate target, without introducing factual misinformation or affecting readability. Comprehensive experiments compared with traditional UE methods demonstrate the superior performance of NTUE. Our findings show that NTUE achieves a high success rate with a poison rate as low as 5%, underscoring its potential as a practical and robust solution for protecting multimodal data in the era of LVLMs.

llm.title_ja: ペンはピクセルよりも強し：大規模視覚言語モデルのための自然テキスト型アンラーナブル例
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模視覚言語モデル（LVLMs）のデータプライバシーを保護するため、事実の誤情報を導入せず読しやすさも保ちながら画像ラベルを微細に操作してモデルを誤導する自然テキスト型アンラーナブル例（NTUE）を提案する。
llm.problem: 広範で機密性の高いデータセットで訓練される大規模視覚言語モデル（LVLMs）のデータプライバシーと不正利用に関する懸念が高まっている。
llm.method: 関心のあるアイデンティティと別のターゲットの間にショートカットを確立し、LVLMを誤導するテキストベースの摂動手法NTUEを提案した。
llm.result: わずか5%のポイズン率で高い成功率を達成し、マルチモーダルデータを保護するための実践的かつ堅牢なソリューションとしての有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: 大規模視覚言語モデル
マルチモーダルデータ

2611.04755.title: iMED: A Multi-Endoscope Dataset for Surgical 3D Perception
2611.04755.abstract: We introduce iMED, the first synchronized multi-endoscope dataset for robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery (RAMIS), designed to address a fundamental limitation in surgical vision benchmarking: the absence of independent held-out viewpoints. Existing surgical datasets capture single-trajectory sequences from a single endoscope, making it impossible to distinguish geometric generalization from photometric interpolation along a narrow forward-facing path. iMED provides 340 sequences ~170K synchronized timepoints with 4 views per timepoint) recorded simultaneously from two independent stereo endoscopes across ex vivo, postmortem, and live surgical settings, spanning 14 specimens with diverse anatomical regions and motion regimes. The dataset includes calibrated camera intrinsics, ArUco-based frame-wise pose estimates with uncertainty quantification, instrument segmentation masks, and rich clinical metadata. Using a train-on-one-endoscope, test-on-another evaluation protocol, we benchmark 23 state-of-the-art methods across rigid and deformable novel view synthesis, pose estimation, feature matching, and monocular depth estimation. Our experiments show that methods relying primarily on photometric supervision degrade substantially under this held-out-endoscope setting, while methods with explicit geometric regularization are more robust across views in our benchmark. Notably, large-scale foundation models transfer surprisingly well to surgical imagery, often outperforming domain-specific models, suggesting pitfalls in current fine-tuning protocols. iMED establishes a new evaluation protocol for geometric generalization in surgical vision.
2611.04755.comment: Published at ECCV 2026. 25 pages, including supplementary material. Code and dataset: https://github.com/surgical-vision/imed

llm.title_ja: iMED: 外科的3D知覚のためのマルチ内視鏡データセット
llm.tldr_ja: 独立した非表示の視点からの評価を可能にし、幾何学的汎化性能をベンチマークするための、ロボット支援低侵襲手術向けの最初の同期マルチ内視鏡データセットiMEDを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の外科用データセットは単一の内視鏡からの単一軌道シーケンスしか取得しておらず、狭い前方パスに沿った幾何学的汎化と測光補間を区別することが不可能である。
llm.method: エクスビボ、ポストモーテム、生体手術の設定から、2つの独立したステレオ内視鏡を用いて同時に記録された340シーケンス（約170Kの同期タイムポイント）を提供するiMEDを構築した。
llm.result: 23の最先端手法をベンチマーク評価し、測光監督に依存する手法は保持された内視鏡設定下で大幅に性能が低下する一方、幾何学的正則化を持つ手法は堅牢であることを示した。

2611.04755.tldr_en: iMED establishes a new evaluation protocol for geometric generalization in surgical vision, and benchmarks 23 state-of-the-art methods across rigid and deformable novel view synthesis, pose estimation, feature matching, and monocular depth estimation.

2611.04748.title: Mass Scaling Laws for Energy-Optimal Horizontal Multirotor Flight
2611.04748.abstract: Multicopters are a type of aerial robot seeing extensive real-world applications but with range and endurance as critical bottlenecks. Optimization of its energy efficiency through energy-aware flight planning (e.g. cruise speed-scheduling) has hence been an important topic. The mass of the multicopter is an important factor to consider, as it has a significant impact on efficiency, and many common applications are subject to frequent mass variation due to payload change. This work derives closed-form scaling relationships between the energy-optimal steady horizontal flight behavior of a multicopter and its vehicle mass, and validates them experimentally on two multirotor platforms. Specifically, for mass-only variation, i.e., when payload changes the vehicle mass while the airframe geometry, aerodynamic characteristics, and rotor configuration remain unchanged, we show through a combination of numerical simulation, theoretical derivation, and experimental validation that (1) the energy-optimal velocity is proportional to the square root of vehicle mass; (2) the energy-optimal pitch angle is constant with respect to mass; and (3) the optimal energy per meter is proportional to mass. The analysis shows that these three relationships arise from a common mass-similarity property of the steady-state flight and rotor-aerodynamic equations. Furthermore, the obtained scaling relationships enable simple yet effective cruise-speed planning to optimize energy efficiency and extend the range and endurance of the multicopter.
2611.04748.comment: Accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, October 2026

llm.title_ja: エネルギー最適水平マルチロータ飛行のための質量スケーリング則
llm.tldr_ja: マルチロータのエネルギー最適定常水平飛行と機体質量の間に閉形式のスケーリング関係を導出し、2つのプラットフォームで実験的に検証した。
llm.problem: マルチロータ機は航続距離と耐久性が課題であり、ペイロード変化による質量変動がエネルギー効率に大きな影響を与えること。
llm.method: 数値シミュレーション、理論的導出、実機検証を組み合わせ、エネルギー最適速度が質量の平方根に比例することなどを明らかにした。
llm.result: エネルギー最適速度は質量の平方根に比例し、最適ピッチ角は質量に対して一定であり、1メートルあたりの最適エネルギーは質量に比例することを示した。

2611.04728.title: SPOD: Recovering Suppressed Temporal Evidence in Video-LLMs via Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition
2611.04728.abstract: Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) have achieved strong performance on many video understanding tasks, yet remain vulnerable to temporal hallucination in time-sensitive reasoning scenarios such as scene transition understanding and event ordering. Existing solutions either require costly retraining or introduce inefficient multi-pass inference and external supervision at test time. In this work, we show that temporal evidence is already encoded in Video-LLM hidden representations but is not fully exploited during standard inference. Motivated by this observation, we propose Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition (SPOD), a training-free framework that recovers suppressed temporal evidence through analytical hidden-state manipulation in a single forward pass. SPOD consists of two components: Frame Distinctiveness Analysis (FDA), which identifies salient frames from middle-layer hidden-state geometry, and Temporal Delta Subspace (TDS), which constructs orthogonal temporal and prior subspaces from weighted inter-frame hidden-state differences. By decomposing final hidden states into temporal, prior, and residual components and rescaling them independently, SPOD enhances dynamic information, suppresses static appearance bias, and preserves complementary information. Experiments on VidHalluc, EventHallusion, and VideoMMMU show that SPOD consistently outperforms strong inference-time baselines across temporal reasoning tasks and model architectures while retaining near-vanilla inference efficiency. These results suggest that improving temporal reasoning in Video-LLMs may depend not only on additional supervision, but also on recovering temporal evidence already present in their internal representations. Our code is available at https://github.com/VioAgnes/SPOD.

llm.title_ja: SPOD: 単一パス直交分解によるVideo-LLMの抑制された時間的証拠の復元
llm.tldr_ja: 学習不要のフレームワークであるSPODを提案し、単一のフォワードパスにおける隠れ状態の解析的操作によって、Video-LLMの時間的幻覚を軽減した。

llm.method: 中間層の隠れ状態から顕著なフレームを特定するフレーム特徴量分析と、直交する時間的・事前部分空間を構築する時間的デルタ部分空間を組み合わせた。
llm.result: VidHalluc、EventHallusion、VideoMMMUの実験において、従来の推論時ベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2611.04711.title: Cycle WAM: Coupling Action and Video through Cycle Consistency
2611.04711.abstract: Recent advances in video modeling have driven substantial progress in world action models (WAMs). Existing approaches exploit pretrained video priors by decoding actions from latent representations or inferring them from generated videos. The underlying link is causal: robot actions produce changes in the scene, and video observations of these changes provide evidence for inferring the actions that produced them. However, existing training formulations do not by themselves ensure that actions and their predicted visual consequences are consistent, potentially limiting the use of pretrained capabilities. We treat video and action as paired modalities linked by this causal relationship and learn their correspondence through a unified training framework designed to better exploit pretrained video priors. Cycle WAM first augments video-action co-training with bidirectional conversion to reinforce cross-modal correspondence and recover forward and inverse dynamics. It then introduces a differentiable cycle-reconstruction objective to further couple the two mappings. The resulting model supports both forward and inverse dynamics, with the potential to improve performance through more effective use of pretrained video priors. Cycle WAM achieves state-of-the-art performance among comparable methods on LIBERO-Pro and substantially improves DreamZero on DROID. Comparisons with UWM characterize its inverse-dynamics performance and show sharper visual detail in the displayed forward-dynamics predictions.

llm.title_ja: Cycle WAM: 周期一貫性を通じた行動とビデオの結合
llm.tldr_ja: ビデオと行動を因果関係で結ばれたペアモダリティとして扱い、事前学習済みビデオ事前分布を活用するための統一された訓練フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の行動モデルは行動と予測された視覚的結果の一貫性を保証せず、事前学習された能力の活用が制限されていること。
llm.method: 双方向変換によるビデオ・行動の共同訓練と、2つのマッピングを結合する微分可能な周期再構成目的を導入した。
llm.result: LIBERO-Proにおいて同等手法の中で最高性能を達成し、DROID上のDreamZeroを大幅に改善した。

2611.04710.title: DenseTwins: Dense Modality Decoupling for Multimodal Self-Supervision
2611.04710.abstract: Multimodal perception is central to many computer vision applications, including robotics and autonomous driving, where different sensing modalities provide complementary cues. Self-supervised learning offers a scalable solution for exploiting large amounts of unlabeled multimodal data. However, existing methods either neglect modality-specific information by enforcing feature-space alignment between modalities or learn only global representations without preserving spatial structure. We propose DenseTwins, a multimodal self-supervised framework that learns dense representations by explicitly decoupling the dense feature space into shared and modality-specific components. The proposed approach combines dense cross-modal correspondences with redundancy-reduction objectives, enabling the model to capture both shared semantics and modality-specific cues within a structured dense embedding space. DenseTwins jointly optimizes an intra-modal objective across augmented views and a cross-modal objective that aligns shared features while decorrelating modality-specific information. We evaluate DenseTwins across multiple multimodal benchmarks and sensing setups, achieving state-of-the-art or competitive performance across multimodal self-supervised baselines. Code available at: https://github.com/CarloSgaravatti/DenseTwins.

llm.title_ja: DenseTwins: マルチモーダル自己教師あり学習のための密なモダリティ分離
llm.tldr_ja: 密な特徴空間を共有成分とモダリティ固有成分に明示的に分離することで、密な表現を学習するマルチモーダル自己教師あり学習フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の手法はモーダル間の特徴空間の整合を強制するか、空間構造を保存せずにグローバル表現のみを学習すること。
llm.method: 密なクロスモーダル対応と冗長性削減の目的関数を組み合わせ、共有セマンティクスとモダリティ固有の手がかりを学習する。
llm.result: 複数のマルチモーダルベンチマークにおいて、既存の自己教師ありベースラインと同等またはそれを上回る性能を達成した。

2611.04710.tldr_en: DenseTwins is proposed, a multimodal self-supervised framework that learns dense representations by explicitly decoupling the dense feature space into shared and modality-specific components within a structured dense embedding space.

2611.04708.title: CLARA: A Cognitively-Driven Clarification Framework for Grounding Ambiguous Requests
2611.04708.abstract: Robotics and AI systems are increasingly deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) to follow high-level instructions, from routine household chores to more complex organizational tasks. Yet, broad directives like "clean the room" or "organize the desk" frequently omit crucial details about user preferences and specific arrangement of objects that influence the desired outcome. Without any further guidance, such models tend to overestimate their grasp of ambiguous instructions and frequently assume they have sufficient understanding despite missing important details. In this paper, we propose CLARA (Conversational cLArification for Robotic Arrangement), a cognitively-driven clarification framework that proactively elicits key information from users, in a similar fashion as humans' clarification seeking behavior. Through targeted questioning, CLARA refines ambiguous requests into structured, detailed instructions describing precisely how objects should be organized or rearranged, according to the user's preferences. These clarifications then guide a diffusion-based image generation pipeline, producing realistic visual renderings of the final, desired scene. This final rendering also serves as a visual confirmation of the system's understanding from the user. Experimental results and user studies demonstrate that CLARA leads to more accurate and consistent outcomes compared to another State-of-the-Art LVLM system, highlighting the importance of interactive clarification for bridging the gap between vague directives and fully grounded task specifications.

llm.title_ja: CLARA: 曖昧な指示をグラウンディングするための認知的駆動型明確化フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: ユーザーとの対話を通じて曖昧な指示を詳細な構造化指示へと洗練させる、認知的駆動型の明確化フレームワークCLARAを提案した。
llm.problem: 「部屋を掃除して」などの幅広い指示には、ユーザーの好みや具体的なオブジェクトの配置に関する重要な詳細が欠けていること。
llm.method: ユーザーへの標的型質問により曖昧な要求を洗練し、拡散ベースの画像生成パイプラインを通じて最終的なシーンの視覚的レンダリングを作成する。
llm.result: 既存の最先端LVLMシステムと比較して、より正確で一貫性のある結果をもたらすことを示した。
keywords_ja: 大規模視覚言語モデル

2611.04708.tldr_en: This paper proposes CLARA (Conversational cLArification for Robotic Arrangement), a cognitively-driven clarification framework that proactively elicits key information from users, in a similar fashion as humans' Clarification seeking behavior, highlighting the importance of interactive clarification for bridging the gap between vague directives and fully grounded task specifications.

2611.04692.title: Just Between Us? Exploring a Wearable-Mediated Channel for Discreet Human-Agent Interaction in a Shared Game Setting
2611.04692.abstract: In shared settings, social robots may need to exchange information with an individual while limiting co-present others' access to or interpretation of that information. Publicly observable speech and gestures may not adequately support such exchanges. We investigate a wearable-mediated channel for discreet interaction that combines in-ear audio messages with deliberate rightward head tilts as responses. To examine its feasibility and participants' experiences, we studied 20 pairs (40 participants) playing a card game with a screen-based conversational agent representing a social robot, controlled by a researcher in a Wizard-of-Oz setup. Each pair played with and without the channel. One participant wore the device (the wearer), while the other (the non-wearer) was informed about the channel after gameplay. The channel conveyed information that could help the wearer or robot character select an opponent they could defeat. The information exchange and subsequent opponent selection occurred as intended in 39 of 40 channel-mediated turns. Wearers reported low perceived pressure/tension in both conditions, with no statistically significant difference between conditions, and favorable usability immediately after use. Retrospective interviews, however, revealed varied accounts of noticing the interaction among non-wearers and contrasting perceptions of teamwork and unfairness. These findings support the feasibility of wearable-mediated exchanges within this game and identify awareness and fairness as considerations for future designs.

llm.title_ja: 私たちだけの秘密？共有ゲーム環境における目立たないヒューマン・エージェント間インタラクションのためのウェアラブル媒介チャネルの探索
llm.tldr_ja: インイヤー音声メッセージと右向きのうなずきを組み合わせた、ウェアラブル媒介による目立たないインタラクションチャネルの実現可能性を検証した。
