2611.04543.title: CANDO: Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization for Residual Reinforcement Learning
2611.04543.abstract: Pretrained generative policies provide strong behavior priors for robot control, but adapting them efficiently with online reinforcement learning remains difficult. A central challenge is how to improve a frozen generative policy without destroying the structure learned from offline demonstrations. Noise-space residual methods address this by modifying the policy's input noise, but existing noise-space methods typically regulate adaptation through fixed latent feasible regions, which may exclude valuable noise edits. In contrast, action-space residual methods are more sample-efficient, but their efficiency can still be further improved. We propose Conservative Noise Directional Optimization (CNDO), a noise-space residual RL method that improves a frozen generative policy by learning state- and noise-conditioned directions around Gaussian latent samples. CNDO removes predefined latent feasible regions and instead regulates noise-space adaptation through the soft conservative constraint, which consists of conservative value estimation and gated execution. We further introduce Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization (CANDO), which adds an action-space residual, combining structured latent-space improvement with local action correction. Experiments show that, once CNDO narrows the gap between noise-space and action-space residual learning, CANDO further improves over single-space optimization, achieving 76.1 NAUC and a 91.4% final success rate, surpassing the best single-space results by 6.6 NAUC and 4.1% success rate. More demos and info are available on https://cando-rl.github.io/.

llm.title_ja: CANDO: 残差強化学習のための保守的行動・ノイズ方向最適化
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの生成ポリシーを改善するために、ソフト保守的制約を用いてノイズ空間の適応を調整するCANDO手法を提案した。
llm.problem: オフラインデモの構造を破壊せずに凍結された生成ポリシーをオンライン強化学習で効率的に適応させることが難しいこと。
llm.method: 事前定義された潜在的可視領域を排除し、保守的価値推定とゲート付き実行からなるソフト保守的制約によってノイズ空間適応を調整する。
llm.result: CANDOは単一空間最適化を上回り、NAUC 76.1および最終成功率91.4%を達成した。

2611.04543.tldr_en: Conservative Noise Directional Optimization (CNDO), a noise-space residual RL method that improves a frozen generative policy by learning state- and noise-conditioned directions around Gaussian latent samples, and Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization (CANDO), which adds an action-space residual, combining structured latent-space improvement with local action correction.

2611.04527.title: Future Representation Distillation for Imagination-free World Action Models
2611.04527.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) use the predictive knowledge of pretrained video diffusion models for robot control through future video prediction. However, iterative video denoising is costly, and inaccurate visual predictions can compromise action prediction. Our key idea is to make this predictive knowledge available through visual representations computed from the current observation, enabling action prediction without generating future videos. We introduce DreamFree, a WAM that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a predictive visual encoder through representation distillation. The visual encoder learns to predict a frozen video diffusion model's representation using only the current observation. An action module is then trained to predict actions by extracting action-relevant information from the visual encoder. Across real-world and simulated tasks, DreamFree achieves higher success rates than state-of-the-art VLAs and WAMs, while performing real-time closed-loop control at 11Hz with a 14B video diffusion backbone. Experiments show that DreamFree can translate stronger video priors and additional video data into better robot control and enable learning new robot tasks from video demonstrations, including videos from a different embodiment, without action annotation for the new tasks.
2611.04527.tldr_en: Experiments show that DreamFree can translate stronger video priors and additional video data into better robot control and enable learning new robot tasks from video demonstrations, including videos from a different embodiment, without action annotation for the new tasks.

2611.04522.title: Action Intent as a Bridge: Transferring Manipulation Knowledge from Human-Centric Videos to Robots
2611.04522.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have achieved promising performance for generalized robotic manipulation, yet their reliance on expensive real-robot data remains a fundamental bottleneck. A scalable alternative is to transfer knowledge from off-the-shelf human-centric videos. However, existing methods extract latent action representations that are entangled with scene-specific noise, diluting the transferred knowledge. Motivated by this limitation, we propose Action-Intent Transfer (AIT), a two-stage method that transfers knowledge through a clean action representation shared across humans and robots. In the first stage, AIT extracts explicit action intents and disentangles the implicit action intent from manipulation videos. In the second stage, AIT aligns the human and robot domains within this shared intent space and decodes the intent into executable robot actions. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world environments demonstrate that AIT transfers human knowledge more effectively and consistently outperforms prior baselines.

llm.title_ja: 行動意図を架け橋として：人間中心のビデオからロボットへのマニピュレーション知識の移転
llm.tldr_ja: 人間とロボットの間で共有されるクリーンな行動表現を通じて知識を移転する2段階の手法であるAction-Intent Transfer (AIT)を提案した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルは高価な実機ロボットデータへの依存がボトルネックであり、既存手法の人間動画からの知識抽出にはシーン特有のノイズが混入すること。
llm.method: 第1段階で明示的な行動意図を抽出し、第2段階で人間とロボットのドメインを共通の意図空間内で整列させて実行可能なロボット行動にデコードする。
llm.result: シミュレーションと実世界の双方の実験において、人間からの知識を効果的に移転し、既存のベースラインを一貫して上回った。

2611.04522.tldr_en: Action-Intent Transfer is proposed, a two-stage method that transfers knowledge through a clean action representation shared across humans and robots that transfers human knowledge more effectively and consistently outperforms prior baselines.

2611.04518.title: LLM-Assisted Planning with Distributed Onboard Behaviour Tree Execution for Multi-AUV Missions
2611.04518.abstract: Coordinating autonomous underwater vehicles requires translating operator intent into feasible assignments while preserving autonomous execution when communication is limited. We present a hierarchical framework that couples Large Language Model (LLM) interpretation of natural-language mission instructions with Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and distributed Behaviour Tree (BT) execution. The LLM extracts assignment and ordering constraints, which the MILP optimizer combines with vehicle capabilities and temporal requirements. A BT-LLM Bridge distributes the resulting allocations to onboard BT Mission Managers. Per-vehicle Robotic Agents assess local faults and request selective replanning, allowing unaffected vehicles to continue their assigned tasks. Evaluation in a ROS-based AUV simulator compares Qwen-3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B on constraint extraction and tests recovery from sensor degradation and critical vehicle faults. Qwen-3-8B provides more accurate constraint extraction, and all tasks are completed in the tested failure scenarios. These simulation results support the feasibility of combining language-based mission specification with structured allocation and distributed execution.

llm.title_ja: マルチAUVミッションのための分散型オンボード行動木実行を伴うLLM支援計画
llm.tldr_ja: 自然言語のミッション指示のLLM解釈と、混合整数線形計画法および分散型行動木の実行を組み合わせた階層型フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 自律型水中ビークル（AUV）の協調には、通信が制限された状況下で自律実行を維持しつつ、オペレーターの意図を実行可能な割り当てに翻訳する必要があること。
llm.method: LLMが割り当てと順序の制約を抽出し、MILPオプティマイザーが車両の能力と要件を組み合わせて配分し、BT-LLMブリッジがオンボードのミッションマネージャーに配布する。
llm.result: Qwen-3-8Bによる正確な制約抽出が示され、センサー劣化や車両故障を伴うすべてのテストシナリオでタスクが完了した。

2611.04518.tldr_en: Simulation results support the feasibility of combining language-based mission specification with structured allocation and distributed execution with Mixed-Integer Linear Programming and distributed Behaviour Tree execution.

2611.04493.title: Physical Diffusion Policy via MPM-Guided 3D Gaussian Simulation
2611.04493.abstract: Learning robust manipulation policies for diverse everyday objects remains challenging because objects with different materials exhibit distinct deformation and contact dynamics. While diffusion policies provide a powerful framework for modeling multimodal manipulation behaviors, they typically lack explicit physical reasoning and may produce averaged actions when facing heterogeneous objects. We present a physics-aware diffusion policy that augments visual imitation learning with object physical understanding. Our framework recovers material properties from visual demonstrations by coupling 3D Gaussian Splatting with differentiable Material Point Method simulation, where video guidance and particle-level constraints enable accurate physical parameter estimation. The estimated physics conditions are further integrated into a material-aware Mixture-of-Experts diffusion policy, allowing adaptive behavior generation across different physical regimes. For practical deployment, we introduce a physics memory bank that provides efficient physical retrieval without requiring online simulation optimization. Experiments on a wide range of simulated and real-world objects demonstrate improved manipulation success and generalization over existing diffusion-based approaches. These results show that incorporating physical knowledge is critical for scalable robot manipulation in diverse environments.

llm.title_ja: MPM誘導3Dガウスシミュレーションによる物理拡散ポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的模倣学習とオブジェクトの物理的理解を統合し、多様な材質のオブジェクトに対して適応的な動作生成を行う物理認識型拡散ポリシーを提案した。
llm.problem: 異物や異なる材質を持つオブジェクトは独自の変形や接触ダイナミクスを持つため、従来の拡散ポリシーでは平均化された行動が生成されやすいこと。
llm.method: 3Dガウススプラッティングと微分可能物質点法（MPM）シミュレーションを結合して視覚デモから物性値を復元し、混合エキスパート拡散ポリシーに統合した。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界の多様なオブジェクトを用いた実験において、既存の拡散ベースの手法を上回るマニピュレーション成功率と汎化性能を示した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2611.04493.tldr_en: A physics-aware diffusion policy is presented that augments visual imitation learning with object physical understanding and shows that incorporating physical knowledge is critical for scalable robot manipulation in diverse environments.

2611.04492.title: Hybrid Particle-Voxel Dynamics for Multimodal 3D World Simulation
2611.04492.abstract: Predicting how the world evolves in response to robot actions is central to policy learning, evaluation, and planning. However, many action-conditioned world models predict future observations in 2D image or video space without explicitly modeling the underlying 3D scene, making spatial consistency across viewpoints and over long-horizon interactions challenging. We introduce 3D World Simulator, an action-conditioned multimodal world modeling framework that jointly predicts appearance, geometry, and tactile observations from a unified 3D representation. Our approach combines a hybrid particle-voxel autoencoder that compresses point clouds into compact 3D voxel latents with an action-conditioned latent dynamics model that predicts their evolution. The shared 3D representation supports geometrically consistent rendering from arbitrary viewpoints and flexible integration of spatially aligned tactile signals. Our experiments demonstrate interactive, long-horizon, multimodal prediction at 50 Hz. We then show how our model enables scalable data generation for policy training and evaluation using tactile and multi-view visual observations, including wrist-mounted and novel camera views. Furthermore, we scale our method to large datasets containing diverse objects and demonstrate model-based planning with unseen objects and robot configurations. Together, these results highlight the potential of hybrid particle-voxel dynamics as a foundation for multimodal 3D world simulation.

llm.title_ja: マルチモーダル3D世界シミュレーションのためのハイブリッド粒子-ボクセルダイナミクス
llm.tldr_ja: 点群をコンパクトな3Dボクセル潜在表現に圧縮するハイブリッド粒子-ボクセルオートエンコーダと、その進化を予測する行動条件付き潜在ダイナミクスモデルを提案した。
llm.problem: 多くの世界モデルは2D画像やビデオ空間で将来の観測を予測するため、視点間や長期的相互作用における空間的一貫性の維持が困難であること。
llm.method: 外観、幾何学、触覚の観測を統一された3D表現から共同で予測するアクション条件付きマルチモーダル世界モデリングフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 50Hzでのインタラクティブで長期的なマルチモーダル予測を実現し、未知のオブジェクトやロボット構成に対するモデルベースの計画を可能にした。

2611.04492.tldr_en: 3D World Simulator is introduced, an action-conditioned multimodal world modeling framework that jointly predicts appearance, geometry, and tactile observations from a unified 3D representation that enables scalable data generation for policy training and evaluation using tactile and multi-view visual observations.

2611.04485.title: All-For-One: Distilling Visual Foundation Models to a Fast, Memory-Efficient Visuomotor Policy
2611.04485.abstract: Visual Foundation Models (VFMs) provide semantic cues such as depth and segmentation useful for robotic manipulation, but directly deploying them in closed-loop control is impractical due to high computational cost, temporal inconsistency, and distribution shift between static internet images and egocentric robot observations. We propose All-For-One (AFO), a two-stage distillation framework that leverages VFMs strictly as privileged information during training, using downstream robotic data. Following the privileged learning paradigm, AFO decouples semantic representation learning from inference-time policy execution. In the All stage, a teacher policy fuses RGB observations with outputs from multiple VFMs to learn a semantically enriched representation. In the For-One stage, this knowledge is distilled in-distribution into a lightweight RGB-only student policy. Evaluated on two Adroit tasks and five MetaWorld tasks in simulation, as well as three real-world manipulation tasks, AFO outperforms prior foundation-model-based approaches while using over 30x fewer parameters than VFM-based encoders and 50x lower latency than its own teacher in simulation benchmarks, providing an efficient pathway for transferring foundation-model knowledge to robotic control.

llm.title_ja: All-For-One: 視覚的基盤モデルを高速でメモリ効率の高い視覚運動ポリシーへと蒸留する
llm.tldr_ja: 学習時にのみ視覚的基盤モデルを特権情報として活用し、その知識を軽量なRGBのみの学生ポリシーにインディストリビューションで蒸留する2段階フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚的基盤モデルはロボット操作に有用なセマンティックな手がかりを提供するが、計算コストの高さや時間的不整合性により、閉ループ制御への直接導入が困難であること。
llm.method: 教師ポリシーがRGB観測と複数のVFMの出力を統合してセマンティックに豊かな表現を学び、それを軽量な学生ポリシーへ蒸留する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび3つの実世界マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、VFMベースのエンコーダより30倍少ないパラメータと50倍低いレイテンシで従来手法を上回った。

2611.04485.tldr_en: All-For-One (AFO), a two-stage distillation framework that leverages VFMs strictly as privileged information during training, using downstream robotic data, is proposed, providing an efficient pathway for transferring foundation-model knowledge to robotic control.

2611.04477.title: Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation
2611.04477.abstract: Diffusion-based policies have achieved strong performance on single-task robotic manipulation. However, a single model trained jointly on multiple tasks consistently underperforms the per-task specialists trained on the same demonstrations. We focus on two challenges. First, the convolutional encoders commonly used in diffusion-based policies produce visual conditions that are not discriminative enough. Second, gradients from incompatible action modes update the shared denoiser's dense parameters along the same directions, causing destructive interference during joint training. To address both, we propose SR-DP (Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy). A frozen VGGT encoder with a spatial-compression adapter produces compact multi-scale semantic-geometric tokens, a task-discriminative visual condition for tasks that share a workspace. We first train the denoiser as a standard diffusion policy, then decompose selected linear layers by SVD into a frozen basis of orthogonal rank-one experts, adapted through spectral routing and Householder input rotations. On six RoboTwin tasks, SR-DP averages a 68.4% success rate, surpassing multi-task VO-DP by 21.8 points and the strongest per-task baseline by 3.8 points. On four real-world bimanual tasks, Stage 2 reaches a 43.0% average success rate and improves over Stage 1 by 19.0 points.
2611.04477.comment: 8 pages. Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)

llm.title_ja: マルチタスクロボットマニピュレーションのためのスペクトルルーティング拡散ポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: マルチタスク学習時の破壊的干渉と視覚条件の識別力不足を解決するため、特異値分解とスペクトルルーティングを用いたSR-DPを提案した。
llm.problem: 単一モデルで複数タスクを共同訓練すると、同一のデモで訓練されたタスクごとの専門モデルよりも性能が一貫して低下すること。
llm.method: 凍結されたVGGTエンコーダによるコンパクトなトークン生成と、SVDを用いた線形層の分解、およびスペクトルルーティングによる線形層の適応を行った。
llm.result: 6つのRoboTwinタスクで平均68.4%の成功率を達成し、マルチタスクVO-DPや最強の個別タスクベースラインを上回った。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション
スペクトルルーティング

2611.04477.tldr_en: SR-DP (Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy) is proposed, a frozen VGGT encoder with a spatial-compression adapter that produces compact multi-scale semantic-geometric tokens, a task-discriminative visual condition for tasks that share a workspace.

2611.04424.title: ReflexArc: Bottom-Up Integration of Instantaneous Tactile Reflexes into Whole-Body Humanoid Control
2611.04424.abstract: Humanoid robots operating in cluttered environments must react to unexpected contacts before the first impact peak, which arrives within tens of milliseconds. Learned whole-body policies running at 50 Hz introduce a policy-cycle delay and may suppress a protective withdrawal as a tracking error. To address these challenges, we propose ARC (Ascending Reflex Control), a bottom-up framework that integrates instantaneous tactile reflexes with learned whole-body control. ARC consists of two components: an instantaneous reflex pathway and bottom-up reflex integration. The reflex pathway detects hazardous contacts from full-body tactile sensing, solves a whole-body withdrawal pose, and delivers it directly to the motors within 10 ms. Bottom-up reflex integration combines reflex-in-the-loop policy learning, reflex-transparent policy alignment, and reflex-informed policy adaptation to sustain the withdrawal, maintain balance, and complete longer-horizon recovery. We deploy ARC on a Unitree G1 and evaluate three categories of hazardous contact. Compared with an otherwise identical reflex delayed by 20 ms, ARC reduces the first force peak by 34.1% and reduces the contact impulse from 0.2632 N s to 0.1225 N s (a 2.15x ratio). We further demonstrate protected motion tracking, teleoperation, and vision-free obstacle traversal guided by foot tactile sensing. Project page: https://minusmodulo.github.io/reflexarc-website/

llm.title_ja: ReflexArc: 瞬時の触覚反射の全身ヒューノイド制御へのボトムアップ統合
llm.tldr_ja: 危険な接触を検出して数ミリ秒以内にモーターへ逃避動作を伝える即時反射経路と、それを全身制御に統合するボトムアップフレームワークARCを提案した。
llm.problem: 不規則な環境で動作するヒューノイドロボットは、数十ミリ秒以内に到達する最初の衝撃のピークに対していち早く反応する必要があること。
llm.method: 全身の触覚センシングから危険な接触を検出する反射経路と、ポリシー学習・アライメント・適応を組み合わせたボトムアップ統合を実装した。
llm.result: Unitree G1での実験において、遅延のある反射と比較して最初の力ピークを34.1%削減し、接触力積を2.15分の1に減少させた。
keywords_ja: ヒューノイドロボット

2611.04424.tldr_en: This work proposes ARC (Ascending Reflex Control), a bottom-up framework that integrates instantaneous tactile reflexes with learned whole-body control and demonstrates protected motion tracking, teleoperation, and vision-free obstacle traversal guided by foot tactile sensing.

2611.04422.title: GVT3D: Gesture-Vision-Text Token Enrichment for 3D Embodied Reference Understanding
2611.04422.abstract: Natural human-robot interaction requires robots to interpret language and gestures within a 3D environment to support tasks such as pick-and-place and object retrieval. 3D Embodied Reference Understanding (3D-ERU) supports this by identifying the 3D location of a target object from a scene (point-cloud) containing a human pointing gesture and an accompanying language description. However, current 3D-ERU models lack alignment of cross-modal representations and incur high processing costs that increase with the point-cloud's size. To address this, we propose GVT3D, which employs an Embodied Fusion module that jointly models language, gesture, and vision inputs within a shared embedding space, promoting cross-modal alignment. We additionally introduce a foveation approach that selectively processes the point cloud within a coarse region around the estimated pointing direction to reduce computations. GVT3D achieves ~8% higher accuracy and foveation enables 2.95x faster execution while maintaining comparable accuracy, relative to prior 3D-ERU models.

llm.title_ja: GVT3D: 3D身体参照理解のためのジェスチャー・ビジョン・テキストトークン拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 言語、ジェスチャー、視覚入力を共有埋め込み空間内で共同モデリングする表現アライメントモジュールと、計算量を削減するフォーベーションアプローチを提案した。
llm.problem: 現在の3D身体参照理解モデルは、クロスモーダル表現のアライメントが不十分であり、点群サイズの増大に伴い処理コストが高くなること。
llm.method: ジェスチャー、ビジョン、テキスト入力を統合するEmbodied Fusionモジュールと、ポインティング方向周辺の点群を選択的に処理するフォーベーション手法を導入した。
llm.result: 既存の3D-ERUモデルと比較して約8%高い精度を達成し、フォーベーションにより2.95倍高速な実行を可能にした。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.04422.tldr_en: This work proposes GVT3D, which employs an Embodied Fusion module that jointly models language, gesture, and vision inputs within a shared embedding space, promoting cross-modal alignment, and introduces a foveation approach that selectively processes the point cloud within a coarse region around the estimated pointing direction to reduce computations.

2611.04420.title: Verifier strength does not buy discovery quality: a pre-registered two-domain test of LLM-based automated research, with post-hoc evidence pointing to proposer-pool composition
2611.04420.abstract: Automated research pipelines pair an LLM proposer with a verifier on an implicit bet: discovery quality rises with verification strength. Under a pre-registered protocol we test this bet in two real-data domains -- job-shop scheduling and vehicular edge offloading on Beijing T-Drive trajectories -- across 100 matched LLM/random pairs per domain and three verifier tiers. The manipulation binds -- a 429-case mutation battery shows scores rising across tiers -- yet the paired LLM-over-random advantage does not scale with it (A, one-sided p=0.1115; D, p=0.9994), and in D shrinks under the strict tier (margin contrast -0.040, p=0.0013). The two lower gates promote identical candidates in 100/100 and 99/100 pairs, so the strict order is untestable when they coincide. Constructively, LLM proposals carry a real paired advantage over random controls, but a post-hoc union-pool analysis shows the fastest path to better discovery is widening the pool, not tightening the gate: mixing the two pools adds +1.52 holdout-value units in domain A (one-sided Wilcoxon, n=100, p=0.0002) -- evidence that pool composition, not verification strength, is the lever. Criteria, ledgers and scripts are archived on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23308866).
2611.04420.comment: 12 pages, 1 figure. Pre-registered two-domain test (100 matched pairs/domain, 3 verifier tiers, 429-case mutation battery). Artifact archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23308866

llm.title_ja: 検証器の強さは発見品質をもたらさない：LLMベースの自動研究に関する事前登録された2ドメインテストと、提案者プールの構成を指す事後証拠
llm.tldr_ja: ジョブショップスケジューリングなどの2つのドメインにおける検証を通じて、発見品質の向上には検証の厳しさではなくプールの構成が重要であることを示した。
llm.problem: 自動研究パイプラインは検証の強さに伴って発見品質が向上するという暗黙の前提に依存していること。
llm.method: 事前登録されたプロトコルに基づき、100対のLLM/ランダムペアと3段階の検証器ティアを使用して2つの実データドメインでテストを実施した。
llm.result: 検証の厳しさとペアでのLLMの優位性は連動せず、プールの構成を広げることがより良い発見への最速の道であることを示した。

2611.04420.tldr_en: A post-hoc union-pool analysis shows the fastest path to better discovery is widening the pool, not tightening the gate: mixing the two pools adds +1.52 holdout-value units in domain A -- evidence that pool composition, not verification strength, is the lever.

2611.04393.title: Voluntary Servitude: Weaponized Safety Warning Mechanisms for Controlling AI Agents
2611.04393.abstract: LLM agents increasingly act on information retrieved from public sources they treat as credible, which turns a manipulated recommendation into a transaction, a dependency, or a decision with physical consequences. The security literature models this threat as instruction injection, in which an adversary writes a command into retrieved content and deployed defenses learn to recognize command syntax. We show that an attacker can instead steer an agent through the agent's own harm-avoidance. A single fabricated hazard, written as an ordinary review, leads the agent to disqualify the legitimate options and select the attacker's target by its own reasoning, with no command for a detector to recognize. We call this voluntary servitude. These payloads steer agents about as often as instruction injection (60.4% vs. 66.0%), and deployed injection detectors score them as benign, so behind a filter they are 1.7-4.4x more effective. We measure this at the generation stage across six models and ten consumer-service domains, for three attack families, and show that it transfers to production browser agents, outperforming instruction injection, and to a retrieval pipeline (1.0-57.0% end-to-end success, depending on the retriever). We then show that a corroboration requirement added to the agent's instructions removes roughly 95% of the exposure against a non-adaptive attacker without retraining. With the requirement in place, the agent still reads the planted hazard and no longer acts on it.
2611.04393.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Main Track). 17 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables

llm.title_ja: 自発的隷属：AIエージェントを制御するための武器化された安全性警告メカニズム
llm.tldr_ja: 攻撃者が命令の構文を用いるのではなく、エージェント自身の害回避メカニズムを利用して偽のハザードによってエージェントを誘導できることを示した。
llm.problem: LLMエージェントが信頼できるとみなして取得した情報に基づいて行動するため、巧妙な推奨が物理的影響を伴う決定につながること。
llm.method: 通常のレビューとして記述された単一の作られたハザードを用いて、6つのモデルと10の消費者向けサービスドメインで生成ステージを測定した。
llm.result: この手法は命令インジェクションと同等の頻度でエージェントを誘導し、フィルターの背後では1.7〜4.4倍効果的であることを示した。
keywords_ja: プロンプトインジェクション

2611.04393.tldr_en: A corroboration requirement added to the agent's instructions removes roughly 95% of the exposure against a non-adaptive attacker without retraining, and is measured at the generation stage across six models and ten consumer-service domains.

2611.04392.title: Aero-VPA: Few-Step Flow-Matching Control over Non-Reconstructive JEPA Latents for Agile Flight on Edge Hardware
2611.04392.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generalize across tasks, but their autoregressive decoders need sequential forward passes in proportion to the action horizon, each bounded below on embedded aerial platforms by streaming billions of parameters from memory. We present Aero-VPA, a lightweight Vision-Predictor-Action architecture for 3D navigation on edge hardware. A compact RGB-D Vision Transformer and a five-head ensemble predictor, trained without pixel reconstruction, forecast the next latent state; a Conditional Flow Matching solver generates a velocity and yaw-rate chunk in two Euler steps, so each decision takes five sequential network evaluations; and the ensemble dispersion drives an uncertainty fallback. Version 1 specified the architecture, deployment and protocol without results. This version reports the first closed-loop evaluation: PX4 software-in-the-loop simulation of quadrotor missions in procedurally generated forests. Behaviour cloning failed on all 60 missions despite open-loop errors of 0.02-0.04 m/s: the policy copies its last command, a copycat form of causal confusion. DAgger with a privileged, safety-gated supervisor gave the first successes but plateaued at 11.1-21.1% across six checkpoints. A map-free runtime shield with a 15 s depth memory, barrier constraints, a cap on motion outside the 73-degree field of view and backoff along the flown path raised the first DAgger policy's success on 180 paired missions from 21.1% to 52.2% (95% CI [45.0, 59.4]; exact McNemar p = 1.2 x 10^-10) and cut its crashes from 72.2% to 22.2%, while timeouts rose from 2.8% to 23.3%. All six checkpoints gained 30.0-34.4 percentage points, at mean speeds of 1.16-1.36 m/s. The code (https://github.com/ylee-sling/Aero-VPA), the trained policy (72.6 MB, https://huggingface.co/ylee-sling/aero-vpa) and the full benchmark dataset are public.
2611.04392.comment: 38 pages, 3 figures, 22 tables. Simulation study (PX4 SITL + Gazebo Harmonic). Version 2 of a preprint first posted on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23633375). Code: https://github.com/ylee-sling/Aero-VPA ; trained policy: https://huggingface.co/ylee-sling/aero-vpa ; benchmark dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ylee-sling/aero-vpa-benchmark

2611.04391.title: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Bridging Representation and Action Space in VLAs
2611.04391.abstract: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies provide a strong starting point for deployment, but adapting them to a target robot and environment still requires costly embodiment-specific demonstrations. Human demonstrations are far easier to collect, yet directly leveraging them is challenging due to the substantial human-robot embodiment gap, particularly when the underlying VLA has been pretrained primarily on robot data. We introduce H2RB (Human-To-Robot Bridge), a human-robot co-training framework for adapting pretrained VLA policies from unpaired human and robot demonstrations. H2RB bridges the embodiment gap at both interfaces: geometry-anchored alignment grounds human and robot observations in a compatible representation, while a decoupled-decoder tokenizer shares action latents without forcing both domains through a single action mapping. This design allows human demonstrations to provide useful behavioral supervision while retaining the rich visual, semantic, and control priors of the pretrained VLA. Across real-world tasks, H2RB substantially improves object transfer performance from 8.0 to 51.8 and enables skill transfer to score 62.7, in settings where co-train baselines totally fail to transfer human-demonstrated skills. The benefit also persists under object-placement shifts, improving out-of-distribution transfer from 6.0 to 45.3. H2RB suggests a way for human demonstrations to serve as a scalable supervision source for adapting pretrained robotic policies, reducing the dependence on costly target-robot data collection.
2611.04391.comment: Accepted for Oral Presentation at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Scaling H2R. Project page: https://junhyeong-park.me/h2rb/

llm.title_ja: VLAにおける表現空間と行動空間の架け橋を介した人間からロボットへの知識移転
llm.tldr_ja: ペアになっていない人間とロボットのデモから事前学習済みVLAポリシーを適応させるための人間-ロボット共同訓練フレームワークH2RBを提案した。

llm.method: 幾何学的に固定されたアライメントにより観察を共通表現で接地し、切り離されたデコーダトークナイザーによってアクション潜在を共有する。

2611.04391.tldr_en: H2RB (Human-To-Robot Bridge), a human-robot co-training framework for adapting pretrained VLA policies from unpaired human and robot demonstrations, suggests a way for human demonstrations to serve as a scalable supervision source for adapting pretrained robotic policies, reducing the dependence on costly target-robot data collection.
2611.04391.hf_summary_en: H2RB adapts pretrained vision-language-action policies to new robots using unpaired human demonstrations via geometry-anchored alignment and a decoupled-decoder tokenizer, substantially improving cross-embodiment skill transfer.

2611.04379.title: Understanding Backdoor Attacks in Scene Graph Generation via Global Context Pathway
2611.04379.abstract: Scene Graph Generation (SGG) produces structured scene representations, yet its training-time backdoor risk remains unexplored. Unlike classification, SGG exposes a pair-level attack surface that enables selective corruption of relations involving a designated object category. However, because SGG largely relies on localized evidence, globally placed triggers may face difficulty in manipulating such predictions. Recent SGG architectures increasingly incorporate global context to improve scene modeling, which may in turn facilitate such attacks. In this paper, we systematically study this backdoor risk and investigate the role of the global context pathway in backdoor behavior. Concretely, we first instantiate this attack with an effective method, and propose a three-axis evaluation protocol to characterize backdoor behavior. Experiments on Visual Genome with representative open-vocabulary and closed-set SGG models demonstrate the effectiveness of the attack. Mechanistic analyses reveal that the explicit global context pathway serves as a major carrier of the backdoor effect across the evaluated SGG models. In particular, replacing the poisoned global context representation with its clean counterpart during inference sharply suppresses the attack, yielding 100% and 97% reductions in attack success for the OvSGTR family and RelationFormer, respectively. Moreover, training-time interventions in the OvSGTR family show that suppressing trigger signals in this pathway either reduces attack success or substantially degrades utility. Together, these findings suggest that explicit global context designs may pose a backdoor risk in SGG architectures.
2611.04379.comment: Accepted by the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM 2026)

llm.title_ja: 大域コンテキスト経路を通じたシーングラフ生成におけるバックドア攻撃の理解
llm.tldr_ja: シーングラフ生成におけるバックドア攻撃のリスクを体系的に調査し、明示的な大域コンテキスト経路がバックドア効果の主要な伝達経路であることを明らかにした。

keywords_ja: オープンボキャブラリー

2611.04379.tldr_en: It is suggested that explicit global context designs may pose a backdoor risk in SGG architectures by investigating the role of the global context pathway in backdoor behavior and proposing a three-axis evaluation protocol to characterize backdoor behavior.

2611.04371.title: Embodied AI for Scientific Discovery: From Physical Action to Scientific Evidence
2611.04371.abstract: Scientific experiments are increasingly selected, executed and interpreted by learned systems that act through physical interfaces. Robot learning builds physical competence, whereas AI for science chooses which experiment to run, each reporting different endpoints. This review treats their interface as one problem, embodied AI for science, where the experiment itself is partially observed: specimen state, apparatus state and measurement processes are latent, actions are costly and irreversible, and missingness depends on execution and outcome. We organize the literature by three closures operating at distinct levels: operational closure (the experiment realized is the one intended), epistemic closure (the result updates beliefs or selects subsequent experiments) and evidential closure (the record supports a claim). We analyze workflows through a record-linked evidence cycle - Record, Diagnose, Calibrate, Confirm - as analytic functions with feedback. A taxonomy crosses these closures with six delegated decisions and five embodiment classes. Our formulation separates commanded, realized and observed conditions and models diagnosis with explicit resource, risk and sample-change costs. We compare experiment-selection methods by terminal decision, review perception, protocol compilation, visuomotor policies, world models, recovery and transfer by evidence emission requirements, and compare chemistry, materials, biology, microscopy and field workflows by what their records establish. An appendix provides an evidence map of 28 workflows (26 physical, two software-boundary), characterizing validation pathways and claim confirmation requirements. We propose evaluation that separates actions, valid experiments, campaigns and confirmed claims, framing open challenges as controlled comparisons with measurable failure conditions.

llm.title_ja: 科学的発見のためのEmbodied AI：物理的アクションから科学的証拠まで
llm.tldr_ja: 物理的インターフェースを通じて科学実験を実行・解釈するシステムを「科学のためのEmbodied AI」として統合的にレビューし、文献を体系化した。

llm.method: 運用・認識・証拠の3つのクロージャーと記録・診断・較正・確認のサイクルを用いた文献の分類と分析。
llm.result: 28のワークフローのエディンスマップを提供し、オープンな課題をフレームワーク化した。

2611.04371.tldr_en: Evaluation is proposed that separates actions, valid experiments, campaigns and confirmed claims, framing open challenges as controlled comparisons with measurable failure conditions.

2611.04368.title: RAFT: Reasoning-Aligned Fine-Tuning Improves Robustness of VLA Post-Training
2611.04368.abstract: Adapting a generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a target task with limited demonstrations can improve nominal task success while reducing robustness to variations in appearance, objects, and instructions. We introduce reasoning-aligned fine-tuning (RAFT), a two-stage post-training procedure: RAFT first trains low-rank adapters on task-relevant reasoning annotations, then freezes them while fine-tuning the policy on action demonstrations. On a physical DROID robot, RAFT achieves $75.0\%$ out-of-distribution success, compared with $27.9\%$ for plain fine-tuning; on a multi-stage bimanual YAM task, it reaches $70.0\%$ mean success, compared with $36.0\%$ for the strongest baseline. RAFT also improves success under visual, object, and instruction shifts in simulated pick-and-place and open-drawer tasks. Compared with plain fine-tuning, RAFT policies place more attention on annotated task regions and yield higher linear-probe accuracy for object identity in later layers. A broader reasoning-data mixture further improves downstream success across demonstration budgets.

llm.title_ja: RAFT：推論アラインメントファインチューニングによるVLAポストトレーニングの頑健性向上
llm.tldr_ja: 限定的なデモンストレーションでVLAポリシーを適応させる際に、推論アラインメントを用いた2段階のポストトレーニングにより頑健性を大幅に向上させた。

2611.04352.title: ReSMap: Recasting Satellite Priors for Robust and Accurate Online HD Map Construction
2611.04352.abstract: Despite recent advances in camera-based online HD map construction, these systems remain susceptible to sensor failures due to their reliance on onboard cameras. In contrast, satellite images remain available independently of real-time sensing conditions as they are cached offline. Existing methods utilizing satellite images, however, primarily leverage them under nominal conditions, without explicitly addressing them as redundancy when a sensor degrades. To address this gap, we propose ReSMap, a redundancy-aware camera-satellite fusion framework for robust online HD map construction. Our framework explicitly leverages satellite images as a complementary source to improve robustness against camera failures. A Predict-then-Fuse (PTF) module fuses camera and satellite BEV features by using each branch's own prediction confidence as a per-pixel reliability weight, with no learned router. An Object-Centric Cooperative Multi-modal Query (OCMQ) decoder then extends this per-modality separation to the query level: each modality cross-attends only to its own BEV, and per-modality updates are merged through a learned per-token gate. Our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on nuScenes across all splits and range settings. More importantly, it also sets the new state-of-the-art under camera-failure scenarios, demonstrating that satellite images serve not only as a strong prior but as practical redundancy for robust online HD mapping.
2611.04352.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. 24 pages, 9 figures, 11 tables. Project page: https://dehsurc.github.io/resmap-page/ Code: https://github.com/dehsurc/ReSMap

2611.04334.title: RAIPAL: A Powerful and Agile Humanoid Arm for Human Tasks
2611.04334.abstract: This paper presents humanoid manipulator hardware designed specifically for human-level performance throughout its broad domain of tasks, from heavy payloads to highly dynamic motions. Unlike conventional designs targeting uniform workspace capability, the proposed approach derives force, speed, and endurance targets from published measurements of task-relevant human upper-limb performance. These targets guide the actuator, mechanism, and thermal design toward torque transparency and sustained operation. The platform integrates force-oriented upper-arm components, speed-oriented forearm components, and a posture-dependent elbow mechanism that shifts its torque-speed behavior. These components are driven by planetary actuators and compact actuator-embedded electronics. Experimental results validate broad task capability, demonstrating a peak payload of 20 kg (2.25x its own mass), an endpoint speed of 20.6 m/s, and continued operation under repeated hammering impacts. Thermal analysis further confirms that the robot's sustained operation capability exceeds the published human load--duration boundary across nearly the entire load spectrum. These findings show that hardware targets derived from human-task measurements narrow the human-to-humanoid capability gap. A supplementary video is available at https://youtu.be/xVUWFICD5G0
2611.04334.comment: Published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), 2026. Supplementary video: https://youtu.be/xVUWFICD5G0

2611.04325.title: Computing Invariant Reachable Sets through Sum-of-Squares Programming
2611.04325.abstract: Funnels, time-varying invariant sets around nominal trajectories, certify that a closed-loop system tracks its plan, and can be composed into verified motion plans. Their computation by sum-of-squares (SOS) programming is well established in formulation but not in practice: the result depends on implementation choices such as the initial guess, Lyapunov function normalization, and termination rule, which the literature documents only briefly. This paper presents a self-contained treatment of SOS-based funnel computation, implemented in the open-source package computeSOSFunnels. We propose a minimum-volume formulation with inlet and outlet constraints under which funnels with coinciding nominal endpoints compose by construction. Numerical experiments on a unicycle, with timing studies on a cart-pole and a 12-state quadrotor, characterize the pipeline: infeasible initial guesses are partly decidable before solving, the certificate shows no violations among 39,000 boundary samples per funnel under the true dynamics, and constructing the semidefinite program, not solving it, dominates computation time.
2611.04325.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology. Code: github.com/khalid2696/computeSOSFunnels

2611.04315.title: Drift No More: Spectral Locking for Long-Horizon Open-Weight Multi-Agent AI
2611.04315.abstract: Long-horizon multi-agent systems suffer from three tightly coupled failures: task drift, role drift, and state staleness. We test the hypothesis that these share a common representational cause: agent hidden states move away from the directions encoding the active task, assigned role, and current shared state. A pilot study over 14,832 annotated turns supports this: drifted turns collapse near-uniformly across all three anchor subspaces (pairwise r = 0.72-0.78). Existing methods address these failures separately, operating at the surface-text level or treating control directions independently. We introduce ATLAS (Algebraic Task-role Locking with Adaptive Spectral Memory), a training-free intervention acting on hidden states before a token is generated. ATLAS builds a positive-semidefinite anchor kernel over task, role, and state subspaces and steers hidden states toward their shared high-coherence eigendirections; a low-rank Gram decomposition keeps this tractable. Across long-horizon memory, state maintenance, tool use, least-privilege coordination, and embodied stress tests, ATLAS outperforms prompting, retrieval, memory, and activation-steering baselines. Against A-MEM it improves memory macro-average accuracy by up to 5.7 points and reduces write/read failures by up to 31.7%/24.8%; against MemoryArena-Agent it gains up to 4.8 points. It gains 10.7-12.1 points under perturbation, reaches 93.5% role consistency, and transfers to a 72B backbone (macro-average 61.0 vs. 56.2). Ablating the joint task-role-state span costs 7.2 points against 0.8 for a matched-rank random span, indicating these directions are functionally implicated, not incidental; supplying them by prompt or retrieval recovers 4.3 points less. ATLAS is therefore a representation-level controller for open-weight multi-agent systems, complementary to output-level protocols for black-box agents.
2611.04315.comment: Accepted at the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2026)

2611.04289.title: When Debate Amplifies Risk: Social-Bias Vulnerabilities in Multi-Agent Safety Deliberation
2611.04289.abstract: Retrieval-augmented Web applications increasingly employ multi-agent debate (MAD) to aggregate conflicting, noisy, and heterogeneous information, yet deliberation is fundamentally a social process susceptible to interpersonal dynamics. When retrieved Web sources contain latent hazards alongside safe factual content, social biases such as conformity pressure and authority deference can override evidence-grounded safety boundaries. In this work, we investigate whether the social structure of deliberation can paradoxically amplify latent Web safety risks. We introduce SafeConflict-Bias, a controlled counterfactual diagnostic protocol spanning six core Web risk categories, which holds queries and retrieved evidence strictly invariant while isolating conversational majority sway, authority cues, and confidence asymmetry. Empirical evaluation across diverse proprietary and open-source backbones reveals that while isolated models reliably reject unsafe guidance, standard MAD catastrophically capitulates to social pressure---surging unsafe adoption from 0.0\% up to 100.0\% and systematically silencing safe minority evidence. To resolve this systemic fragility without retraining or debate regeneration, we propose RiskTrace-Debias, an inference-time auditing framework uniting evidence-first precommitment, social-metadata masking, and consistency-gated arbitration. RiskTrace-Debias suppresses worst-case unsafe adoption to $\le 2.0\%$ across all architectures without inducing over-refusal, while generating verifiable provenance traces to audit interpersonal manipulation in Web deliberation.

llm.title_ja: 議論がリスクを増幅するとき：マルチエージェント安全審議における社会的バイアスの脆弱性
llm.tldr_ja: マルチエージェント議論において同調圧力などの社会的バイアスが安全境界を無効化し、安全でない決定を増幅させる現象を実証し、その監査・是正フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: マルチエージェント議論は同調圧力や権威への迎合といった社会的バイアスにより、安全リスクをかえって増幅させる可能性がある。
llm.method: 会話の過半数の影響や権威の手がかりを隔離する診断プロトコルSafeConflict-Biasと、推論時監査フレームワークRiskTrace-Debiasの提案。
llm.result: 標準的な議論手法では安全でない選択が最大100%に達するのに対し、提案手法により最悪の場合でも2.0%以下に抑制できた。

2611.04289.tldr_en: SafeConflict-Bias is introduced, a controlled counterfactual diagnostic protocol spanning six core Web risk categories, which holds queries and retrieved evidence strictly invariant while isolating conversational majority sway, authority cues, and confidence asymmetry and RiskTrace-Debias, an inference-time auditing framework uniting evidence-first precommitment, social-metadata masking, and consistency-gated arbitration.

2611.04255.title: ActOR: Ambient AI-Based Agentic Orchestration for Humanoid Autonomy in Operating Rooms
2611.04255.abstract: Operating rooms (ORs) increasingly contain ambient sensing infrastructure to enable AI-based optimization of workflows and utilization. We pursue an alternative path: using ambient AI to guide robot action and optimize utilization. Deploying humanoids in the OR without ambient AI is severely limited by cumbersome de novo orientation and planning due to partial onboard observations. We posit that this can be achieved by coupling an ambient AI-based agentic orchestrator with the humanoid robotic actor, providing shared perception and execution feedback for humanoid autonomy in the OR. ActOR fuses a wall-mounted ambient camera and the robot's head-mounted camera into a shared object-level digital twin (DT). A large language model agent plans over the DT using pre-programmed locomotion and manipulation skills without task-specific training. During execution, DT updates and execution outcomes inform retries, alternative approaches, or replanning. We evaluated ActOR in simulated and physical environments. Across three tasks in two simulated ORs reconstructed from real rooms, ambient perception reduced exploration from 1.05 to 0.12 Explore calls per trial when targets were initially outside the robot's view. Closed-loop feedback increased success from 46.7% to 83.3% under nominal execution and from 8.3% to 51.7% under injected navigation, object-relocation, and grasp perturbations. In a physical mock OR with a humanoid, ActOR completed 14 of 20 single-object disposal trials and demonstrated replanning after scene changes. Ambient AI-based observations provide scene state that improves robot action planning, increasing success and reducing exploration compared with robot-only observations. Feeding skill outcomes and DT updates back to the planner improves multi-step task success. Our results show the feasibility of humanoid task autonomy for multi-step disposal tasks in a mock OR.

llm.title_ja: ActOR：手術室におけるヒューマノイド自律性のための環境AIベースのエージェント型オーケストレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 手術室内の環境カメラとヒューマノイドのカメラを統合したデジタルツインを活用し、LLMエージェントによるロボットのタスク計画と再計画を実現した。
llm.problem: 限られた車載観測のみによる手術室でのヒューマノイド展開は、不十分な姿勢推定や計画により著しく制限される。
llm.method: 壁面カメラとヘッドマウントカメラをオブジェクトレベルのデジタルツインに統合し、LLMエージェントが事前プログラムされたスキルを計画するActORの提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機の模擬手術室において、探索を削減し閉ループフィードバックによりタスク成功率を大幅に向上させた。

2611.04255.tldr_en: Ambient AI-based observations provide scene state that improves robot action planning, increasing success and reducing exploration compared with robot-only observations, and shows the feasibility of humanoid task autonomy for multi-step disposal tasks in a mock OR.

2611.04241.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds
2611.04241.abstract: Video games provide a practical setting for collecting vision-language-action (VLA) data, whose acquisition in physical environments is costly. Existing datasets, however, remain limited by restricted game coverage, sparse language supervision, or temporal hierarchies that do not necessarily reflect changes in task objectives. We introduce AceAction, a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games for learning skill composition and subgoal transitions. AceAction organizes demonstrations around complete tasks, linking overall instructions, ordered subgoals, and local skill instructions to temporally aligned visual observations and keyboard-and-mouse actions. To construct these annotations, we develop a vision-language model pipeline that identifies subgoals from changes in objectives or interaction targets, anchors navigation goals to visually recognizable waypoints, and composes adjacent subgoals into task instructions. The resulting demonstrations cover navigation, reconnaissance, combat, interaction, and recovery, with explicit stage boundaries that connect task progression to fine-grained control. We assess annotation quality through model-based verification and human inspection. An audit of 500 trajectories yields a 95.8% pass rate across independent reviewer assessments. AceAction provides a data foundation for studying how agents execute, combine, and switch skills to follow complex instructions in dynamic game environments.

llm.title_ja: AceAction-5M：3Dゲーム世界における汎用アクション学習のための階層的目標
llm.tldr_ja: 3Dゲーム世界の人間プレイからスキル構成やサブゴール遷移を学習するための、階層的な指示と視覚的観測を含む大規模データセットAceActionを構築した。
llm.problem: 物理環境でのVLAデータの収集はコストが高く、既存のゲームデータセットはカバレッジや言語指導、時間的階層が限られている。
llm.method: 全体的な指示、順序付けられたサブゴール、ローカルなスキル指示を視覚的観測やキーボード・マウス操作に結び付けるVLMパイプラインの開発。
llm.result: 500の軌跡の監査で95.8%の合格率を達成し、複雑な指示に従うためのデータ基盤を提供した。

2611.04241.tldr_en: This work introduces AceAction, a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games for learning skill composition and subgoal transitions, and develops a vision-language model pipeline that identifies subgoals from changes in objectives or interaction targets, anchors navigation goals to visually recognizable waypoints, and composes adjacent subgoals into task instructions.

2611.04228.title: DualWorldBench: Can Agents Plan Deliveries across Symbolic and Grounded Worlds?
2611.04228.abstract: Recent multimodal agents have shown promising progress in embodied planning and web interaction. However, existing evaluations often rely on simplified tasks with limited combinatorial structure, leaving it unclear whether current agents can robustly integrate perception and reasoning for multi-goal planning under temporal, physical, and multimodal constraints. We introduce DualWorldBench, a unified benchmark for evaluating agent planning under controlled symbolic--temporal and grounded--topological complexity. Built around a shared pickup--delivery interface, DualWorldBench consists of three complementary components: TextWorld, which isolates symbolic planning under varying task compositions and release dynamics; SimWorld, which evaluates grounded path planning under controlled topological variation with text, image, or multimodal inputs; and DualWorld-VQA, a diagnostic suite spanning perception, scene understanding, and planning. Experiments reveal a common gap between local understanding and globally consistent planning. In TextWorld, agents struggle to derive optimal task sequences under interacting temporal constraints; in SimWorld, grounded observations are not reliably converted into feasible action sequences. DualWorld-VQA further confirms that perception and topology understanding do not necessarily translate into constrained planning. Together, these results identify the central challenge as composing symbolic or grounded evidence into globally feasible and efficient multi-goal plans. These findings establish DualWorldBench as a challenging testbed for agents with tighter perception--reasoning--planning integration. All datasets and code are publicly available at our project website https://dualworld.netlify.app/.

llm.title_ja: DualWorldBench：エージェントはシンボル世界とグラウンド世界の双方で配送計画を立てられるか？
llm.tldr_ja: エージェントのマルチゴール計画能力を評価するため、シンボル・時間的複雑性とグラウンド・位相的複雑性を統合したベンチマークDualWorldBenchを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の評価は限られた組合せ構造の単純なタスクに依存しており、エージェントが知覚と推論を統合してマルチゴール計画を行えるか不明である。
llm.method: シンボル計画を分離するTextWorld、グラウンド経路計画を評価するSimWorld、知覚・推論を診断するDualWorld-VQAからなる統合ベンチマークの構築。
llm.result: ローカルな理解とグローバルに一貫した計画の間に共通のギャップがあることを明らかにし、知覚・推論・計画の統合の必要性を示した。

2611.04228.tldr_en: DualWorldBench is introduced, a unified benchmark for evaluating agent planning under controlled symbolic--temporal and grounded--topological complexity and is established as a challenging testbed for agents with tighter perception--reasoning--planning integration.

2611.04226.title: DiMuRe: Diagnosis-Guided Multilevel Recovery for Robotic Task Execution
2611.04226.abstract: Disturbances can invalidate the conditions required by a robot's next action even when much of its task program remains useful. A recovery system must therefore choose a response suited to the current state. We present DiMuRe (diagnosis-guided multilevel recovery), a framework for robot-use agents that uses phase-specific evidence and method preconditions to select program reuse or predefined recovery skills, including bounded vision-language-action (VLA) grasping. After the original program exits, a multimodal large language model (MLLM) can generate corrective code from images and execution feedback. Local verification checks the outcome of each recovery attempt. We also introduce LIBERO-Disturb, a benchmark for robustness and recovery under mid-execution disturbances, supporting program-based agents and VLA policies. On 801 scheduled disturbed Encore development cases, Local DiMuRe (program reuse and recovery skills) achieves 77.65% complete-task success, compared with 58.68% for the original program under the same physical-step allowance. Full DiMuRe achieves 81.90% with terminal replanning, an additional step allowance, and early handoff. Local DiMuRe also uses fewer physical steps per scheduled episode than the original program.

llm.title_ja: DiMuRe：ロボットのタスク実行に向けた診断ガイド付きマルチレベルリカバリ
llm.tldr_ja: タスク中の外乱に対して、フェーズ固有の証拠やプログラムの再利用、事前定義されたリカバリスキルを選択して柔軟に対応するフレームワークDiMuReを提案した。
llm.problem: 外乱が発生すると、タスクプログラムの大半が有用であっても次のアクションの前提条件が満たされなくなる。
llm.method: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデルを活用して画像や実行フィードバックから修正コードを生成し、局所検証を行うDiMuReフレームワークとベンチマークの導入。
llm.result: スケジュールの乱れた開発ケースにおいて、ローカルDiMuReによりタスク成功率が元のプログラムの58.68%から77.65%に向上した。
keywords_ja: ロボットエージェント

2611.04226.tldr_en: DiMuRe (diagnosis-guided multilevel recovery), a framework for robot-use agents that uses phase-specific evidence and method preconditions to select program reuse or predefined recovery skills, including bounded vision-language-action (VLA) grasping, is presented.

2611.04221.title: Mamba3R: Fixed-Capacity Selective State Memory for Long-Sequence 3D Reconstruction
2611.04221.abstract: Streaming 3D reconstruction must maintain geometric quality over long inputs within a fixed GPU budget. A pretrained recurrent model provides bounded state, but freezing its backbone also fixes its learned state-observation interactions. We introduce Mamba3R, a jointly designed state-memory adapter that provides a trainable adaptation path without updating the backbone or task heads. A selective state-space mixer jointly transforms native state features and a fixed-capacity auxiliary memory, explicit read and write paths carry information across frames, and a decomposed feedback path regulates what the added memory feeds back. Only 1.28 million adapter parameters are trained. Under a shared periodic-reset protocol, it lowers trajectory error and improves accumulated surface and depth accuracy over recurrent baselines on public indoor and outdoor datasets and robot-recorded traversals, gaining up to 40 percent on one metric. Matched comparisons support both the choice of the mixing operator and the utility of carrying the auxiliary memory across frames. Allocated memory remains unchanged and throughput moves by at most 1.4 percent from one to two thousand frames. Replaying its recorded traversals offline, the platform's RTX 4060 averages 11.7 frames per second within 5.1 GiB with the same checkpoint, a mean throughput covering the 10 Hz sensor rate.
2611.04221.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 8 tables. The supplementary material referenced in the text is not included in this version

llm.title_ja: Mamba3R：長期シーケンス3D再構築のための固定容量選択的状態メモリ
llm.tldr_ja: 限られたGPU予算で長期入力の幾何学的品質を維持するため、バックボーンを更新せずに訓練可能な適応パスを提供する状態メモリアダプターMamba3Rを提案した。
llm.problem: ストリーミング3D再構築では、固定GPUバジェット内で長期入力にわたる幾何学的品質を維持する必要がある。
llm.method: ネイティブ状態特徴と固定容量の補助メモリを変換する選択的状態空間ミキサーと、明示的な読み書きパスを持つMamba3Rアダプターの導入。
llm.result: 公開されている屋内・屋外データセットやロボット記録において、再構築ベースラインに比べて軌跡誤差を減らし表面・深度精度を向上させた。

2611.04221.tldr_en: Mamba3R is introduced, a jointly designed state-memory adapter that provides a trainable adaptation path without updating the backbone or task heads, and improves accumulated surface and depth accuracy over recurrent baselines on public indoor and outdoor datasets and robot-recorded traversals.

2611.04204.title: Online iLQR-MPC with Whole-Body Control for Robust Humanoid Locomotion
2611.04204.abstract: Humanoid locomotion requires deciding where to step and how to distribute contact forces. However, a disturbance can invalidate the nominal plan, requiring coordinated revision under constraints that switch with every footfall. To solve this online, the proposed approach employs the single-rigid-body model, which retains attitude dynamics and the full contact wrench. An iterative linear-quadratic-regulator MPC (iLQR-MPC) then jointly optimizes contact forces and footstep locations in a single receding-horizon problem, without a separate step planner. Specifically, contact and motion constraints are incorporated into the backward pass through augmented-Lagrangian and relaxed-barrier penalties. A whole-body controller subsequently maps the plan to joint torques at 500 Hz while preserving contact feasibility. The model-based formulation makes disturbance responses interpretable through explicit costs and constraints, and requires no platform-specific policy training. In MuJoCo simulations, the iLQR-MPC replans at 100 Hz (mean solve time 8.9 ms); the Unitree G1 sustains steady-state walking and recovers from impulsive 245 N forward and 175 N lateral pushes.

llm.title_ja: 頑健なヒューマノイド歩行のための全身制御を伴うオンラインiLQR-MPC
llm.tldr_ja: 単一剛体モデルを用いて接触力と足踏み位置を単一の非ホライゾン問題で同時に最適化し、外乱から復帰するオンラインiLQR-MPCフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイド歩行において、外乱により公称計画が無効化された際、足が着地するたびに変化する制約下で協調的な修正が必要となる。
llm.method: 姿勢ダイナミクスと接触レンチを保持する単一剛体モデルを用いた反復LQR-MPCと、全身コントローラによる500Hzでの関節トルクマッピング。
llm.result: MuJoCoシミュレーションにおいて100Hzで再計画を行い、Unitree G1が安定した歩行を維持し強力な前方および側方の押し付けから回復することを実証した。

2611.04195.title: SettleSplat: Monocular Gaussian Mapping under In-View Scene Changes
2611.04195.abstract: Online 3D Gaussian mapping enables fast and high-fidelity novel view synthesis, with broad applications in augmented reality, robotics, and autonomous systems. However, many current methods assume static scenes or filter out dynamics as outliers. In this paper, we study in-view scene changes where objects are manipulated in front of the camera within a single online sequence, unlike prior works that detect changes outside the camera view or between separate captures. This setting entangles transient and persistent dynamics, as objects can be distractors while moving and persistent once they settle. While recent studies start to address distractors by removing them for clean static background, in-view scene changes remain underexplored. To resolve this, we present SettleSplat, a monocular mapping system that maintains up-to-date 3D Gaussian maps under such changes. Specifically, we lift coarse per-pixel uncertainty into Gaussian dynamicity field, then prune transient ones. For persistent changes, we derive geometric contradictions weighted by parameter-free rendered depth uncertainty to separate true changes from under-optimized regions. On Bonn and Co-Fusion, SettleSplat achieves consistent 3D Gaussian maps, outperforming current baselines on both full images and change regions while maintaining comparable speed.

llm.title_ja: SettleSplat：視界内シーン変化における単眼ガウス・マッピング
llm.tldr_ja: カメラの前でオブジェクトが操作される視界内のシーン変化に対応し、一時的なダイナミクスを枝刈りしつつ永続的な変更をモデル化する単眼マッピングシステムSettleSplatを提案した。
llm.problem: 多くのオンライン3Dガウス・マッピング手法は静的シーンを仮定するか、動的な要素を外れ値としてフィルタリングしているため、視界内の動的変化への対応が不十分である。
llm.method: 粗いピクセルごとの不確実性をガウス動的場に持ち上げ、パラメータフリーのレンダリング深度不確実性を用いて真の変化を分離する手法の提案。
llm.result: BonnおよびCo-Fusionデータセットにおいて、同等の速度を維持しながら既存のベースラインを上回る一貫した3Dガウス地図を実現した。
keywords_ja: 3Dガウス・スプラッティング

2611.04195.tldr_en: SettleSplat is presented, a monocular mapping system that maintains up-to-date 3D Gaussian maps under in-view scene changes where objects are manipulated in front of the camera within a single online sequence, unlike prior works that detect changes outside the camera view or between separate captures.

2611.04176.title: Grasping and Stabilizing Tumbling Objects with Rotating-Base Multi-Arm Space Manipulators
2611.04176.abstract: This paper presents an innovative guidance and control method for a space manipulator that actively maneuvers its base to hold a tumbling object stationary relative to the base during proximity operations. This simplifies motion planning, reduces collision risk, and enables impact-free capture using single- or multi-arm configurations, with or without predefined grasping interfaces. The proposed approach involves two phases. In the pre-grasping phase, a synchronization control aligns the target's center of mass (CoM) with the system's instantaneous center of rotation (ICR), virtually rigidizing the target-servicer system to keep the object stationary for reliable grasping. In the post grasping phase, a control strategy based on Hamiltonian dynamics and optimal control stabilizes the combined system by minimizing time, fuel, or energy, while respecting base torque limits and multiple grasping constraints. For structured targets, applied forces and torques stay within their bounds; for unstructured ones, friction constraints prevent slipping. A case study demonstrates the method's effectiveness in enabling both the subsequent grasping and detumbling phases.

llm.title_ja: 回転ベースを持つ多腕宇宙マニピュレータによるタンブリング物体の把持と安定化
llm.tldr_ja: 近接作戦時にタンブリング（回転）している物体をベースに対して静止させるための、宇宙マニピュレータ向け新規誘導・制御手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 宇宙空間でのタンブリング物体の捕獲において、動的ターゲットの動きに合わせた把持や衝突リスクの回避が課題となる。
llm.method: ターゲットの重心をシステムの瞬間回転中心に合わせるプレ把持フェーズの同期制御と、ハミルトン力学に基づくポスト把持フェーズの安定化制御。
llm.result: ケーススタディを通じて、その後の把持およびデタムブリング（回転停止）フェーズを有効に実現できることを実証した。

2611.04166.title: Say the Same, Act Differently: Diagnosing and Steering Text-Action Divergence in Reasoning VLAs
2611.04166.abstract: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) models pair physical control with natural-language rationales that supervisors can read to monitor embodied safety. Prior attacks on VLA reasoning corrupt the rationale itself and leave visible evidence in the text. We show that visual perturbations can instead alter the physical action while keeping the generated rationale word-for-word identical. At the shared text/action interface of Alpamayo for driving and InstructVLA for manipulation, our text-neutral action-subspace (TNAS) diagnostic shows that the locally most action-sensitive direction is nearly orthogonal to the active text-loss gradients, with 1.87% and 5.28% norm overlap. At equal hidden-state perturbation norms across both models, interventions along this text-neutral residual shift actions 4.64x to 47.8x more than text-gradient perturbations, whereas text-gradient perturbations induce 21.2x to 277x more text drift. Steering visual perturbations along this direction reaches the same decoupling from the image. Across 154 obstacle-annotated driving scenes in Alpamayo, TNAS-guided attacks induce a new collision under a word-for-word identical rationale in 52.6% of scenes under full-image perturbations and 35.1% under a localized forward-camera patch, compared with 4.55% for unguided action attacks. Relative to a text-preserving baseline, TNAS guidance raises exact rationale preservation from 83.0% to 89.5% and cuts teacher-forced text drift by 68.4% at a comparable collision rate. In InstructVLA, TNAS guidance cuts text drift by 40.5% and preserves the exact response on 85.0% of examples alongside a 1.73-unit action-chunk shift. An unchanged rationale therefore cannot certify a safe action, so monitors for reasoning VLAs must verify the predicted action channel directly.
2611.04166.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. 23 pages, 3 figures, 8 tables

llm.title_ja: 同じことを言い、異なる行動をとる：推論VLAにおけるテキスト・行動乖離の診断とステアリング
llm.tldr_ja: 推論VLAモデルにおいて、生成される自然言語の理由は完全に同一のまま、視覚的外乱により物理的な行動のみが変化させられる脆弱性を実証した。
llm.problem: 推論VLAモデルの自然言語の理由は読み取り可能であるが、理由を改変せずに物理的行動だけを不正に変化させる攻撃ベクトルが未解明であった。
llm.method: テキストに依存しない行動部分空間（TNAS）を診断し、アクションに敏感な方向へ視覚的外乱をステアリングする手法の提案。
llm.result: AlpamayoおよびInstructVLAにおいて、同一のテキスト理由を維持したまま衝突を引き起こす行動の変化を誘発できることを示した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルモデル

2611.04166.tldr_en: This work shows that visual perturbations can instead alter the physical action while keeping the generated rationale word-for-word identical, in a text-neutral action-subspace of Alpamayo and InstructVLA.
2611.04166.hf_summary_en: Visual perturbations can alter physical actions in vision-language-action models while leaving rationales unchanged, demonstrating that unchanged reasoning does not guarantee safe actions.

2611.04106.title: Structure, Dimensionality, and Distribution Shape - What Makes Pretraining Data Transferable, and Why the Input Pipeline Decides Which
2611.04106.abstract: What makes a pretraining corpus transferable? We describe a corpus by three properties: its structure, its dimensionality, and the distribution shape of each unit's values. We propose the Transfer-Invariance Principle: the same property can be irrelevant to transfer under one input transform and decisive under another, so the model's input transform, not the data modality, decides which properties can matter. To test it we build TransferForge, a generator that places a synthetic population at any prescribed structure, dimensionality, and distribution shape. KernelSynth, the synthetic prior of Chronos, cannot, because it draws independent series. When the model standardizes each input window (PatchTST on UCR), the distribution shape is inert and the structural setting governs. Synthetic pretraining then matches a real corpus of the same size and exceeds it once scaled. When the model encodes calcium fluorescence signals without normalization (POYO Plus), the shape becomes a governing constraint, and a shape-matched synthetic corpus replaces real pretraining with zero real neural activity. Flipping only the input normalization, with the model and data fixed, changes the effect of a shape manipulation by a factor of 5.3, so the pipeline, not the modality, sets the switch. The principle yields a recipe that chooses what to synthesize before any training. Pretraining data then becomes something to manufacture for the model, most valuably where real data is scarce, expensive, or private.

llm.title_ja: 構造、次元数、分布の形状―事前学習データの転移可能性を決定づけるもの、そして入力パイプラインがそれを決める理由
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習データの転移可能性を左右する要素を構造、次元数、分布形状の観点から分析し、データのモダリティではなく入力変換処理が重要であることを示した。
llm.problem: どのような事前学習コーパスが優れた転移性能を持つのか、またその決定要因が何であるのか十分に理解されていない。
llm.method: 所定の構造・次元・分布形状を持つ合成データを生成するTransferForgeを用いた検証と、転移不変性原理の提案。
llm.result: 入力正規化の変更のみで形状操作の効果が5.3倍変わり、モデルの入力パイプラインが事前学習データの転移性を決定することを実証した。

2611.04106.tldr_en: The Transfer-Invariance Principle is proposed: the same property can be irrelevant to transfer under one input transform and decisive under another, so the model's input transform, not the data modality, decides which properties can matter.

2611.04096.title: Online Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability Onboard the Robot Control Loop: A Real-Time GPU Solver for Safety-Critical Autonomy
2611.04096.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides certified backward reachable tubes (BRTs) for safety-critical robotic systems, but the level-set computation scales exponentially in the state dimension and has historically been performed offline. As autonomy stacks (ADAS/AV, humanoid robotics, and vision-language-action models) increasingly rely on black-box, probabilistic policies, a deterministic safety layer with formal guarantees is an essential complement. We present a CUDA implementation of the canonical WENO5 + TVD-RK3 + Lax-Friedrichs level-set Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs solver for 2D, 3D, and 4D dynamics that is fast enough to run inside a robot's control loop. In 32-bit floating point (FP32) on a single workstation GPU (NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada), it computes the 3D Air3D BRT at 112 Hz, a 4D pursuit-evasion BRT at 61 Hz, and a 2D wind-affected drifter BRT at 74-147 Hz, 5.9-17.5x faster than the JAX reference hj_reachability at matched precision and 1.7-16x faster than a torch.compile reimplementation of the same scheme. In 64-bit floating point (FP64) it agrees with hj_reachability on eight benchmark cases, reproduces Mitchell's Air3D BRT to within 0.04% of the reference cell count, and runs 2.0-4.6x faster. On an embedded NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor it computes Air3D at 66 Hz (N=41) and the 2D drifter at 54 Hz, 3.8-8.9x faster than hj_reachability on the same device. As a multi-agent application, an in-kernel label-propagation extension recovers the K-agent capture-basin Voronoi tessellation from a single combined HJ solve, independent of fleet size; it runs at 4.0 ms per tick in a closed-loop wildfire-response simulation of six quadcopters under time-varying, non-uniform wind.

llm.title_ja: ロボット制御ループ上のオンラインハミルトニアン・ジャコビ可到達性：安全確保のためのリアルタイムGPUソルバー
llm.tldr_ja: 安全性が極めて重要なロボットシステム向けに、制御ループ内で実行可能な高速CUDAベースのハミルトニアン・ジャコビ・アイザックスソルバーを開発した。
llm.problem: ハミルトニアン・ジャコビ可到達性は状態次元に対して指数関数的に計算量が増大するため、従来はオフラインでの実行に限定されていた。
llm.method: WENO5 + TVD-RK3 + Lax-Friedrichsスキームを用いた2D、3D、4Dダイナミクス向けCUDAレベルセットソルバーのCUDA実装。
llm.result: RTX 4000 Ada上でAir3Dを112Hzで計算し、既存のリファレンス実装と比較して数倍〜十数倍高速に動作することを実証した。

2611.04096.tldr_en: This work presents a CUDA implementation of the canonical WENO5 + TVD-RK3 + Lax-Friedrichs level-set Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs solver for 2D, 3D, and 4D dynamics that is fast enough to run inside a robot's control loop.

2611.04093.title: VARP: A Visual Adaptive Rearrangement Planner for Non-Monotone Object Rearrangement Planning
2611.04093.abstract: Object rearrangement planning in cluttered environments is often non-monotone, requiring objects to be temporarily relocated before reaching their final destinations. Although search-based planners can solve such tasks, they incur substantial computational cost and require expensive replanning when the environment changes. We propose the Visual Adaptive Rearrangement Planner (VARP), which learns non-monotone rearrangement directly from visual state representations generated from expert demonstrations. VARP predicts pick-and-place actions from the current and goal visual state representations, and incorporates an Action Refinement Strategy (ARS) to improve action feasibility and a Progress Enforcement Strategy (PES) to mitigate progress stagnation. By continuously updating actions from the latest visual state representations, VARP adapts online to disturbances without replanning from scratch or performing online combinatorial search. In challenging rearrangement benchmarks, VARP achieves a 98.3\% success rate with only 0.4 s planning time per task, 97.5\% success under execution-time disturbances, and 94.5\% under continuous severe disturbances, while generalizing effectively to unseen object counts. These results demonstrate that VARP provides a scalable and robust solution for non-monotone object rearrangement.

llm.title_ja: VARP：非単調オブジェクト再配置計画のための視覚的適応型再配置プランナー
llm.tldr_ja: 専門家のデモンストレーションに基づく視覚的状態表現から非単調なオブジェクト再配置を学習し、外乱にオンラインで適応するVARPを提案した。
llm.problem: 複雑な環境でのオブジェクト再配置は非単調であり、探索ベースのプランナーは多大な計算コストと高価な再計画を必要とする。
llm.method: 視覚状態表現からピック・アンド・プレース行動を予測し、行動洗練戦略と進捗強制戦略を組み合わせたVARPの提案。
llm.result: 再配置ベンチマークにおいてタスクあたり0.4秒の計画時間で98.3%の成功率を達成し、実行時の外乱にも効果的に適応した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.04093.tldr_en: The Visual Adaptive Rearrangement Planner (VARP), which learns non-monotone rearrangement directly from visual state representations generated from expert demonstrations, and incorporates an Action Refinement Strategy (ARS) to improve action feasibility and a Progress Enforcement Strategy (PES) to mitigate progress stagnation.

2611.04083.title: MABEL: An Open Anthropomorphic Mobile Bimanual Platform for Teleoperation and Learning
2611.04083.abstract: As robot learning moves beyond the tabletop, many tasks require mobility, adjustable reach, active perception, and bimanual dexterity. Commercial platforms combining these capabilities are costly, while affordable open-source alternatives cover only a subset and require software integration. We present MABEL, an open-source anthropomorphic mobile bimanual robot with 56 degrees of freedom (DOF) and a US$8.1k parts cost. It combines two 7-DOF arms with 17-DOF hands, a pitching torso, a lift, a 3-DOF neck, and a holonomic base. Back-drivable arms and torso support compliant interaction, with fingertip reach from floor level to 2.23 m. The head and torso roughly triple modeled camera coverage relative to a torso-fixed camera. Apple Vision Pro head and hand tracking enables whole-body teleoperation without handheld controllers, with 137 ms mean glass-to-glass stereo video latency over the robot's Wi-Fi hotspot. We demonstrate an end-to-end imitation learning pipeline, from teleoperated data collection to policy deployment, using a shared command interface and whole-body controller.
2611.04083.comment: 8 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Project page: https://robotmabel.github.io/website/

llm.title_ja: MABEL：テレオペレーションと学習のためのオープンな人間型モバイル双腕プラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: 56自由度を持ち8,100ドルの部品コストで作られたオープンソースの人間型モバイル双腕ロボット「MABEL」を提案し、エンドツーエンドの模倣学習パイプラインの実証を行う。
llm.problem: 商業用プラットフォームは高価であり、手頃なオープンソースの代替品は機能の一部しかカバーせずソフトウェアの統合が必要である。
llm.method: 56自由度、ピッチング胴体、リフト、3自由度の首、ホロノミックベースを組み合わせたオープンソースの人間型モバイル双腕ロボットを構築し、Apple Vision Proによる全身テレオペレーションを実装した。
llm.result: 137msの平均ガラス間遅延でのテレオペレーションを実現し、テレオペされたデータ収集からポリシー展開までのエンドツーエンドの模倣学習パイプラインを実証した。

2611.04083.tldr_en: This work presents MABEL, an open-source anthropomorphic mobile bimanual robot with 56 degrees of freedom (DOF) and a US$8.1k parts cost, and demonstrates an end-to-end imitation learning pipeline, from teleoperated data collection to policy deployment, using a shared command interface and whole-body controller.

2611.04080.title: FEIJOA: Task-Driven Grounding and Execution for Mobile Manipulation
2611.04080.abstract: A mobile manipulator asked to "put the toys away in the toy box" must decide which objects are toys and which container the user means, then find base poses, grasps, and placements it can execute. Because a scene representation is built before the instruction is known, it may lack the attributes, affordances, or concepts needed to resolve the task. We present FEIJOA, a language-model agent that grounds the instruction at test time. It queries a grounding tool over a posed RGB-D scan, inspects the returned candidates, and refines its queries until they resolve the instruction. An embodiment-aware harness checks each skill's preconditions, samples base poses from which the target is reachable, and verifies the skill's effect from observations before and after execution. On 103 open-ended grounding queries, FEIJOA resolves 94.2% exactly, compared with 68.0% for the best prebuilt representation. Over 50 real-world trials on Spot, it completes 35 tasks; 17 of these successes follow recovery from a failed tool call or verification check. Of the 15 failed trials, 13 were caused by the robot's physical skills, and only 2 by grounding or the agent's reasoning. Project website: https://williamshen-nz.github.io/feijoa/.

llm.title_ja: FEIJOA：モバイルマニプレーションのためのタスク駆動型グラウンディングと実行
llm.tldr_ja: テスト時に言語指示をグラウンディングし、スキルの前提条件の確認や把持・配置のポーズサンプリングを行う言語モデルエージェント「FEIJOA」を提案し、実世界のSpotでタスクを完了できることを示す。
llm.problem: 指示が知られる前にシーン表現が構築されるため、タスクを解決するために必要な属性やアフォーダンスが不足する場合がある。
llm.method: テスト時に指示をグラウンディングする言語モデルエージェントFEIJOAを提案し、RGB-Dスキャン上でグラウンディングツールをクエリして候補を検証・洗練させる。
llm.result: 103件のオープンエンドなグラウンディングクエリのうち94.2%を正確に解決し、Spotを用いた50件の実世界試行で35件のタスクを完了した。
llm.limitation: 失敗した15件の試行のうち13件はロボットの物理的スキルに起因し、グラウンディングや推論に起因するのは2件のみであった。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2611.04080.tldr_en: FEIJOA, a language-model agent that grounds the instruction at test time, is presented, a language-model agent that queries a grounding tool over a posed RGB-D scan, inspects the returned candidates, and refines its queries until they resolve the instruction.

2611.04027.title: A Practical Causal Framework for Autonomous Mobile Robots: From Simulation to Real-World Human Environments
2611.04027.abstract: Causal inference has emerged as a powerful paradigm enabling robots to make safe, efficient decisions by reasoning about the ``why'' behind events. However, its real-world application is hindered by the difficulty of collecting causal data, especially in human-populated environments where training takes time, while users expect immediate operation. To this end, we tackle the challenge of transferring simulation-learnt causal relations to the real world with minimal effort. While retaining the invariant high-level causal structure, we empirically demonstrate the system adapts efficiently to real-world situations by updating only the causal model parameters with a limited set of new observations. Our results show that the parameter update enables rapid sim-to-real transfer. The framework runs efficiently onboard of a mobile robot and significantly outperforms a non-causal baselines navigating successfully and safely in complex human-shared scenarios.
2611.04027.comment: Accepted in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)

llm.title_ja: 自律移動ロボットのための実用的な因果フレームワーク：シミュレーションから現実世界の人間環境へ
llm.tldr_ja: 不変の高次因果構造を維持しながら限られた新しい観測で因果モデルパラメータのみを更新することで、シミュレーションで学習した因果関係を実世界へ効率的に転移するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 因果推論の現実世界への応用は、特に訓練に時間がかかる人間のいる環境において因果データの収集が困難であることによって妨げられている。
llm.method: 高次の因果構造を維持しつつ、限られた新しい観測データを用いて因果モデルのパラメータのみを更新することで、シミュレーションで学習した関係を実世界へ適応させる。
llm.result: パラメータ更新により迅速なSim-to-Real転移が可能になり、移動ロボットのオンボードで効率的に動作し、複雑な人間共存シナリオでのナビゲーションに成功した。

2611.04027.tldr_en: This work empirically demonstrate the system adapts efficiently to real-world situations by updating only the causal model parameters with a limited set of new observations, and shows that the parameter update enables rapid sim-to-real transfer.
