2611.04016.title: Physical Experience Builds Continual Spatial World Models
2611.04016.abstract: World models are increasingly used to support prediction and planning in embodied agents, but the knowledge is usually established before deployment and then carried into later encounters. Continual operation faces a different problem. A familiar environment may change, and the agent must use previous experience without allowing old expectations to override current physical evidence. This study asks what repeated physical experience must contribute for a spatial world model to become progressively more useful rather than simply more persistent. A physics-grounded dynamic maze separates recurring spatial change from the continuous consequences of action. Cross-episode Spatial Change Memory learns relations among environmental transformations, while state-action-outcome experience refines predictions of motion. Structured experience progressively reduces the need for future route correction and transfers to spatial transitions not encountered during learning. The advantage disappears when past changes contain no information about future ones. Continuous navigation further shows that predictive memory changes behavior when a previous decision becomes invalid but leaves behavior unchanged when the decision remains correct. Physical tests expose a complementary limit: correct topology does not guarantee correct action prediction, and accumulated physical experience reduces this mismatch within the modeled dynamics. The results characterize continual world knowledge as experience that improves future prediction and action beyond stored episodes while remaining revisable by the physical outcomes it is intended to predict.

llm.title_ja: 物理的経験が継続的な空間世界モデルを構築する
llm.tldr_ja: 物理法則に基づく動的迷路を用いて、空間的変化の記憶と状態・行動・結果の経験の蓄積が、予測精度を向上させ、過去の記憶を過剰に優先させずに新しい物理的証拠に修正されることを示す。
llm.problem: 継続的な運用において、環境が変化した際、過去の経験を利用しつつ古い期待が現在の物理的証拠を上書きしないようにする必要がある。
llm.method: 物理法則に基づく動的迷路を使用し、クロスエピソード空間変化記憶によって環境変換間の関係を学習し、状態・行動・結果の経験によって動作予測を洗練させる。
llm.result: 構造化された経験が将来のルート修正の必要性を漸進的に減らし、学習時に遭遇しなかった空間遷移へも転移することを示した。

2611.04016.tldr_en: The results characterize continual world knowledge as experience that improves future prediction and action beyond stored episodes while remaining revisable by the physical outcomes it is intended to predict.

2611.04007.title: Physics-Informed Identification of Tensegrity Prestress across Taut-Slack Transitions
2611.04007.abstract: Prestress governs the stability, stiffness, and dynamic behavior of tensegrity structures, but it is not directly observable from sparse structural measurements, and it may decrease during service life. Under strong excitation, the cables may slacken and the dynamics become nonsmooth. Existing identification methods are limited to the taut regime, and physics-informed networks for tensegrities solve only the forward problem of predicting the response from known member parameters. This study formulates the inverse problem. Neural networks are trained on the equation-of-motion residual in constrained Cartesian coordinates, where the mass matrix is constant and the force densities enter linearly. The force densities, damping, and axial stiffness are trainable parameters, and the tension-only cable law is kept. A Fisher-information analysis shows, before inversion, which member parameters a record can determine. The method is tested on simulated planar tensegrity frames with up to five modules and a three-dimensional prism, and on measured records of a biomimetic leg and a full-scale tensegrity simplex. On the one-module frame, the identifiable force densities are recovered within 1.5% from noisy accelerations at half the free coordinates, on records with and without taut-slack transitions. Records with transitions determine members that taut records leave undetermined. On the five-module frame, a 16-cable two-span bridge, the median force-density error rises moderately, to 4.2%. On measured records, an identified spring stiffness is within 0.1% of its independently measured value on average, and the identified simplex prestress at 13 levels agrees with its cable force transducers to 2.9% root-mean-square.
2611.04007.comment: 44 pages, 15 figures, 15 tables; supplementary material included

llm.title_ja: 弛緩・緊張遷移をまたいだテンセグリティプレストレスの物理情報に基づく同定
llm.tldr_ja: 制約付きデカルト座標における運動方程式の残差を用いてニューラルネットワークを訓練し、弛緩状態を含むテンセグリティ構造の逆問題としてのプレストレス同定を実現する。
llm.problem: プレストレスはスパースな構造測定から直接観測できず、強励振下ではケーブルが弛緩して動的挙動が非滑らかになるため、既存の同定手法は緊張レジームに限定されている。
llm.method: 制約付きデカルト座標における運動方程式の残差に基づいてニューラルネットワークを訓練し、力密度、減衰、軸剛性を訓練可能パラメータとしてテンション専用ケーブル法則を維持する逆問題を定式化する。
llm.result: 1モジュールフレームにおいて、ノイズを含む加速度から識別可能な力密度を1.5%以内で回収でき、実測データにおいても同定されたバネ剛性やプレストレスが実測値と良好に一致した。
keywords_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワーク

2611.04006.title: Controlling Action-Head Co-Adaptation to VLM Representation Anisotropy
2611.04006.abstract: Modern learning systems increasingly combine pretrained models with downstream heads. Despite the growing importance of such modular designs, how the downstream model co-adapts to the geometry of pretrained representations remains relatively underexplored. We study this problem through vision-language-action models (VLAs), where a pretrained vision-language model (VLM) conditions an action model for control. We find that the action model progressively concentrates its sensitivity on high-variance dimensions of the VLM outputs. Through controlled experiments across different backbone-head models, we further show that counteracting this sensitivity concentration can be beneficial under representation--task mismatch settings. Motivated by these observations, we introduce \emph{Adaptive Interface Equalizer} (AdaIE), a parameter-free mechanism that reweights pretrained representations according to the evolving downstream sensitivity during training. AdaIE improves VLA success rates on simulation benchmarks, with gains of up to $+5.28$ percentage points (pp) on RoboCasa-GR1 and $+1.68$ pp on RoboTwin 2.0, and achieves an average gain of $+19$ pp across five real-world manipulation tasks. It further generalizes to diffusion policies and world models, improving downstream performance in both settings. Our results highlight interface co-adaptation as an important optimization problem when coupling pretrained representations with downstream models.

llm.title_ja: VLM表現の異方性に対するアクションヘッドの共適応の制御
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済み表現の幾何学的構造に対する下流モデルの共適応に着目し、学習中の下流の感度に応じて表現を再重み付けするパラメータフリーなメカニズム「AdaIE」を提案し、VLAの成功率を向上させる。
llm.problem: 事前学習済みモデルを下流のヘッドと組み合わせる際、下流モデルが事前学習済み表現の幾何学にどのように共適応するかは十分に探求されていない。
llm.method: トレーニング中の進化する下流の感度に応じて事前学習済み表現を再重み付けするパラメータフリーなメカニズム「Adaptive Interface Equalizer (AdaIE)」を導入する。
llm.result: シミュレーションベンチマークおよび5つの実世界マニピュレーションタスクにおいて成功率を大幅に向上させ、拡散ポリシーや世界モデルにも一般化することを示した。

2611.04006.tldr_en: AdaIE, a parameter-free mechanism that reweights pretrained representations according to the evolving downstream sensitivity during training, is introduced, highlighting interface co-adaptation as an important optimization problem when coupling pretrained representations with downstream models.

2611.04005.title: Characterizing Adversarial GEO via Implicit Brand Injection
2611.04005.abstract: Generative search engines increasingly shape how users discover products, services, and commercial entities by generating answers from retrieved web content. This creates an opportunity to influence which brands appear in these answers by modifying the content available to the retrieval system. In this work, we study an adversarial generative engine optimization (GEO) setting in which a predefined brand is added to an article through a single contextually integrated mention. The challenge is to make the mention fit the surrounding article without making the content overtly promotional, while keeping it relevant enough to be retrieved and to influence the generated answer. To study this, we introduce Implicit Brand Injection (IBI), a multi-agent framework that identifies insertion locations, rewrites the selected sentence, verifies the edit, and selects the final candidate. To evaluate IBI at scale, we construct IBIBench, which contains 1,000 web articles and 60 synthetic brands across 12 diverse domains, with both endemic and non-endemic brand placements. We compare IBI with Direct Prompting and Best-of-N with ranking under an equivalent budget, evaluating insertion quality, target-chunk retrieval, and downstream brand propagation. Compared with the baselines, IBI produces insertions that better preserve semantics and disrupt perplexity less, while improving Hit@k across all evaluated cutoffs, query regimes, and placement settings. IBI achieves up to 82.2% Hit@10 and 0.74 MRR@10, while Brand Mention Rate (BMR) and Conditional Propagation (CP) reach up to 62.7% and 75.9%, respectively. These results show that a single brand mention can increase both retrieval exposure and brand visibility in generated responses, highlighting the need for defenses against implicit content manipulation in generative search.

llm.title_ja: 暗黙的ブランド注入を通じた敵対的GEOの特性評価
llm.tldr_ja: 生成検索エンジンにおいて単一の文脈に統合された言及を通じて定義されたブランドを記事に追加する敵対的生成エンジン最適化（GEO）設定を研究し、マルチエージェントフレームワーク「IBI」を提案する。
llm.problem: 生成検索エンジンがブランドや製品の発見を形作る中で、プレースメントが露骨に宣伝的にならず、かつ検索・生成に影響を与えるようにブランドを出現させることが困難である。
llm.method: 挿入場所を特定し、選択した文を書き換え、編集を検証し、最終候補を選択するマルチエージェントフレームワーク「Implicit Brand Injection (IBI)」を導入する。
llm.result: ベースラインと比較して、セマンティクスをより良く保持しつつ、評価されたすべてのカットオフやクエリレジームでHit@kを改善し、最大の露出と可視性を達成した。

2611.04005.tldr_en: Results show that a single brand mention can increase both retrieval exposure and brand visibility in generated responses, highlighting the need for defenses against implicit content manipulation in generative search.

2611.03975.title: Self-governed access control in open robot swarms using a blockchain-based DAO
2611.03975.abstract: Robot swarms harness simple, local interactions among many individually limited robots to produce complex, coordinated collective behavior, making them valuable across domains from agriculture to disaster response. We envision the next frontier for such swarms as open swarms, in which robots join or leave the swarm dynamically at runtime. The ability to dynamically adjust swarm size has been shown to be beneficial, for instance by reducing inconsistencies and network partitioning, especially under sparse connectivity or in complex environments, ultimately improving task performance. For practical deployment, however, open swarms requires governance, particularly protection against Byzantine behavior (i.e., faulty or malicious robots), since allowing robots to join freely also makes the swarm easier to infiltrate. Blockchain technology has recently been incorporated into robot swarms, offering secure, decentralized coordination and improved resilience, though largely in closed settings with a fixed, predetermined membership. In this work, we extend these benefits to open swarms by introducing robot swarms governed by a blockchain-based decentralized autonomous organization (DAO), in which the swarm regulates itself using autonomous rules encoded in smart contracts. We outline several DAO-based governance mechanisms for robot swarms, depending on the needs of the application, and present a proof-of-concept implementation of a simple DAO that regulates swarm membership and prevents Byzantine infiltration. Our simulation results and real-robot validations show that DAO-governed access control and robot removal can maintain proper swarm functioning while keeping the number of Byzantine robots within acceptable limits.

llm.title_ja: ブロックチェーンベースのDAOを用いたオープンロボット群における自己統治型アクセス制御
llm.tldr_ja: スマートコントラクトにエンコードされた自律規則を用いてロボット群が自己規制するブロックチェーンベースの分散型自立組織（DAO）を導入し、オープンなロボット群におけるアクセス制御とバイザンチン攻撃からの防御を実現する。
llm.problem: オープンなロボット群では、ロボットが自由に加入できるようにすることで群への侵入が容易になるため、バイザンチン挙動（障害や悪意のあるロボット）からの保護を含むガバナンスが必要となる。
llm.method: ブロックチェーンベースの分散型自立組織（DAO）により群が自らメンバーシップを規制し、バイザンチン侵入を防ぐ自己統治メカニズムを実装する。
llm.result: シミュレーション結果と実ロボットの検証により、DAOによってガバナンスされたアクセス制御とロボットの除外が、バイザンチンロボットの数を許容範囲内に抑えながら適切な群の機能を維持できることが示された。

2611.03975.tldr_en: This work outlines several DAO-based governance mechanisms for robot swarms, depending on the needs of the application, and presents a proof-of-concept implementation of a simple DAO that regulates swarm membership and prevents Byzantine infiltration.

2611.03944.title: h-NESDF: An Infinitely Differentiable Signed Distance Between Two Sets with Robotic Applications
2611.03944.abstract: Computing distances between sets is important in many robotic applications, such as motion planning and control. In many applications, derivatives of the distance are needed as well. It is well known that the Euclidean distance is not always differentiable, which create issues to algorithms that need a derivative. In this paper, we introduce NESDF, the Normal Euclidean Signed Distance Function between two general (with mild regularity assumptions but possibly non-convex) sets. This metric is still not differentiable, but it allows us to introduce a generalization, $h$-NESDF, which has a smoothing parameter $h$ such that the metric is infinitely differentiable for all $h>0$ and that reduces to the NESDF when $h$ goes to $0$. The metric is amenable to GPU parallelization, and thus can be computed efficiently. We show extensive simulation results to evaluate its viability in motion planning.
authors: Pedro Antonio de Souza Campos Rodrigues

llm.title_ja: h-NESDF：ロボット工学への応用を持つ2つの集合間の無限回微分可能な符号付き距離
llm.tldr_ja: 2つの一般集合間の正規ユークリッド符号付き距離関数（NESDF）を一般化し、任意の$h>0$に対して無限回微分可能でGPU並列化に適した$h$-NESDFを提案する。
llm.problem: ユークリッド距離は必ずしも微分可能ではなく、微分を必要とするモーションプランニングなどのアルゴリズムにおいて問題を引き起こす。
llm.method: 平滑化パラメータ$h$を持ち、すべての$h>0$に対して無限回微分可能で、$h$が0に近づくにつれてNESDFに縮退する一般化指標$h$-NESDFを導入し、GPU並列化による効率的な計算を実現する。
llm.result: モーションプランニングにおける実行可能性を評価するための広範なシミュレーション結果を示した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.03944.tldr_en: NESDF is introduced, the Normal Euclidean Signed Distance Function between two general (with mild regularity assumptions but possibly non-convex) sets, and a generalization, $h$-NESDF, which has a smoothing parameter such that the metric is infinitely differentiable for all and can be computed efficiently.

2611.03940.title: Coordinate Frame Recovery, Per Class NMS and Null Return Modelling for Sim2Real V2X LiDAR Detection
2611.03940.abstract: We describe our approach to the V2X-Real track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, in which a 3D object detector must be trained exclusively on synthetic data and evaluated on unseen real roadside LiDAR from an Ouster OS1-64 unit, while the synthetic point clouds are simultaneously scored for distributional realism. Our final entry scores 0.7457 combined, from a detection mAP of 0.4382 and a realism score of 0.9251. Three findings account for most of our result, and all three were diagnostic rather than architectural. First, a coordinate frame mismatch between our predictions and the evaluation ground truth was suppressing detection AP entirely; recovering it took our score from 0.3520 to 0.5147 in a single submission. Second, a single global non maximum suppression threshold was destroying genuine pedestrian detections, because pedestrians occur in groups and a 0.3 IoU threshold applied to a 0.7 m box suppresses distinct neighbouring people; correcting this per class raised overall mAP from 0.0751 to 0.4295. Third, approximately 31 percent of the real reference point cloud consists of null returns encoded as the literal point (0, 0, 0), a format feature entirely absent from our synthetic clouds, which pinned Earth Mover's Distance near its floor until we modelled it. Negative results are reported at equal length, and Section 9 gives a full account of data provenance and compliance. That section also accounts for every mechanism contributing to the submitted score.
2611.03940.comment: 8 pages. 1st place, Track 7 (UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR, V2X-Real), DriveX Grand Challenge, ECCV 2026 Workshop. Code: https://github.com/amanupg/urbantwin-sim2real-v2x

llm.title_ja: Sim2Real V2X LiDAR検出のための座標系復元、クラス別NMSおよびヌルリターンモデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 合成データのみで訓練された3Dオブジェクト検出器を実世界のロードサイドLiDARで評価するUrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDARチャレンジにおいて、座標系の不一致解消、クラス別NMS、ヌルリターンのモデリングにより高得点を達成した。
llm.problem: 合成データのみで訓練された3Dオブジェクト検出器を未知の実世界ロードサイドLiDARで評価する際、座標系の不一致や特有のデータ特性が性能を著しく低下させる。
llm.method: 予測と評価のグランドトゥルース間の座標系ミスマッチの解消、クラス別の非最大抑制（NMS）しきい値の調整、および実点群に含まれるヌルリターンの明示的なモデリングを行う。
llm.result: 検出mAP 0.4382、リアリズムスコア 0.9251を達成し、チャレンジのトラックで上位の成績を収めた。

2611.03937.title: FlowBench: Counterfactual Imagination Training for Spatial Intelligence
2611.03937.abstract: Humans imagine scene changes under hypothetical motions, an ability central to spatial reasoning and robotic planning. However, this capability remains underexplored in vision-language models and world models. We formalize this capability as Counterfactual Spatial Imagination (CSI) and introduce FlowBench, a resource for training and evaluating both, with 428K training examples spanning simulated and real-world scenes, household environments and tabletop manipulation, and diverse question types. A scalable, fully automatic pipeline pairs each hypothetical motion with spatial questions and, in simulation, exact outcome frames and optical flow. For VLMs, proprietary models exhibit an imagination gap, performing worse when motion outcomes must be inferred than when observed, and open-source models perform near chance; fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B on FlowBench-Sim-Train raises its accuracy by 29.5 percentage points in simulation and 16.9 on real images, a strong sim-to-real transfer. For world models, training on FlowBench-Sim improves text-to-flow prediction for all four model families we test, raising the accuracy of Psi-0.6 from 52.1% to 61.7%. FlowBench thus serves as a training and evaluation resource for both. Code and datasets are released at https://github.com/liuyifan22/FlowBench.

llm.title_ja: FlowBench：空間知能のための反実仮想イマジネーション訓練
llm.tldr_ja: 仮想的な動きに対するシーンの変化を想像する「反実仮想空間イマジネーション（CSI）」を定式化し、シミュレーションと実世界の多様なデータを含む訓練・評価リソース「FlowBench」を提案する。
llm.problem: 仮想的な動きの下でのシーン変化を想像する能力は、視覚言語モデルや世界モデルにおいて未だ十分に探求されていない。
llm.method: 仮説上の動きと空間的質問、正確な結果フレーム、オプティカルフローをペアリングする自動パイプラインを構築し、FlowBenchを構築してVLMや世界モデルのファインチューニングを行う。
llm.result: Qwen3-VL-8BをFlowBenchで微調整することで、シミュレーションでの精度が29.5%、実画像で16.9%向上し、世界モデルのテキストからフローへの予測精度も向上した。

2611.03937.tldr_en: FlowBench is introduced, a resource for training and evaluating Counterfactual Spatial Imagination (CSI) and a scalable, fully automatic pipeline that pairs each hypothetical motion with spatial questions and, in simulation, exact outcome frames and optical flow.

2611.03936.title: Geometric Refinement and Distributional Alignment for Sim2Real Roadside LiDAR Detection
2611.03936.abstract: We describe our approach to the LUMPI track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, in which a 3D object detector must be trained exclusively on synthetic data and evaluated on unseen real roadside LiDAR, while the synthetic point clouds are simultaneously scored for distributional realism. Our final entry scores 0.4793 combined, from a detection mAP of 0.1333 and a realism score of 0.9126. Our contribution is not a new architecture. Working from a PointPillars baseline, we obtained most of our gains from three sources. First, a diagnosis that small object failure in roadside LiDAR is a localisation problem rather than a detection problem, which led to a parameter free geometric refinement worth 86 percent relative on pedestrian AP. Second, an audit of our own post processing which revealed that a shipped rule was destroying valid predictions, the repair of which produced our single largest detection gain at 335 percent relative on the Van class. Third, treating the realism metrics analytically rather than as a black box, which showed that one of the four components is a closed form function of nine summary statistics. We also report an experimental methodology that we believe is the more transferable result. Because mean AP decomposes into independent per class terms, a single submission can carry several mutually controlled experiments, and a submission assembled entirely from previously measured components has a score that is known before it is sent. We predicted our final score to four decimal places prior to submission. We report negative results at equal length, and give a full account of data provenance and compliance in Section 8, including a full account of every mechanism contributing to the submitted score.
2611.03936.comment: 8 pages. 1st place, Track 6 (UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR, LUMPI), DriveX Grand Challenge, ECCV 2026 Workshop. Code: https://github.com/amanupg/urbantwin-sim2real-lumpi

llm.title_ja: Sim2RealロードサイドLiDAR検出のための幾何学的洗練と分布整合
llm.tldr_ja: 合成データのみで訓練され実世界ロードサイドLiDARで評価される3D物体検出器に対し、パラメータフリーな幾何学的洗練、後処理の修正、分布の解析的アプローチを導入して検出精度とリアリズムを向上させる。
llm.problem: ロードサイドLiDARにおける小物体の失敗は検出問題ではなく局所化問題であり、後処理のルールが無効な予測を破壊するなど、Sim2Realのギャップが存在する。
llm.method: PointPillarsをベースラインとし、歩行者APを改善するパラメータフリーな幾何学的洗練、Vanクラスの予測を修正する後処理の監査、およびリアリズム指標の解析的処理を行う。
llm.result: 検出mAP 0.1333、リアリズムスコア 0.9126を達成し、予測通りのスコアを正確に算出できる実験的メソドロジーを実証した。

2611.03936.tldr_en: This work describes its approach to the LUMPI track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, in which a 3D object detector must be trained exclusively on synthetic data and evaluated on unseen real roadside LiDAR, while the synthetic point clouds are simultaneously scored for distributional realism.

2611.03932.title: CoReMatch: Recurrent Continuous Coordinate Refinement for Real-Time Robotic Feature Matching
2611.03932.abstract: Feature matching underpins many robotic perception tasks, including visual localization, mapping, SLAM, and autonomous navigation. Existing semi-dense matchers predict confidence on fixed grids, limiting correspondences to predefined locations and requiring costly high-resolution grids for precise localization. We present CoReMatch (Coordinate Refinement Match), a recurrent framework that refines correspondences directly in continuous coordinate space rather than predicting discrete confidence maps. CoReMatch progressively improves correspondence estimates by propagating information across iterations. At the coarse stage, a Deep Aggregated Transformer captures global context and iteratively updates correspondence coordinates, while a lightweight regression head further sharpens their localization. Experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks show that CoReMatch strikes a strong balance between accuracy and efficiency, outperforming Efficient LoFTR in accuracy while running more than 10x faster on embedded edge hardware. These results demonstrate that recurrent coordinate refinement offers an efficient and scalable approach to real-time feature matching for robotic perception.

llm.title_ja: CoReMatch：リアルタイムロボット特徴量マッチングのための再帰的連続座標洗練
llm.tldr_ja: 離散的な信頼度マップを予測するのではなく連続座標空間で直接対応関係を洗練する再帰的フレームワーク「CoReMatch」を提案し、精度の高さを維持しながらエッジハードウェア上で高速に動作させる。
llm.problem: 既存の半密なマッチャーは固定グリッド上で信頼度を予測するため、対応関係が事前定義された位置に制限され、正確な局所化に高解像度グリッドが必要となる。
llm.method: Deep Aggregated Transformerによりグローバルコンテキストを捉えて対応座標を反復的に更新し、軽量な回帰ヘッドによって局所化をシャープにする再帰的フレームワーク「CoReMatch」を構築する。
llm.result: 屋内および屋外のベンチマークにおいてEfficient LoFTRを精度で上回り、組込みエッジハードウェア上で10倍以上高速に動作することを実証した。
keywords_ja: ビジュアルローカリゼーション

2611.03932.tldr_en: Experiments demonstrate that recurrent coordinate refinement offers an efficient and scalable approach to real-time feature matching for robotic perception, outperforming Efficient LoFTR in accuracy while running more than 10x faster on embedded edge hardware.

2611.03885.title: Self-Consistent Neural Control: Learning Trajectories for Implicit Equilibrium
2611.03885.abstract: One big challenge in physical AI is interacting with systems whose states are defined by implicit equilibrium. Learning in these systems is difficult because their responses can be multistable, path-dependent, and sensitive over long horizons. Adjoint learning provides an efficient way to optimize trajectories without unrolling iterative equilibrium solvers, but its gradient relies on the frozen-tangent approximation, which neglects higher-order sensitivity terms and can become inaccurate when the local equilibrium varies rapidly. In this work, we introduce Self-Consistent Neural Control (SCNC), optimizing trajectories along which sensitivity variations are explicitly controlled. We derive a mathematical bound on the resulting gradient error and develop a practical finite-difference approximation. We validate the framework on deformable objects, which are representative of implicit equilibrium systems, ranging from simple quadratic energy models such as elastic rods to complex systems including thin-walled tubes, measuring tapes, and Slinky-like structures. Compared with the adjoint learning and the gradient-free iCEM baselines, SCNC achieves faster convergence and more stable optimization by reducing switching to undesirable equilibrium branches, doubling the stable optimization rate over adjoint learning 83.3% vs. 41.7% and reducing the average loss by more than 1.5 orders of magnitude on thin-walled tubes, where sensitivity variations are pronounced.

llm.title_ja: 自己無撞着ニューラル制御：暗黙的平衡のための軌道学習
llm.tldr_ja: 感度変動を明示的に制御しながら軌道を最適化する「自己無撞着ニューラル制御（SCNC）」を提案し、変形可能オブジェクトの安定した効率的な最適化を実現する。
llm.problem: 暗黙的平衡によって状態が定義されるシステムは応答が多安定性、経路依存性、長地平線での高感度を持ち、学習が困難である。
llm.method: 勾配誤差の数学的導出と実用的な有限差分近似を行い、感度変動を明示的に制御しながら軌道を最適化する自己無撞着ニューラル制御（SCNC）を開発する。
llm.result: 薄壁チューブなどの変形可能オブジェクトにおいて、 adjoint学習と比較して安定した最適化率を倍増（83.3%対41.7%）させ、平均損失を1.5桁以上削減した。
keywords_ja: 変形可能オブジェクト

2611.03885.tldr_en: This work introduces Self-Consistent Neural Control (SCNC), optimizing trajectories along which sensitivity variations are explicitly controlled, and derives a mathematical bound on the resulting gradient error and develops a practical finite-difference approximation.

2611.03853.title: Performance, Scalability and Maintenance: An Experimental Study of RPA vs. Autonomous Agents in the Healthcare Domain
2611.03853.abstract: Healthcare information systems are fragmented, and retrieving data from legacy web portals is a recurrent need. Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is deterministic but sensitive to interface changes, whereas autonomous agents based on large language models (Agent Process Automation, APA) promise adaptability at a higher computational cost. Following Design Science Research, we developed and compared an RPA solution (Playwright) and an APA solution (browser-use, LangGraph and Gemini 2.5 Flash-lite) to retrieve mammography and breast ultrasound reports from a laboratory portal, treating reports solely as informational artifacts. Across two rounds (T and T+7), RPA reached 98.90% accuracy and 98.27% F1-score versus 96.49% and 94.48% for APA, was about 13 times faster (16.07 s vs. 207.21 s per patient) and cost about six times less per report (USD 0.030 vs. 0.187). Both reached 100% step success rates; APA varied more over time. For a stable interface, RPA was superior.
authors: Ana Paula Wernz da Cunha Müller

llm.title_ja: ヘルスケア分野におけるRPAと自律型エージェントのパフォーマンス、拡張性、保守性の実験的研究
llm.tldr_ja: レガシーなウェブポータルからデータを取得するタスクにおいて、決定論的なRPA（Playwright）と大規模言語モデルに基づく自律エージェント（APA）のパフォーマンス、速度、コストを比較評価する。
llm.problem: ヘルスケア情報システムは断片的であり、レガシーなウェブポータルからのデータ取得は反復的なニーズがあるが、RPAはインターフェース変更に脆弱でAPAは計算コストが高い。
llm.method: デザインサイエンス研究に基づき、マンモグラフィと乳房超音波検査のレポートを取得するためのRPAソリューションとAPAソリューションを開発し、正確性、速度、コストを比較する。
llm.result: RPAは精度98.90%、F1スコア98.27%を達成し、APA（96.49%、94.48%）より優れており、約13倍高速でコストは約6分の1であった。
keywords_ja: ロボティックプロセスオートメーション

2611.03853.tldr_en: This work developed and compared an RPA solution (Playwright) and an APA solution (browser-use, LangGraph and Gemini 2.5 Flash-lite) to retrieve mammography and breast ultrasound reports from a laboratory portal, treating reports solely as informational artifacts, and found RPA was superior for a stable interface.

2611.03850.title: RoboScope Kit: Unified Interfaces for Fast and Scalable Embodied-AI Evaluation
2611.03850.abstract: Simulation benchmarks are the standard way to compare robot policies, but each benchmark brings its own evaluator, observation layout, and action convention, and evaluation is slow: 500 RoboTwin Easy episodes with one simulator and one model on one GPU take 359.7 minutes. Profiling the official StarVLA evaluator shows that simulation occupies CPU cores while the GPU averages 14.3% utilization. RoboScope Kit wraps each model once in a Python class called a Policy, and each benchmark once in an adapter around the benchmark's own evaluator, so the benchmark's rules and scoring stay unchanged. Scheduling runs simulator workers and Policy replicas as separate pools, sizes both from measured probes, and shards work deterministically across GPU instances; runtime optimization renders only the observations an action-chunk Policy reads. Adapters cover six benchmark families. On LIBERO-Long with a StarVLA checkpoint on one 48 GiB RTX 4090, the concurrency search selects twelve simulator workers sharing three Policy replicas, which evaluate 500 episodes 4.45$\times$ faster than the official StarVLA evaluation with equivalent success rates, 2.78$\times$ faster than RLinf, and 1.52$\times$ faster than vla-eval at its tuned configuration. With CUDA MPS, which lets the replicas run their kernels concurrently, the search selects sixteen workers sharing four replicas, 6.16$\times$ faster than StarVLA, 3.85$\times$ faster than RLinf, and 2.10$\times$ faster than vla-eval. On RoboTwin Easy, four GPUs with chunk-boundary observation complete the 500 episodes in 14.4 minutes, 25.04$\times$ faster than the single-GPU baseline, with identical success outcomes and terminal steps.
2611.03850.comment: 29 pages, 9 figures. Project page: https://roboscope.pages.dev/ Code: https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/RoboScope-Kit

llm.title_ja: RoboScope Kit：高速かつ拡張性のあるembodied-AI評価のための統一インターフェース
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレータワーカーとポリシーレプリカを別々のプールとしてスケジュールし、ワークをGPUインスタンス間で決定論的にシャードすることで評価を高速化する「RoboScope Kit」を提案する。
llm.problem: シミュレーションベンチマークは固有の評価器や観察レイアウトを持ち、評価が遅く、従来の評価ではGPU利用率が低い。
llm.method: モデルをPythonクラス（Policy）でラップし、各ベンチマークをアダプターでラップすることで、シミュレータワーカーとポリシーレプリカを別プールとしてスケジュールし、CUDA MPSを活用して並列実行する。
llm.result: LIBERO-LongやRoboTwin Easyなどのベンチマークにおいて、公式の評価方法と比較して数倍から25倍以上の高速化を達成しつつ、同等の成功率を維持した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション評価

2611.03825.title: A Tutorial on Shape Servoing of Deformable Objects-Part II: Advanced Concepts
2611.03825.abstract: In robotics, shape control, or shape servoing, refers to the automatic manipulation of a deformable object toward a desired shape. This article is the second of a two-part tutorial on data-driven, Jacobian-based shape control, in which the deformation Jacobian, a local model of how robot motion changes the measured shape, is estimated from measurements. Part I built the shape-servoing loop and derived a local stability condition. This paper starts by using the singular value decomposition of the deformation Jacobian to identify shape changes that can be produced by small robot motions, those that require large robot motions, and those that are locally unavailable. It then analyses how the choice of shape features determines how the controller regulates the object's shape and, therefore, how much the object deforms on its way to the target. It then describes three ways in which the shape control loop can fail: loss of controllability, loss of observability, and occurrence of mechanical instabilities. It closes with shape-control extensions to time-varying targets, secondary tasks, and three-dimensional objects.
2611.03825.comment: Part II of a two-part tutorial. 10 pages, 9 figures. Code: https://github.com/nachocz/tutorial_on_shape_servoing_of_deformable_objects. Interactive demos: https://nachocz.github.io/tutorial_on_shape_servoing_of_deformable_objects/

llm.title_ja: 変形可能オブジェクトの形状サーボに関するチュートリアル - パートII：高度な概念
llm.tldr_ja: データ駆動型のヤコビアンベース形状制御における特異値分解を用いた形状変化の分析、制御ループの失敗原因、および時間変動するターゲットへの拡張について解説する。
llm.problem: 変形可能オブジェクトの自動マニピュレーション（形状サーボ）において、可制御性・可観測性の喪失や機械的不安定性などの失敗要因に対処する必要がある。
llm.method: 変形ヤコビアンの特異値分解を用いた形状変化の分析、形状特徴の選択による変形レギュレーションの解析、制御ループの3つの失敗モードの解説を行う。
llm.result: 時間変動するターゲット、二次タスク、3次元オブジェクトへの形状制御の拡張について論じた。
keywords_ja: 変形可能オブジェクト

2611.03825.tldr_en: This paper starts by using the singular value decomposition of the deformation Jacobian to identify shape changes that can be produced by small robot motions, those that require large robot motions, and those that are locally unavailable.

2611.03815.title: AIRoA-0: Long-Horizon, Precise, Cross-Embodiment Manipulation from Handheld Data
2611.03815.abstract: AIRoA-0 (A-0) is a bimanual manipulation system learned from 16,151 hours of handheld demonstrations, with no robot data collected at any stage. The demonstrations are recorded with YUBI, our open-source handheld gripper, which lets people record manipulation data anywhere with no robot present. From a single instruction, A-0 sorts more than a dozen small parts into their numbered cells and changes the mop pads and brush of a robot vacuum; among other tasks, it unzips a pencil case and folds a towel. It performs these tasks using only a camera on each wrist, with no head or scene camera, at a site where none of its training data was recorded. Across the ten tasks of our evaluation, it averages a success rate of 78%, against 27% for the strongest of four other vision-language-action models post-trained on the same task demonstrations. We collect no teleoperation data and use no reinforcement learning or on-robot corrections, and the robot appears only at test time. The system learns which regions of each wrist view matter for the task, predicts the stage the task has reached, and decodes actions as a continuous stream. A-0 is embodiment-agnostic: it runs on robots that mount the YUBI gripper, such as a bimanual Franka, TX-G2, OpenArm and UR. We are releasing the dataset, to our knowledge the largest open dataset of handheld-gripper demonstrations with task and subtask instructions, together with the pre-trained weights and the post-training recipe. Videos of A-0 on every task are on the project page, https://a-0.airoa.io. Anyone can build the gripper, record a task of their own and post-train the model on it in under four hours on a single node of eight H200 GPUs.

llm.title_ja: AIRoA-0：ハンドヘルドデータからの長期、高精度、クロスエンボディメントマニピュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットデータを使用せず、オープンソースのハンドヘルドグリッパーYUBIによる16,151時間のデモンストレーションから学習した、双腕マニピュレーションシステム「AIRoA-0」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のマニピュレーション学習には膨大なロボットによる実機データ収集が必要でありコストがかかる。
llm.method: ハンドヘルドグリッパーYUBIで記録されたデモンストレーションデータを用いて、タスクの進行状況を予測し連続的なストリームとしてアクションをデコードするビジョン言語行動モデルを学習させる。
llm.result: 10の評価タスクにおいて平均78%の成功率を達成し、他の視覚言語行動モデルを大きく上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: 双腕マニピュレーション
クロスエンボディメント

2611.03815.tldr_en: The dataset is released, to the knowledge the largest open dataset of handheld-gripper demonstrations with task and subtask instructions, together with the pre-trained weights and the post-training recipe.

2611.03647.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
2611.03647.abstract: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment. Finally, because estimated actions cannot fully capture contact-rich interactions, we collect on-policy human corrections through DAgger to improve performance. We evaluate Pixel-UMI on five challenging tasks spanning articulated-object manipulation, deformable-object handling, constrained-space reaching, whole-body collision avoidance, and contact-rich bimanual coordination, achieving 87.0% average task progress. Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi
2611.03647.comment: Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi

llm.title_ja: Pixel-UMI: センサー付きの人のデモンストレーションから環境認識型全身マニピュレーションを学習する
llm.tldr_ja: 人のデモンストレーションから環境認識型の全身マニピュレーションポリシーを学習するパイプライン「Pixel-UMI」を提案し、5つの困難なタスクで平均87.0%のタスク達成度を記録した。
llm.problem: 体格の違いがポリシー学習を複雑にし、残余姿勢誤差による視点ミスマッチが生じる。
llm.method: 環境認識型リターゲット（EAR）、リターゲット誤差考慮型マスキング（REAM）、およびDAggerによる人による修正の収集を用いる。
llm.result: 5つの困難なタスクで平均87.0%のタスク達成度を達成した。

2611.03647.tldr_en: This work presents Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data, and introduces Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment.

2611.03648.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
2611.03648.abstract: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel

llm.title_ja: Pixel: 汎用モバイルマニピュレーション学習のための共同設計されたフルスタックロボットシステム
llm.tldr_ja: 汎用モバイルマニピュレーション学習に向けて、ハードウェア、データ収集、全身制御、ポリシー学習を統合した共同設計フルスタックシステム「Pixel」を提案する。
llm.problem: コンポーネントが個別に開発されるためミスマッチが生じ、システム全体の能力が制限される。
llm.method: 低コストの車輪型ヒューマノイド、多様なデータ収集インターフェース、統合された全身コントローラー、共通のポリシー学習パイプラインを組み合わせる。
llm.result: 器用さ、能動知覚、ナビゲーション、全身協調を必要とするモバイルマニピュレーション動作を実証した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2611.03646.title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
2611.03646.abstract: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence, yet it requires models to accurately understand fine-grained human actions from egocentric observations. However, existing benchmarks remain limited in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association. We introduce EgoActionBench, a benchmark that represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. EgoActionBench contains 1,407 episodes with 41,132 human-refined action annotations. To evaluate such dense predictions, we propose an evaluation protocol that retrieves temporally eligible candidates, selects a prediction by content agreement, and scores semantic fidelity and temporal overlap alongside action precision and recall, jointly capturing what happens, when it happens, and which hand performs it. We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems on EgoActionBench and further adapt two backbones, Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning on automatically annotated training episodes. EgoAction improves EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points on the two backbones, and both adapted models outperform all open-source baselines. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations of current models in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association, highlighting the gap between general video understanding and the action understanding required for embodied intelligence.

llm.title_ja: EgoActionBench: 視点映像に対する密なアクションキャプションのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 連続する人のマニピュレーションを時間的に局所化したアトミックアクションとして表現するベンチマーク「EgoActionBench」を導入し、20のベースラインモデルを評価した。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークはアクションの原子性、時間的精度、手の動作の関連付けにおいて限界がある。
llm.method: 左手、右手、または両手に紐づく時間的に局所化されたアトミックアクションのアノテーションを含むデータセットを構築し、評価プロトコルを提案する。
llm.result: 既存モデルにはアクションの原子性や時間的精度、手の関連付けに重大な限界があることが明らかになった。

2611.03646.tldr_en: This work introduces EgoActionBench, a benchmark that represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands, and proposes an evaluation protocol that retrieves temporally eligible candidates, selects a prediction by content agreement, and scores semantic fidelity and temporal overlap alongside action precision and recall.

2611.03779.title: Robot-Matched Soft Fingers for UMI Data Collection: Lessons from 100 Hours of Pick and Place
2611.03779.abstract: Training robot policies for multi-task pick and place requires demonstrations on many objects, which handheld Universal Manipulation Interfaces (UMIs) can collect quickly and cheaply. However, existing UMIs depend on external base stations, use rigid fingers that give no signal about contact forces, or use parallel-jaw fingers that limit grip strength. We present a battery-powered handheld interface, built on YUBI, whose soft, angled fingers wrap around objects, deform visibly under load as a visual proxy for force, and match the grippers of the robot. With it, we collect a 99.7-hour dataset over 53 objects, train $π_{0.5}$ policies on 49 of them, and hold out the other 4 as unseen objects. We find that a top camera raises success by 13 points even when only about half of the data includes it, and that mid-training on our multi-task data raises success after fine-tuning on unseen objects from 35% to 57%. Finger design, dataset, and data processing code: https://lute-corp.github.io/soft-yubi-site/
2611.03779.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Accepted as a poster at the CoRL 2026 UMI Arena Workshop (Track 3). Project page: https://lute-corp.github.io/soft-yubi-site/
2611.03779.tldr_en: A battery-powered handheld interface, built on YUBI, whose soft, angled fingers wrap around objects, deform visibly under load as a visual proxy for force, and match the grippers of the robot is presented.

2611.03622.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
2611.03622.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. To resolve these limitations, we introduce D&A (Describe & Assess): our approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics. By compelling the VLM to synthesize an explicit, text-based definition of absolute success before scoring, the framework anchors evaluations to an external, global criterion rather than the video's internal timeline. Empirical results demonstrate that our method calibrates zero-shot estimates and mitigates confirmation bias, providing fine-grained, partial progress metrics that accurately penalize failed executions while correctly interpolating successful runs. Being purely prompt-based, D&A generalizes across tasks, embodiments, and benchmarks---matching or surpassing post-trained reward models---and its reward estimates enable efficient downstream reinforcement learning.

llm.title_ja: D&A: 記述と評価の分離によりVLMをゼロショットのロボット報酬モデルとして活用する
llm.tldr_ja: シーンダイナミクスを客観的に記述するフェーズと明確な基準で評価するフェーズに分離する手法「D&A」により、VLMのゼロショット進捗推定の確認バイアスを緩和する。
llm.problem: VLMのゼロショット進捗推定は、確認バイアスやハルシネーションに苦しんでおり、非線形な進捗や失敗を捉えられない。
llm.method: タスクに根ざしたシーンダイナミクスの客観的テキスト記述と、明示的な評価基準を用いた評価フェーズに分離する。
llm.result: ゼロショット推定を調整し、確認バイアスを緩和して、失敗を適切にペナルティしつつ成功を補間する微細な進捗メトリクスを提供した。

2611.03622.tldr_en: D&A (Describe&Assess): the approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics, which generalizes across tasks, embodiments, and benchmarks and enables efficient downstream reinforcement learning.

2611.03617.title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
2611.03617.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts-the facts observed once during training-set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship cannot be explained by training-set diversity alone and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data. Together, our results identify monofact rate in training data as a key factor governing discoveries in language models.

llm.title_ja: 大規模言語モデルの科学的発見能力のトレーニングデータへのトレーシング
llm.tldr_ja: トレーニングセット内のモノファクト（一度だけ観測された事実）の割合が、オープンウェイトモデルの科学的発見能力を決定する鍵であることを理論的・実験的に示した。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデルの信頼性の高い科学的発見を可能にする要因について基本的な疑問が残されている。
llm.method: トレーニングセットにおけるモノファクトの割合を直接操作し、複数のオープンウェイトモデルファミリー等で発見数を検証する。
llm.result: より多くのモノファクトが一貫して多くの発見をもたらし、トレーニングデータのモノファクト率が発見を左右する主要因であることを特定した。

2611.03617.tldr_en: This work directly manipulates monofact rates in training sets and finds that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets.

2611.03595.title: DynaSolver: A Neural Operator for Autoregressive 4D Flow Prediction with Dynamic Boundaries
2611.03595.abstract: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), but most are designed for static geometries and are not equipped to model unsteady flows induced by continuously moving boundaries. We study dynamic-boundary 4D CFD prediction for articulated moving geometries and introduce RoboCFD-4D, a temporally resolved robotic CFD benchmark spanning diverse morphologies and flow conditions. To address the computational and autoregressive challenges of this setting, we propose DynaSolver, a neural operator that explicitly conditions on boundary evolution and causal flow history. DynaSolver employs an efficient physical-token formulation that amortizes point-to-token projection across the operator stack, substantially reducing repeated point-space spatio-temporal computation while retaining accurate point-level reconstruction. We further introduce Replay-Augmented Parallel Training, which exposes the model to autoregressively generated histories while preserving parallel dense supervision, narrowing the gap between ground-truth-conditioned training and autoregressive rollout. Experiments on RoboCFD-4D show that DynaSolver achieves the best full-rollout accuracy among a broad range of learned CFD surrogates, with its advantage increasing as rollout proceeds, indicating substantially reduced autoregressive error accumulation. Project page: https://made-gpt.github.io/DynaSolver-ProjectPage.

llm.title_ja: DynaSolver: 動的境界を持つ自己回帰的4D流体予測のためのニューラルオペレーター
llm.tldr_ja: 連続的に動く境界によって引き起こされる非定常流をモデル化するニューラルオペレーター「DynaSolver」を提案し、動的境界4D CFD予測の精度を向上させた。
llm.problem: 従来のニューラルオペレーターは静的ジオメトリ用に設計されており、動的境界を持つ流れをモデル化できない。
llm.method: 境界の進化と因果的流体履歴を明示的に条件付けするニューラルオペレーターと、物理トークン定式化を採用する。
llm.result: RoboCFD-4Dにおいて学習済みCFD代替モデルの中で最高のフルロールアウト精度を達成した。
keywords_ja: ニューラルオペレーター

2611.03595.tldr_en: DynaSolver is proposed, a neural operator that explicitly conditions on boundary evolution and causal flow history and achieves the best full-rollout accuracy among a broad range of learned CFD surrogates, with its advantage increasing as rollout proceeds, indicating substantially reduced autoregressive error accumulation.

2611.03588.title: 3D-BBDA: Backpropagation-Free Black-Box Domain Adaptation for Robust 3D Point Cloud Recognition
2611.03588.abstract: Robust 3D point-cloud recognition is critical for robotics, mapping, and urban sensing, yet point-cloud classifiers often suffer performance drops under domain shifts caused by sensor changes, environmental variation, and acquisition artifacts. Many existing adaptation methods are difficult to deploy in practice because they require access to source data or the internal parameters of the source model, which may be restricted by privacy, licensing, or security constraints. We present 3D-BBDA, a backpropagation-free black-box domain adaptation framework that adapts a source-trained predictor to unlabeled target data using only black-box outputs. Our method performs pseudo-label guided prototype-based alignment and employs a weighted prediction module to fuse source logits with alignment logits, reducing sensitivity to noisy pseudo-labels. To stabilize prototype memory when pseudo-label coverage is incomplete, we construct a Gaussian-perturbed prototype prior from unlabeled target predictions and use it as a fallback for missing or unreliable class prototypes during alignment. Experiments on four corrupted 3D benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines. On ModelNet-40C, 3D-BBDA achieves mean errors of 32.08% (PointNet) and 29.62% (GDANet), outperforming Source-only (35.88% / 34.03%) and BFTT3D (33.78% / 32.36%). 3D-BBDA requires only a single forward pass with no gradient updates making it suitable for real-time, privacy-preserving deployment in transferable 3D recognition pipelines. Project page is available at https://visdomlab.github.io/3D_BBDA

llm.title_ja: 3D-BBDA: ロバストな3D点群認識のための逆伝播不要ブラックボックスドメイン適応
llm.tldr_ja: ソースデータの内部パラメータにアクセスせず、ブラックボックス出力のみを用いて教師なしターゲットデータに適応するフレームワーク「3D-BBDA」を提案した。
llm.problem: プライバシー、ライセンス、セキュリティの制約により、ソースデータや内部パラメータへのアクセスが制限される。
llm.method: 擬似ラベル誘導型プロトタイプベースの整合と、ソースロジットと整合ロジットを融合する重み付き予測モジュールを用いる。
llm.result: ModelNet-40Cなどの4つの破損3Dベンチマークで一貫した性能向上を実証した。

2611.03588.tldr_en: 3D-BBDA is presented, a backpropagation-free black-box domain adaptation framework that adapts a source-trained predictor to unlabeled target data using only black-box outputs and requires only a single forward pass with no gradient updates making it suitable for real-time, privacy-preserving deployment in transferable 3D recognition pipelines.

2611.03584.title: TAMPAgent: Agentic Belief-Space Planning for Mobile Manipulation
2611.03584.abstract: Open-world robotic mobile manipulation requires acting in physical environments with only partial information. While recent Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM) agents show strong open-world reasoning capabilities, existing architectures that rely on direct tool calling struggle with geometric uncertainty and thus are limited to fully-observable tabletop environments. In contrast, Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) systems can solve long-horizon tasks under partial observability but incur high computational costs and require closed worlds. We propose \textbf{TAMPAgent}, an agentic planning framework that unifies the reasoning of LVLMs with the structured constraint satisfaction of TAMP systems. We endow an LVLM agent with a belief-space planning model operating over an extensible API of perception, planning, and control tools. The agent formulates a partial task plan composed of parameterized observation and execution actions, which is subsequently completed using classical search algorithms. After extracting the plan's geometric constraints, the agent leverages its tool API to bind valid parameter values, satisfying feasibility requirements and producing an executable motion plan. Upon execution, the agent continuously updates its belief history and repeats this closed-loop process by interleaving observation and manipulation actions. Evaluated across complex household mobile manipulation tasks on Rainbow Y1 and Unitree G1 platforms, TAMPAgent significantly outperforms direct tool-calling agentic baselines, demonstrating that integrating TAMP constraint satisfaction into agentic planning loops is essential for unstructured, partially observable environments.

llm.title_ja: TAMPAgent: モバイルマニピュレーションのためのエージェント型信念空間計画
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模ビジョン言語モデル（LVLM）のエージェントの推論とTAMPシステムの制約充足を統合したエージェント型計画フレームワーク「TAMPAgent」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のLVLMエージェントは幾何学因果関係の不確実性に苦しみ、完全観測可能な卓上環境に限定されている。
llm.method: 感知、計画、制御ツールの拡張可能API上で動作する信念空間計画モデルをLVLMエージェントに装備する。
llm.result: 家庭内モバイルマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、直接ツール呼び出し型のエージェントベースラインを大きく上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2611.03584.tldr_en: Evaluated across complex household mobile manipulation tasks on Rainbow Y1 and Unitree G1 platforms, TAMPAgent significantly outperforms direct tool-calling agentic baselines, demonstrating that integrating TAMP constraint satisfaction into agentic planning loops is essential for unstructured, partially observable environments.

2611.03585.title: Seeing Through the Illusion: Test-Time Scaling for World Action Models
2611.03585.abstract: World action models (WAMs) jointly generate actions and imagined futures, but a plausible prediction need not be realized by its co-generated action. We introduce WISE (\emph{World Action Inference Scaling through Evaluation}), a pre-execution selector that scores each sampled rollout on action validity and temporal regularity, inverse-dynamics consistency between the proposed action and the imagined motion, and instruction-conditioned task progress, and executes the highest-scoring candidate while keeping the WAM frozen. With four candidates per decision, WISE raises closed-loop success from 6.0\% to 24.0\% on RoboLab with Cosmos~3 Edge and from 75.1\% to 78.3\% mean success on LIBERO with DreamZero, and exceeds the best existing selector in aggregate by 4.0 and 0.9 points. Component ablations and agreement analyses show that the three scores rank candidates differently and that task progress carries the largest weight in the fused decision.
2611.03585.comment: Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on From Generative Models to Robot Actions (G2A)

llm.title_ja: 幻影を通して見る: 世界行動モデルのためのテスト時スケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 世界行動モデル（WAM）のサンプリングされたロールアウトを評価・選択する事前実行セレクター「WISE」を提案し、閉ループの成功率を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルは妥当な予測を生成するが、もっともらしい予測が必ずしも対応する行動によって実現されるとは限らない。
llm.method: 行動の妥当性、時間的規則性、逆動力学の整合性、タスクの進捗に基づいて各ロールアウトをスコアリングし、最良の候補を実行する。
llm.result: RoboLabやLIBEROにおいて閉ループの成功率を大きく向上させ、既存の最良セレクターを上回った。
keywords_ja: テスト時スケーリング

2611.03585.tldr_en: WISE is introduced, a pre-execution selector that scores each sampled rollout on action validity and temporal regularity, inverse-dynamics consistency between the proposed action and the imagined motion, and instruction-conditioned task progress, and executes the highest-scoring candidate while keeping the WAM frozen.

2611.03548.title: Mediating Human-Swarm Interactions Through a Robot Helper: A Shepherding-Inspired Approach
2611.03548.abstract: This work investigates human-swarm interaction (HSI) for steering large collectives through an intermediary robot helper. While prior robot-swarm control and HSI techniques commonly assume swarm members are addressable, these assumptions often fail for ``ungovernable'' swarms such as wildlife flocks and schools of fish. Motivated by pastoral shepherding, we compare low-level teleoperation to a higher-autonomy motion-primitives interface in a virtual reality (VR) shepherding task under varied swarm cohesion dynamics. Results indicate that motion primitives that operate on collective shape (e.g., boundary-based control) improve task performance and reduce perceived workload.

llm.title_ja: ロボットヘルパーを通した人間と群れの相互作用の仲介: 牧羊にインスパイアされたアプローチ
llm.tldr_ja: 仲介役のロボットヘルパーを用いて大規模な群れを誘導する人間と群れの相互作用（HSI）を調査し、集合の形状に基づくモーションプリミティブがタスク性能を向上させることを示した。
llm.problem: 野生の鳥の群れや魚の群れなど、制御不可能な群れに対して従来の群れ制御やHSI手法は適用できない。
llm.method: 牧羊にインスパイアされ、低レベルのテレオペレーションと、群れの集合形状を操作する高自律なモーションプリミティブインターフェースを比較する。
llm.result: 集合形状を操作するモーションプリミティブが、タスク性能を向上させ、知覚される作業負荷を軽減することを示した。
keywords_ja: 人間とロボットの協調
モーションプリミティブ

2611.03548.tldr_en: This work compares low-level teleoperation to a higher-autonomy motion-primitives interface in a virtual reality shepherding task under varied swarm cohesion dynamics and indicates that motion primitives that operate on collective shape improve task performance and reduce perceived workload.

2611.03520.title: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Robust Touch-Centric Manipulation
2611.03520.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation benefits from tactile feedback that captures both detailed contact geometry and interaction forces. When scooping grains, contact patterns help infer spoon orientation, while resistance transmitted through the grasp guides motion. To provide these complementary sensing capabilities, we present PanoTac, a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip designed for dense three-axis tactile sensing. Each fingertip provides a $12 \times 32 \times 3$ tactile representation, with one normal ($z$) and two shear ($x$, $y$) response components at each taxel. The sensor operates at 60 Hz and costs less than $50 per fingertip. Sensor characterization quantifies response repeatability and consistency across sensor instances and contact locations. We integrate PanoTac into a robotic system with a visuo-tactile pipeline. Across test-tube preparation, grain scooping, and salt pouring, the resulting policies outperform vision-only baselines by an average of 46.7 percentage points. Ablations show that removing either spatial contact information or shear feedback reduces overall performance across the task suite. Our project page is available at https://panotac.github.io.

llm.title_ja: PanoTac: ロバストな触覚中心マニピュレーションのための高密度3軸触覚センサー
llm.tldr_ja: 詳細な接触ジオメトリと相互作用力を捉える低コストで柔軟な3軸触覚センサー「PanoTac」を開発し、視覚のみのベースラインを大幅に上回る性能を実証した。
llm.problem: 接触の豊かなマニピュレーションには接触ジオメトリと力の両方を捉える触覚フィードバックが必要である。
llm.method: 12×32×3の触覚表現を持つ低コストで柔軟な触覚指先を開発し、視覚触覚パイプラインに統合する。
llm.result: 試験管の準備、穀物のすくい上げ、塩の注ぎにおいて、視覚のみのベースラインを平均46.7ポイント上回った。
llm.limitation: 要旨 in 記載なし
keywords_ja: 触覚マニピュレーション

2611.03520.tldr_en: PanoTac, a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip designed for dense three-axis tactile sensing, integrates into a robotic system with a visuo-tactile pipeline and shows that removing either spatial contact information or shear feedback reduces overall performance across the task suite.

2611.03501.title: When Robots Outweigh Objects: How Inertia Mismatch Shapes Robot Policy Learning
2611.03501.abstract: Conventional robot arms can be extremely heavy compared with the everyday objects they manipulate, creating a significant inertia mismatch at contact. Even a small accidental bump from a heavy arm can knock a light object out of place. Modern learning methods have nevertheless demonstrated a wide range of successful manipulation behaviors on these platforms, suggesting that even extreme inertia mismatch can be overcome with sufficient data. However, it remains unclear whether high inertia imposes a hidden cost on learning, potentially worsening scaling with data or lowering the performance ceiling of modern robot learning methods. We investigate this question through controlled simulation experiments that vary robot and object masses. We find that reinforcement learning succeeds across a broad range of mass combinations, while behavior cloning learns more reliable policies when a lighter robot manipulates a heavier object. Heavier robots require more demonstrations to attain the same performance as lighter robots. Finally, because new hardware is rarely an option, we explore ways to lower an existing arm's inertia at contact with existing hardware, either by choosing a lower-inertia workspace before collecting data or by steering the demonstrator toward lower-inertia configurations during the task. In both cases, the lower-inertia demonstrations are imitated more reliably. Project website: https://younghyopark.me/inertia-mismatch/
2611.03501.tldr_en: Reinforcement learning succeeds across a broad range of mass combinations, while behavior cloning learns more reliable policies when a lighter robot manipulates a heavier object, and more data narrows the resulting gap without closing it.

2611.03498.title: SNAP: Semantic Navigation Among Pedestrians
2611.03498.abstract: Navigating crowded urban environments requires robots to avoid pedestrians while adhering to social norms such as remaining on sidewalks. Existing approaches typically address either crowd avoidance or semantic path planning in isolation. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) navigation policy that jointly reasons about semantic terrain and dynamic obstacles from a single semantically annotated bird's-eye-view (BEV) map, without relying on explicit human-state estimation. Our policy outperforms established crowd-navigation and semantic-aware baselines and transfers zero-shot to a legged robot, demonstrating socially compliant navigation in highly dynamic real-world scenarios.

llm.title_ja: SNAP: 歩行者の中でのセマンティックナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 明示的な人間状態の推定に頼らず、単一のセマンティック注釈付き鳥瞰図（BEV）マップからセマンティック地形と動的障害物を同時に推論する強化学習ナビゲーションポリシーを提案した。
llm.problem: 混雑した都市環境をナビゲートする際、群れの回避とセマンティックな経路計画が個別に扱われがちである。
llm.method: 単一のセマンティックBEVマップを用いてセマンティック地形と動的障害物を同時に推論する強化学習ポリシーを構築し、脚式ロボットにゼロショット移行する。
llm.result: 既存の群れナビゲーションおよびセマンティック認識ベースラインを上回り、脚式ロボットへのゼロショット移行に成功した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックナビゲーション

2611.03498.tldr_en: This paper proposes a reinforcement learning navigation policy that jointly reasons about semantic terrain and dynamic obstacles from a single semantically annotated bird's-eye-view (BEV) map, without relying on explicit human-state estimation.

2611.03490.title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
2611.03490.abstract: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions.
2611.03490.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

llm.title_ja: リプシッツ定数を使わない過駆動マルチローター配分のための遅延保証即応性バリア
llm.tldr_ja: 速度コントローラーの遅延やサンプリングに対応し、リプシッツ定数を必要とせずに過駆動マルチローターの即応性を保証するテストを提案した。
llm.problem: 過駆動マルチローターにおいて、サンプリングされたコマンドと可変な速度コントローラーの遅延により、頑健性のBoundsが非常に小さくなる。
llm.method: 各ローターの単調かつ閉形式の応答特性を利用し、切り替え時間下で到達可能な速度を安価なボックスとして計算する。
llm.result: ヘキサローターのシミュレーションにおいて、遅延やジッターがある場合でも安全バリアの違反を引き起こさなかった。

2611.03489.title: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
2611.03489.abstract: Pre-touch sensing, or sensing information about an object before contact, is an attractive modality for robot hands as it can allow a robot to anticipate and respond to a contact before it happens. In this work, we introduce ToFTouch, a multimodal tactile sensor combining three multizone (4$\times$4 resolution) time-of-flight sensors with an optics-based pressure sensing array. We mount this sensor on a parallel jaw gripper and demonstrate its utility on three distinct tasks: (i) pre-grasp adjustment, (ii) item extraction from clutter, and (iii) item insertion into tight spaces. For pre-grasp adjustment, ToF feedback reduced cycle time by 7.4$\%$ by enabling anticipatory gripper closure during approach. For extraction, ToF sensing enabled successful retrieval across all tested depth offsets ($\pm$2 cm) deviating from the nominal pick point, including conditions where baseline approaches failed, with standard deviations below 0.4 cm. For insertion into dense clutter, we explore the proximity and tactile information provided from ToFTouch during an insertion trajectory. The results demonstrate the utility of multizone ToF sensing in a manipulation environment.

llm.title_ja: ロボットマニピュレーションに向けた近接・触覚センシングの探索
llm.tldr_ja: 3つのマルチゾーンToFセンサーと光学式圧力センサーアレイを組み合わせたマルチモーダル触覚センサー「ToFTouch」を開発し、把持前調整や狭い空間への挿入等での有用性を実証した。
llm.problem: 接触前の情報を取得する事前接触センシングのロボットハンドへの応用やその検証が求められている。
llm.method: 3つのマルチゾーンToFセンサーと光学式圧力センシングアレイを組み合わせたマルチモーダル触覚センサーをパラレルジョーグリッパーに搭載する。
llm.result: ToFフィードバックにより、把持前調整のサイクルタイム短縮や、クラッタからのアイテム抽出、狭所への挿入精度向上が実現できた。

2611.03489.tldr_en: ToFTouch, a multimodal tactile sensor combining three multizone time-of-flight sensors with an optics-based pressure sensing array, is introduced and its utility on three distinct tasks is demonstrated: pre-grasp adjustment, item extraction from clutter, and item insertion into tight spaces.

2611.03772.title: RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills
2611.03772.abstract: Third-party Agent Skills extend what an autonomous agent can do, but a malicious Skill can hide data exposure or output manipulation inside a legitimate workflow. Neither reading a Skill's description nor granting it tool permissions tells whether its execution meets the user's security requirements. We introduce RuntimeTickets, a protocol that enforces and audits these requirements while a Skill runs. From released malicious-Skill datasets we derive a risk model and build adversarial-benign Skill pairs. From the task's delivery contract, a language model proposes security obligations for that task. Each obligation cites the Skill lines it answers, and the ticket tightens the host's approvals into fine-grained allowed actions but never loosens them. A runtime gate checks the recipient, object and amount of every outbound send before forwarding it, and trusted monitors record the effects within their observation scope. The ticket links these checks and observations to the approved obligations of each Skill run, and a deterministic decoder turns the ticket's status into governable data flows and verifies each obligation. Neither enforcement nor decoding involves a language model, so text injected by a Skill can change the proposal but never the rule that decides a send. We evaluate RuntimeTickets at the network egress boundary of three unmodified agent frameworks against production Skill scanners and runtime baselines, among them an AgentBound-derived allow-list and SkillGuard. RuntimeTickets eliminated both failure modes of current Skill defenses, overlook (malicious Skills let through) and overkill (benign Skills blocked): its overlook rate was 0.0% and its overkill rate 0.0%, while the scanners erred on both sides. RuntimeTickets ties approved requirements to verifiable execution evidence and offers a common foundation for the safe and auditable deployment of third-party Skills.

llm.title_ja: RuntimeTickets：エージェントスキルのためのソースグラウンドされたセキュリティ義務
llm.tldr_ja: LLMによるタスクのセキュリティ義務の提案とチケットによる実行時のアクション検証を組み合わせ、悪意のあるスキルのデータ漏洩や出力操作を防ぐ「RuntimeTickets」プロトコルを提案する。
llm.problem: サードパーティのエージェントスキルは正当なワークフローの中にデータ露出や出力操作を隠すことができ、説明や権限付与だけではセキュリティ要件を満たしているか分からない。
llm.method: タスクの契約から言語モデルがセキュリティ義務を提案し、チケットがホストの承認をきめ細かな許可アクションに制限し、ランタイムゲートが送信前に確認を行う「RuntimeTickets」プロトコルを導入する。
llm.result: 3つの未変更エージェントフレームワークにおいて、悪意のあるスキルを通してしまう見落とし率と良性スキルをブロックしてしまう過剰処理率の双方で0.0%を達成した。
keywords_ja: アクセスコントロール

2611.03446.title: Clinician-AI Collaboration in Endovascular Neurointerventions: In-Vitro User Study of Copilot Assistance Modes for Robotic Navigation Across the Autonomy Spectrum
2611.03446.abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is an effective treatment for acute ischemic stroke, yet access remains limited by the availability of neurointerventional expertise. Telerobotic and AI-assisted systems may help address this challenge, but it remains unclear how clinicians interact with different levels of autonomy and how autonomous navigation systems perform in realistic environments. This work introduces Copilot Assistance Modes (CAMs), a framework for clinician-AI collaboration in robotic endovascular navigation spanning the autonomy spectrum from manual operation to full autonomy. In the first in-vitro user study comparing clinician-AI collaboration strategies, 11 experts and two students evaluated six navigation modes in a patient-specific vascular phantom. Objective performance metrics were combined with subjective assessments, including workload and usability. Autonomous performance was additionally evaluated both in silico and in vitro to investigate sim-to-real transfer. Hands-on manual navigation achieved the strongest overall performance (100% success). While fully autonomous navigation achieved 81% success in simulation, performance dropped to 23% in vitro. In contrast, several clinician-AI shared-autonomy modes achieved success rates of 92-97%, approximately four times higher than full autonomy and comparable to direct robotic control (95%), demonstrating mitigation of sim-to-real domain shift through clinician-AI collaboration. Among the evaluated AI-driven approaches, user-directed task delegation and rotational shared control demonstrated the most favorable balance between performance and clinician acceptance. These findings suggest that effective clinician-AI collaboration and allocation of control authority may currently be more important for reliable robotic neurointerventional navigation than increasing autonomy alone.

llm.title_ja: 血管内神経治療における臨床医とAIの協調: 自律性のスペクトラムにわたるロボットナビゲーションのコパイロット支援モードの体外使用者調査
llm.tldr_ja: 手動操作から完全自律までの自律性スペクトラムにわたる臨床医とAIの協調フレームワーク「CAMs」を提案し、体外ファントムを用いたユーザー調査を実施した。
llm.problem: 急性虚血性脳卒中の機械的血栓回収術において治療へのアクセスが限られており、臨床医が様々なレベルの自律性とどう協調するか不明確である。
llm.method: 手動から完全自律までの6つのナビゲーションモードを評価する、11人の専門家と2人の学生による体外使用者調査を実施する。
llm.result: 臨床医とAIの共有自律モードは、完全自律に比べ約4倍高い92〜97%の成功率を達成し、ドメインシフトを軽減できることを示した。
keywords_ja: 血管内ナビゲーション

2611.03446.tldr_en: Copilot Assistance Modes (CAMs) are introduced, a framework for clinician-AI collaboration in robotic endovascular navigation spanning the autonomy spectrum from manual operation to full autonomy, suggesting that effective clinician-AI collaboration and allocation of control authority may currently be more important for reliable robotic neurointerventional navigation than increasing autonomy alone.

2611.03430.title: Evaluating Depth-Augmented Visual Features for Cross-Dataset Lunar Traversability Estimation
2611.03430.abstract: Autonomous mobility is essential for sustained lunar surface operations, as communication delays and line-of-sight occlusions limit continuous teleoperation. Although recent traversability estimation methods increasingly rely on deep learning, the domain gap between terrestrial analogue environments and real lunar terrain can limit their generalisation, and real lunar traversability labels are scarce, making fully supervised training difficult. To address these challenges, we build a weakly supervised framework trained on sparse pairwise annotations and study whether augmenting visual features with depth-derived geometric information: depth, surface normals, and combined geometric descriptors. We evaluate the models in both in-domain and cross-domain settings using two terrestrial analogue datasets and the real lunar Chang'E PCAM dataset. Contrary to expectations, we find that naive geometric augmentation yields no consistent improvement over a strong visual-only baseline in either setting, with effects small relative to seed-to-seed variance. Instead, the choice of training source emerges as the dominant factor in transfer quality: models trained on domain-relevant sources transfer substantially better to real lunar imagery than the geometric fusion strategy improves any single model. Our evaluation runs onboard a resource-constrained edge device and provides a controlled baseline for designing more expressive multimodal fusion architectures in future lunar perception systems.

llm.title_ja: クロスデータセット月面走行可能性推定のための深度拡張視覚特徴の評価
llm.tldr_ja: 疎なペアワイズアノテーションで訓練された弱教師ありフレームワークを構築し、深度由来の幾何学的情報の追加が月面走行可能性推定の汎化性能に与える影響を評価した。
llm.problem: 地球のアナログ環境と実際の月面地形の間のドメインギャップが汎化を制限し、実際の月面走行可能性ラベルが不足している。
llm.method: 深度、法線、幾何学的記述子などの深度由来の幾何学的情報を視覚特徴に統合し、複数のデータセットでモデルを評価する。
llm.result: 素朴な幾何学的拡張は一貫した性能向上をもたらさず、データセットの選択が転移品質の支配的要因であることが判明した。

2611.03430.tldr_en: A weakly supervised framework trained on sparse pairwise annotations is built and it is found that naive geometric augmentation yields no consistent improvement over a strong visual-only baseline in either setting, and the choice of training source emerges as the dominant factor in transfer quality.

2611.03428.title: Toward Uncertainty-Aware, Physics-Grounded Human World Models
2611.03428.abstract: A robot that acts around people needs a world model of the human: a belief over the person's body state and a dynamics model that predicts where that state goes next. This abstract argues that two published components form exactly these two halves, and specifies how to couple them. KNOWN [1] reconstructs the 3D human body while estimating both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in real time (11.6 ms per frame); its aleatoric term identifies unreliable observations, its epistemic term identifies inputs from low-density regions of the training data, and refinement driven by the epistemic term reduces the error on such inputs from 81.3 to 70.3 mm. PhysMoP [2] predicts future body configuration by solving the Euler-Lagrange equations of the body with learned dynamics terms, reducing the 80 ms prediction error from 9.6 to 2.1 mm on Human3.6M and from 12.1 to 0.7 mm on 3DPW. We define the interface between the two, propose three mechanisms by which KNOWN's uncertainty enters PhysMoP, and specify an evaluation protocol on in-the-wild video. No new experimental results are reported here.

llm.title_ja: 不確実性を考慮した物理ベースの人間世界モデルに向けて
llm.tldr_ja: 人の3D身体再構築を行うKNOWNと物理ベースの挙動予測を行うPhysMoPの2つのコンポーネントを結合し、不確実性を考慮した物理ベースの人間世界モデルのインターフェースと評価プロトコルを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットが人の周りで行動するためには、人の身体状態の信念とそのダイナミクスを予測する人間世界モデルが必要である。
llm.method: KNOWNが提供する不確実性をPhysMoPのダイナミクス予測に組み込む3つのメカニズムとインターフェースを定義する。
llm.result: 新しい実験結果は報告されておらず、モデルの統合方法、インターフェースの提案、および評価プロトコルの策定を行った。
llm.limitation: 新しい実験結果は報告されていない

2611.03428.tldr_en: It is argued that two published components form exactly these two halves, and how to couple them is specified, and three mechanisms by which KNOWN's uncertainty enters PhysMoP are proposed.

2611.03418.title: Myoelectric Control for Upper-Limb Exoskeletons: A Decoder-Shaper-Controller Framework, Design Guidelines, and Future Directions
2611.03418.abstract: Myoelectric Control Systems (MCSs) enable voluntary control of wearable robots through muscle activity. However, intention decoding, assistance shaping, and low-level actuator control are often not explicitly distinguished, making their contributions difficult to evaluate and compare. This review introduces a functional decoder-shaper-controller framework for continuous myoelectric control of upper-limb exoskeletons. The decoder estimates an intention-related variable from surface electromyography (sEMG), the shaper maps it to a control reference according to an assistance policy, and the controller realizes that reference through actuator control. This decomposition separates intention estimation from assistance-policy design and enables comparison of heterogeneous architectures. Representative approaches are critically examined in terms of module design, calibration, and evaluation. The analysis highlights that the shaper, despite determining the magnitude and shape of assistance, lacks established design and tuning methodologies and is often embedded within the decoder or controller. Key open issues include inconsistent reporting of assistance levels, limited use of interaction-aware stability and passivity tools, and insufficient validation across degrees of freedom, users, and tasks. Building on these findings, this review provides design guidelines for systematic module-wise tuning and identifies future research priorities to bridge the gap between accurate intention decoding and safe, effective, and generalizable assistance under real-world operating conditions.

llm.title_ja: 上肢外骨格のための筋電制御: デコーダー・シェーパー・コントローラーフレームワーク、設計指針、および今後の方向性
llm.tldr_ja: 上肢外骨格の連続的な筋電制御に向けた機能的デコーダー・シェーパー・コントローラーフレームワークを提案し、モジュール設計や今後の研究課題を総括した。
llm.problem: 意図のデコード、アシストのシェーピング、低レベルの駆動制御が明確に区別されておらず、貢献の評価や比較が困難である。
llm.method: 表面筋電図（sEMG）からの意図推定、制御リファレンスへのマッピング、アクチュエーター制御への分解によるフレームワークを導入し、従来手法を分析する。
llm.result: シェーパーの設計手法の欠如や、アシストレベルの報告の不統一などの課題を明らかにし、系統的なモジュール別チューニングのための設計指針を提供した。
keywords_ja: ウェアラブルロボット

2611.03418.tldr_en: A functional decoder-shaper-controller framework for continuous myoelectric control of upper-limb exoskeletons is introduced and design guidelines for systematic module-wise tuning are provided to bridge the gap between accurate intention decoding and safe, effective, and generalizable assistance under real-world operating conditions.

2611.03410.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
2611.03410.abstract: Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and skin-temperature sensing. Its software architecture separates acquisition, event interpretation, interaction policy, and robot execution. We characterize seven operating modes and evaluate speech and gesture control with 10 participants. Across five commands and 250 trials per modality, speech and gestures achieved task success rates of 90.4% and 88.8%, respectively. Recognition accuracy exceeded task success for both modalities. Gaussian hidden Markov models achieved higher accuracy than a support vector machine across three vocabulary sizes, with longer scoring times. Following a shared spoken task start, gesture-based adjustments had shorter median response times than speech. Whole-task success was 70.0% with gestures and 64.0% with speech. We further examine physiological-event-triggered robot interaction using simulated event notifications. Mean notification-receipt-to-arrival times were 11.71 s for the robot and 9.20 s for an on-site person.
